state: My husband had heard about this ice cream shop from a coworker, and he wanted to try it out. The shop is a small older building that is located under a bridge. It has adequate parking but little seating outside. I ordered a vanilla soft-serve ice cream with peaches on top. The ice cream tasted very rich, and the peaches were sweet. I ordered a size small, but it was the perfect size for me. The employee who served us was polite. My husband ordered a root-beer float because this business seems to make their own root beer. He enjoyed his float. Prices were reasonable. We would feel happy to be return customers in the future.

state: I love Sprinkles in Las Vegas! The location is truly the best part of this place. It’s right in front of the High Roller—a huge roller coaster located outside the Las Vegas Strip. You can take amazing photos here! Additionally, there’s a fountain right outside, which creates a very pleasant atmosphere, especially in warmer weather. You can sit by the fountain and enjoy the desserts. Of course, the cupcakes and ice cream from Sprinkles are delicious. You can expect the same quality as anywhere else at Sprinkles. The service has always been fast and friendly, and the store has always been clean. If you’re in this area and looking for a quick, easy, and reliable dessert option, Sprinkles is the perfect place to get one.

state: I came here last night to celebrate my birthday, as it’s my favorite place in Charlotte to eat ice cream! They have a wide variety of flavors to choose from! The best part is that you can order a “flight” of 3 different flavors, or even more, so you can try a few of your favorite flavors. I chose vanilla, raspberry, and goat cheese with cherries ice cream. All of them were delicious! The staff is very friendly and knows each flavor well, and they allow you to try as many as you want! If you visit on your birthday, the ice cream is also free! Sometimes they get crowded and there’s a long line, but it’s worth waiting! They also have waffle cones made right away, which have a great smell and taste! I can’t wait to come back.

state: Considering the reputation of this place, I really wanted to try it out. Actually, I had tried it two years ago and wasn’t very impressed. So, I decided to try it again, because my wife liked it. There was a wide variety of items: almond chocolate croissants, wine grapes bread (a sweet bread with raisins), strawberry croissants, chocolate croissants, beignets (fried pastries), walnut rolls, and some other things I can’t remember. The only things I really liked were the strawberry croissants, which had a crunchy topping, and the beignets. I felt that everything else had a slightly dry taste. By the way, the latte was really good. Overall, the prices weren’t bad, considering we’re in a casino in Las Vegas where everything is more expensive. I thought most of the desserts were better than average, but not as good as any simple bakery in a train station in Paris. I don’t think I would go there, but I might stop by if I’m on my way. To be honest, the croissant bakery near my house makes croissants that are lighter, softer, and more flavorful, but their coffee is terrible. After reading some of the other comments, I wanted to buy a macaron, but I didn’t see any reason to pay $3.50 for one. There’s an Italian bakery in Little Italy, in San Francisco, that makes and sells these desserts for less than $1, and they’re perfect. Although they’re a bit smaller.

state: Minus 2 stars for the absolutely horrible in store service. We were the only ones in the store and there were at least 4 employees, including the manager Priscilla, who was the absolute worst of the bunch. Right when we began to order, some employee (named Kat?) seemed utterly confused and annoyed that we wanted two separate orders. Is that such a difficult request? After she takes both our orders to the register, she gets confused and asks us if we want to pay together. I said no, and once again, I'm met with a confused look. After a bit of commotion, another employee asks ME what is in the box, and after I tell her I'm not sure, she throws the box back down and proceeds to leave. I'm not asking to be treated like a princess, but if you don't know what's in the box, can't you just open it and check if it's my order or not?! Now I was actually getting annoyed at this point so I asked for the manager. Turns out the woman who was too lazy to check what was in my box WAS the manager. Not sure if I caught them on a bad day or if they were too lazy to work, but thankfully there was one competent employee (blonde haired, tall male named Aaron?) who took the time to apologize for something he didn't even do. I would've just left without any macarons after all that attitude and sass, but since they are soo good, I had to suck it up and stay. Delicious treats, but horrible employees (minus Aaron).

state: I love it so much! I love all the flavors! When I used to buy from online, I would feel very sad when a pint was gone. Now I have options and can go get one after work. The ice cream shop is really cute and offers many choices. I love how the flavors can change—I can buy a pint for myself and a “pup cup” for my pet. I highly recommend trying a variety for yourself or to share with a friend, family member, or partner! I also like that the ice cream is gluten-free, just like the waffle cones. My favorite flavor during this visit was “The Song of Fire & Ice” – a maple ice cream with Nutkrack spices. There’s parking right next to the shop, or many parking options on the street.

state: Finally, 85C has arrived in Las Vegas—something that had been long awaited. If you’re a fan of Asian-style desserts and breads (light, fluffy, and not too sweet), this is the perfect place for you. Be prepared to wait in line, as it’s a newly opened establishment. When we went there tonight, the line lasted about 20 minutes. Although many of the bread displays were almost empty or had few items, the display cases with cakes and pastries were quite full. They were working hard to be efficient, and there was an employee in the middle of the line who packed each bread item into individual plastic bags before it reached the counter. Download the 85C app to earn rewards and get free coffee just by registering. We tried some products, but the “Black Forest” cake really stood out. Excellent, delicious, moist, and not too sweet. They offer a wide range of breads and pastries to satisfy almost any taste, so don’t hesitate to visit 85C if you’re looking for a less sweet but still delicious dessert. There are some tables inside, but given how busy it is, it’s probably better to bring your own food to eat there.

state: This rating is for those of you gluten free types like my wife who has celiac disease. I get it, this place might be overhyped for some people. Yes, great dessert exists other places. Yeah, cereal milk ice cream might sound a little gimmicky (still delicious though), blah blah blah... Listen hipsters, you're the reason places like this exist and then you're the reason it's ends up having a mediocre 3 1/2 stars on Yelp a year or two later. You get bored and cynical, I get it. I probably got a lil hipster in my blood too. But man, if you are gluten free and you bite into the gf version of a succulent, dense, delicious, moist, piece of Christina Tosi's utterly magnificent birthday cake creation, you will understand why there's a big friggin line up to the counter most hours of the day. It really is that good. And I'm gonna go out on a logic limb here and say that the gluten version of the birthday cake is probably even better. But I didn't even feel the need to go there since the gf version was just THAT good. The wife ordered a big ol slice of cake twice over the two days we were there, and like any good gluten free girl on vacation in Las Vegas, she ate a lot of that cake for breakfast. There's other gf options on the menu besides the birthday cake too, and methinks it's probably a good idea for all you gf kids to try them all.

state: Having lived here for over 20 years, I’ve visited all the old locations of Mary Coyle’s shop. It’s great that someone bought this local business from the original owners so we can continue to enjoy it! The last location of MC in Central is closer to me, and that makes me very happy! I’ve been there twice in the past two weeks, and both times, the staff were very kind, followed safety protocols, and served delicious homemade desserts from MC. The last time, I came with a friend: I ordered a mint cone ice cream. It was delicious and refreshing! My friend ordered a black licorice cone – an unusual flavor, so thank you! But it could have been more intense. The second time, I came alone and ordered a chocolate and mint ice cream. It was an excellent flavor because it was refreshing and full of real chocolate chunks, not just pieces or crumbs. What’s your most popular flavor? Salty caramel with nuts. I never expected that… so I’ll have to try it next time! Here are some measures being taken to ensure a safe experience for both staff and customers during the pandemic: * Staff wear masks and gloves * All people who enter use masks (three different people, plus me) * Seating areas are separated to ensure social distancing, except for one private table available. There are many parking options: 1) Turn into Encanto and there are spaces behind the store. 2) Parking on the street in Encanto. 3) Parking just north of Mary Coyle in West Vernon. There’s the Birdhaus café there… Thank you very much for providing such a simple way to share ice cream with friends or family at Mary Coyle right now!

state: What an incredible and transformative experience!! Although the lunch at Momofuku next door wasn’t the best, Momofuku’s dessert concept, the Milk Bar, was a success! I requested samples of both the “crack” cake and the milk ice cream with cereal. The “crack” cake was delicious and flavorful, but a little too sweet for my taste. So I chose the milk ice cream with cereal—it’s, after all, one of the most famous desserts at this place. However, the best decision I made during the whole trip was ordering an affogato with cereal—milk ice cream served with a shot of espresso poured over it. This turned the already excellent milk ice cream into an experience worth celebrating! The bitter intensity of the espresso perfectly complemented the sweetness, richness, and creaminess of the ice cream. I was so happy—I got my share of coffee and also a piece of Milk Bar ice cream! The best $5 investment I’ve ever made!! Finally, I don’t understand why people complain about the prices here. You’re in Las Vegas, in a luxury resort on the Strip, in one of the best dessert places in the US. There are many things to complain about when it comes to Las Vegas (maybe the prices of clubs, for example?!). I know that you, party lovers, can spend $7 on ice cream.

state: I always look for high-quality ice creams with unique flavors. Thankfully, Churn exists in Phoenix to satisfy my cravings. I came here one Thursday night with my girlfriend, and there was a long line. When it was finally our turn, I tried several flavors, and in the end, I decided to try the cookie and mint ice cream. I was unsure between this and the Vietnamese coffee ice cream, but in the end, I chose the cookie and mint one. It was delicious! Without a doubt, one of the best mint ice creams I’ve ever tried. My friend also got the cookie and mint ice cream. You know it’s really good when we don’t order two different flavors and end up ordering the same thing. The texture of the ice cream was soft and creamy—not too cold or gritty. Really, I wish I lived closer to here. But on the other hand, maybe it’s a blessing that I don’t live here, because if I did, I would be here all the time…

state:
I’ve been to Las Vegas several times, but never before I looked for a place to have breakfast or buy donuts. For some reason, I did it this time—and it was probably the best decision of my life! They were probably the best donuts (of high quality) I’ve ever tried. They’re located in the center, near Fremont Street (in English). When we arrived there on a Saturday morning, around 9 a.m., it seemed that their famous strawberry cake or whatever it was had run out :(, but we could still try some amazing donuts.

1. Crème brûlée: They try to recreate the original dessert, and they don’t disappoint. Usually, I don’t like donuts with cream filling, but this one was light and sweet at the same time.
2. Oreo/Christmas cake: They had exactly the flavor they claim.
3. A type of donut filled with strawberries.

All three were incredible, coming from someone who usually prefers chocolate donuts with glaze. What’s most surprising is that they only cost about 2-3 dollars each, so I hope the prices won’t go up—because it’s an incredible deal! There are other higher-quality donuts nearby where I live, but they definitely can’t compare to Donut Bar. It’s likely going to become one of my favorite places in Las Vegas!

state: I was so excited to go to Milk from all of the pictures i see on social media. I got 3 things at Milk. First since I am a cake lover I got a slice of Birthday Cake which is a vanilla rainbow cake, rainbow cake crumbs, sprinkles, vanilla frosting. The cake was moist and and the frosting did have a big vanilla taste but as far as cakes go it was a little underwhelming. Really nothing special with that slice of cake. The second thing I ordered was the Crunchy Cereal Shake which was made with milk, cornflakes, brown sugar and a pinch of salt. It did taste like cereal like I expected but all I really did was pay $9 to drink cereal, nothing special there either. The last thing I ordered which was the best thing was the Crack Pie. I can see why this is there fan favorite because it is addicting as if you were doing crack. Haha. The Crack Pie has a toasted oat crust and a gooey butter filling. So you get that crunch of the crust with that creamy gooey filling. This is the one thing you must have at Milk, but overall this place was pricey and not as exciting as it has been made out to be. BrandonFitFoodie

state: Have you really been to Charlotte if you haven't been to AMELIE'S?! Amelie's sits perfectly into NoDa and is a definitive part of Charlotte's Art District. Walking in, you are welcomed with friendly staff and tons of quirky decor. Mismatched furniture adds to its fun vibes and makes an overall welcoming and great place to hang out, relax, or get some work done. Of course, the desserts and other edibles and drinks are always a delight and the vast arrangement is extremely pleasing to the eye and will make you want to buy more desserts than your body could take. The macarons are always a classic and I have bought tons for a party before and they are definitely a crowd pleaser! The salted caramel brownie is a classic favorite and one of my new favorites. The tarts are amazing and the espresso cake has the perfect dash of coffee. They also make cakes when you need one for a big event and the prices aren't too bad! If you haven't been to Amelie's and you live in the Charlotte area or you are visiting and don't know where to go, well girllllllll (and guys), this is it!

state: I’ve always been a big fan of Jack Frost. Their donuts are delicious and beautiful. Unfortunately, my recent experience wasn’t good. Last weekend, I tried to order donuts for two events. The first was a request for cannoli donuts for a birthday party, and the second was a cake made of donuts. I tried making these orders several times. My calls weren’t answered, and when I went to place the order, the store was closed or there were no donuts available. When I finally got there and found the store open, they said I couldn’t place an order for the cake. I had to call the manager. I actually ordered the cannoli donuts and paid for them in advance. Several hours later, the manager called me and confirmed the order for the cake, paying by phone as requested. A few days later, I received the cake, but they told me that they never made the cannoli donuts order. The woman who said this was the same person who took my order in person and paid for it. She tried to send a message to the manager, but he wasn’t in the store. The manager didn’t answer. Then he found the order and said they hadn’t made it. They gave me two dozen donuts, which weren’t the type I wanted, and said the manager would call me. I waited a whole week to write this review, hoping that Jack Frost would resolve this issue, at least call me and offer to make the cannoli donuts. So far, they haven’t contacted me, and honestly, I doubt they will. Although Jack Frost’s donuts are beautiful and delicious, I don’t think I’ll buy from them anymore. Their customer service is terrible. I’m really disappointed with them.

state: I came here to share the “secret phrase” I found on Facebook that allows me to get a free cupcake. I thought it would be a quick process, so I left Yardhouse just to see if it worked. There was a line of about 3 people in front of me, so I decided to wait. While the couple in front of me made their order, I thought maybe another employee could help me. She said she could help, but couldn’t pack my order. Another supervisor or manager said they could put on gloves and help me, so I told them the secret phrase for the day, and they gave me a free cupcake. However, the process took longer than I expected. Maybe it’s because it’s a relatively new business and they’re still learning the ropes. I’ve been to Sprinkles several times, and seeing the line really discourages me—the line starts outside and goes inside. After my last experience and waiting so long for just one cupcake with only 3 people in front of me, I wouldn’t dare wait again. The cupcake was delicious (it was a chai latte), and it tasted exactly like a chai latte with cream cheese frosting—not too sweet. I also like how they serve ice cream; something I’ve never seen anywhere else at Sprinkles. However, I will go back, but I don’t want to wait in a long line with barriers like entering a club. I understand you have to wait for things that are very popular, but these are just cupcakes—they’re already ready. Cupcakes are like ice cream and cookies—once you see them, you want them right away. I’ll try the “cupcake dispenser” – maybe that’s more my style: quick and easy to get cupcakes! *Great location, with many restaurants and bars around, and Sprinkles is a great way to end the day/evening.*

state: I was excited when it was announced that Sprinkles was coming to Vegas. I used to frequent their Newport Beach location when I lived in California, and thought they were the best cupcakes ever!! So we waited a few months before coming here. I had heard from a few people that the lines were ridiculously long and that the cupcakes were not very good. I thought ok, maybe they just need some time to get their sh!t together. My husband and I finally stopped in after eating dinner at the Yard House and riding the High Roller. When you walk in, you will notice that cupcakes are on the left and ice cream is on the right. I ended up buying 4 cupcakes, but was kind of disappointed when I ate them at home. The cake wasn't as moist and the frosting wasn't as tasty as I remember. :( However, my husband ordered the sprinkles sundae, which was actually pretty good! Ok, so its just a cupcake cut in half with a scoop of ice cream in the middle. I don't know if the milk chocolate cupcakes were just fantastic that day, or if ice cream just makes them that much better. But I highly recommend the sundae if you are going to spend your $ here! Overall, I am disappointed that they are not as good as I remember. Customer service on the ice cream side needs improvement since none of them were greeting customers and it basically seemed like they didn't care. Plus, the location is inconvenient for us locals who don't really spend time on the strip!

state: I was looking for a bakery in the area, and this one appeared. I passed by this place many times, but never knew it existed. This place has a very unique selection of cupcakes, cakes, parfaits, baked desserts, and brownies. I love their modern yet rustic buttercream designs. I also appreciate that they offer gluten-free options. If you're looking for a simple vanilla flavor, this place isn’t for you. I bought 6/7 items here. They have a wide variety of cupcakes, tarts, and brownies. The buttercream on the cupcakes is delicious. It’s not too sweet, but it’s very light. If you like raisins, try their oat and raisin crumble. Otherwise, you won’t go wrong with their chocolate brownies. It’s one of the best brownies I’ve ever tried!

It's expensive & I wouldn't buy a dozen, but if I want a quick sweet treat at the LINQ, it's good. They have a schedule for what flavors they have on each day so if you want something in particular, be sure to go on a day that it's there.

state: Not too impressed with the prices or quality of this semi new ice cream place. The lone asian women behind the counter was nice, but this shop immediately reminded me of one of those asian donut shops you see in every city. The donuts in those places are not usually good and the ice cream here was less than memorable as well. First off, make the size of the sundae bigger or lower the $6.50 price of that sundae. It's not even a sundae technically because it has no syrup. You get two small scoops of bad ice cream (i needed to try 5 flavors to find decent one), two stale macaroons and that "famous" toasted marshmallow. One person with me had a bad aftertaste for at least an hour after the nutella. My flavor was cinnamon toast crunch, which like many flavors, are just vanilla with cereal tossed inside. If your gonna overpay for ice cream, go to creamistry. BTW , If you go non sundae, prices are normal.

state: I’ve only been here twice so far, but it’s already become one of my favorite local ice cream shops. The donuts and ice cream together make a perfect combination—and it’s even better with freshly baked donuts and the handcrafted flavors from Novel! Plus, there’s a lovely pink house in the center of Phoenix—that’s it! Choosing a flavor is really difficult for me, but they always have plenty of options. The honey and lavender flavor is incredible, but I’ll always have a special place in my heart for the chai flavor. Thankfully, two flavors can be combined in one donut. All the other flavors I’ve tried were also delicious. There’s really nothing like ice cream with donuts and frosting. The only downside is that the ice cream melts very quickly, especially during summer days. Brandon and his wife are very kind and enthusiastic about the business, and I’m glad they brought Novel and donut-style ice cream to Phoenix. I’ll definitely bring them to my friends whenever we feel like having ice cream (which happens all the time!). Fresh ice cream, delicious donuts, and amazing people behind the business—what more could you ask for? Let’s support local businesses! I highly recommend this place!

state: Homemade ice cream, local and of good quality. This place is very charming, and the staff is always very friendly. There’s a variety of old-fashioned desserts, which adds a retro and vintage charm to your visit. The ice cream is always excellent, as is the delicious salty caramel topping, which has won awards. (A rich and creamy topping… do I need to say more?) There’s limited parking, but there are several options nearby. I think we can all walk just one block to get some ice cream… 😉 And if not, ask someone to come get it for you! There are no tables inside; only outdoor areas in front and behind. If you appreciate the local charm and are looking for ice cream, milkshakes, maltes, or delicious cookies, stop by Churn. P.S.: Walnut ice cream with salty caramel is one of my favorites!

state: After thinking about getting ice cream for hours, while sitting in the couch and watching John Oliver, I decided to turn to Yelp and investigate my neighborhood options. As it turns out, there is quite the burgeoning ice cream scene here in Phoenix. Obviously, coming from ho-dunk Tucson, I was shocked to learn this. Though most of my shock was really pleasant surprise, I was quickly overcome by an overwhelming fear of making the wrong choice. Chrurn, being the highest rated was very alluring, but unfortunately, it didn't convincingly seem to be the most novel or hip. Other options looked like they were on the cutting edge. One even boasted a nitrogen infused shake. As I continued my yelpagation (yelp investigation) I eventually became paralyzed by the fear of picking another mediocre wannabe ice cream shop. Thus, as I write this review, I remain on the couch and have yet to actually endeavor out. Thanks yelp, for saving me from me another painful disappointment. Maybe one day I'll eventually work up the courage to try this hot spot that's really all rage. Until then, Stay calm yelpers and yelp-on.

state: If you want your creamy dessert to stay frozen, come in February. Here, the dessert melts as soon as you touch it, and since I hate melted ice cream, that’s quite annoying. There’s a wide variety of flavors, but they are a bit reluctant to offer any toppings. Again, these desserts should be special, but in reality, they’re just ice cream with some milk. The price is a bit high for that. If you like creamy and tasty desserts, go to Culver’s. Otherwise, go to Coldstone and buy regular ice cream. The only positive thing is that they kept their original decor and atmosphere, which is very charming! I also love that it’s a place where residents gather during hot summer nights. It’s definitely a place worth visiting, but maybe just once.

state: SEE ATTACHED PHOTOS!! Cleveland HOMEMADE Ice-Cream. I LOVE Honey Hut Ice-Cream. I visited the State Road location with my friend Lesly N. in early September 2019. I ordered the Honey Chai and Sea Salt Caramel on a waffle cone ($3.50). My friend bought the Honey Chai and the Chocolate Pecan flavour on a cup with sprinkles on top. We sat outside on a nice weather day. There is no seating inside because it is set up as a walk-up ordering place. Outside has benches to sit on including an area with a white canopy like covering that has benches below. ICE-CREAMS -- There are a bunch of flavours to choose from. The honey chai is the perfect combination of honey and chai. This is a very unique flavour. The sea salt caramel is sweet and delightful if you enjoy caramel. I can't wait to return. Ice cream at Honey Hut makes life a little bit sweeter :) **** - 149 total reviews in 2019 - 358 total overall Yelp reviews - Reviewed on 7 December 2019

I’ll come back if I ever visit Charlotte again. Now I know what to order.

state: We arrived late and went to that pool party without eating anything. It was so fun that I didn’t even think about food. After five hours under the strong sun and walking along the Strip, my sister literally fainted on the ground. I rushed quickly (also because I was hungry; I couldn’t run) to Bouchon and ordered a grilled cheese sandwich and orange juice. The juice was fresh, and I’m sure they didn’t add sugar. It was delicious. The grilled cheese was well coated with butter, and there must be some secret ingredient, because it was amazing—or maybe I just thought so because I was hungry. My sister recovered quickly after drinking the juice :)

state: My first visit to Jarling’s was on a Saturday night, after having an excellent meal at Thara Thai, which is also located in Champaign. In fact, I had been here before while in Champaign, but I didn’t stay long. I looked up some dessert options in the area, and it seemed that Jarling’s was very popular. When I went to Jarling’s, I knew I wanted to order a “snowstorm” – similar to the concrete mixer at Culver’s, or the blizzard at DQ. I also wanted to try their famous “cold chocolate,” which is melted chocolate, but it’s cold and doesn’t melt the cream (a girl who works there explained it to me). Anyway, I decided to order the “snowstorm” with a “turtle” base. At first, they gave me the turtle ice cream, which I should have started eating, but I returned it. I guess they got confused because I asked what the “cold chocolate” was; normally, cold chocolate comes with ice cream, but still. They quickly replaced it with a “snowstorm” with a “turtle” base. I also ordered a cup of ice cream with a cake base. A “polar bear cup” at Jarling’s is a portion equivalent to a spoonful, containing 6 ginger cookies and a cherry. One portion costs $1.75, but the “polar bear cup” costs $2.25. In my opinion, it wasn’t worth it. To be honest, I was a little confused about my “snowstorm.” I thought it was vanilla ice cream, but it seemed to be chocolate. The “turtle” base supposedly has cold chocolate, almonds, and caramel. When they brought back the wrong turtle ice cream, it was vanilla ice cream with a layer of cold chocolate on top. For my “snowstorm,” it was a different color, so I got confused. I didn’t even try the caramel, which I was really looking forward to. I went here with my brother, and he ordered the same “polar bear cup” as well as a “macaron snowstorm.” I tasted a little of his, and it was much better than mine. I think they got my order wrong, but still, the ice cream was very good. The ice cream with a cake base wasn’t anything special, to be honest. There were no pieces of cake or any kind of topping. They have a weekly menu of flavors, along with their usual options (check their updated website). Just one comment: we arrived at 8:45 PM on a Saturday night, and it was pretty full. There were several tables inside, as well as a takeout service. We decided to order and go to my car, which was parked in one of the access areas. While we were eating, two fire trucks from Wonder Lake stopped next to us. A girl who got out of one of the trucks decided to open the door of her car in my area, and she didn’t even bother checking anything. I’m not sure if I want her to respond to a fire (nothing against Jarling’s, but it happened there). $15 for our 4 dishes. I’m not sure if I’ll order a “snowstorm” or ice cream next time I visit, but I will come back. I think next time I should have ordered something with coconut, peanut butter, or chocolate. To be honest, my “turtle” was disappointing, but I will come back because I love desserts, and I prefer this place over DQ, any yogurt place, or McD. In fact, I would compare it to Culver’s, but I like to support local businesses, and I’d like to see if I can improve my experience.

state: I was very happy to find out that this place met my expectations! Food: 5/5. These donuts are incredible. The dough is soft and fluffy, almost like brioche! The flavors are unique and delicious, but none were overly sweet. Additionally, they’re beautifully decorated, with no excess glaze or mess. I was surprised to learn they’re vegan, as I couldn’t guess from the taste and texture. I highly recommend the strawberry cake and cookie cream! Service: 4/5. I waited about 40 minutes in line, after arriving at opening time (9 a.m., a Sunday!). But the staff were very friendly, and they follow social distancing policies, allowing only one person at a time inside the store and requiring masks. The place was impeccable and very clean. I will definitely come back. The best donuts I’ve tried in Cleveland!

state: My best friend and I came here for a special treat after dinner, and we succeeded. She had been here before and was thrilled; I understood why. When we entered, there was a small line, and when we reached the end of the line, one of the owners was serving customers. It was clear that he not only had knowledge but also a passion for his business. They offer delicious desserts, like ice cream inside a donut. I chose to have my treat in a glass. It was fantastic! In the end, I ordered the mimosa, which was incredible. I would love to order it again, but unfortunately, I don’t live in Phoenix. But every time I’m in the city… I definitely will stop by here! They have outdoor tables, but not inside. This is an excellent business, and a perfect place for a date or to meet a friend or someone special.

state: Walking into dripps I instantly felt refreshed. The space is bright and vibrant. It's small but just big enough to seat a moderate amount of ice cream eaters. Dripps produces Instagram worthy treats that are catered to cereal addicts. But the don't only have cereal as a topping. You can easily choose from several different candy bars or melty drizzles. There is something for everyone. I ordered a milkshake. Not just any milk shake but a snickers crushed and infused melody of crunchy vanilla goodness. It was delish. My bf ordered a sundae with Capitain crunch and my mom ordered a surprisingly delicious vanilla cone chucked full of strawberry flavor and snicker dust on top (copy cat). We all enjoyed our treats and sat at a cute table near the window. This place gets busy pretty quick but the line seems to move rather quickly. I don't enjoy giving Reviews that are under 5 stars if I enjoyed my experience at a restaurant or establishment. In fact it's annoying to see someone give a rave review under a 4 star rating. *rolls eyes* I'm giving 4 stars because although I enjoyed my experience I was pretty shocked to see how small the ice cream cup was that my bf received. It literally looked like a kids serving. And that in itself costs $6. My milkshake was huge and the cone was huge. I looked around and saw others with larger servings as well. Maybe they messed up the order? Idk. I'll be back again but I don't suggest ordering a cup of ice cream. Get a milkshake or cone.

state: There’s a reason why this place has over 600 reviews, and almost all of them are 5 stars. It’s simply amazing! Our family stopped at Novel Ice Cream during a weekend trip to Phoenix. Some places are well-known, but they don’t meet expectations… But Novel Ice Cream is different. It’s located near other stores, restaurants, and bars. The store is relatively small, with no indoor seating, but there’s plenty of space outdoors. Additionally, there’s a park nearby. The parking space is limited, but we drove a few blocks and found spots on the street. After a short walk, we arrived. Since it was around 6:30 p.m. on a weekday, the line wasn’t very long. I bet it’s much longer on weekends and later in the evening. They offered all the samples we wanted, and we took advantage of that offer. The owner was there and was very helpful, explaining the different flavors and all the ingredients. They’ve won several awards for their ice cream. We make ice cream at home, and that inspired me to improve my skills. My kids chose “Cookie Monster” and “Butter Pecan”. I ordered “Dough Melt”—ice cream between a warm donut and a covering—with their special chocolate flavor. I forget what my wife ordered, but she loved it. The price is higher than at places like “Thrifty’s” or “McDonald’s”, but the quality is much better, and it makes no sense to compare. Of course, there was that famous “sugar rush” and the resulting energy drop, but we really enjoyed this place. I asked if they could open a store in Tucson, but maybe it’s better that they haven’t done so yet.

state: Vietnamese coffee with roasted marshmallow cream: Delicious! This coffee is my favorite ice cream flavor, and I really love Vietnamese coffee. I often order it when I’m at Vietnamese restaurants, because I always crave “pho”. The flavor of this ice cream really resembles Vietnamese coffee ice cream—rich and intense. Plus, it isn’t too sweet, which usually prevents me from trying other flavors. Since I wanted to eat roasted marshmallow, I added it for an extra dollar. The combination of Vietnamese coffee ice cream and roasted marshmallow was amazing! The sweet and fluffy marshmallow complemented the creamy, more bitter taste of the ice cream. Moreover, the marshmallow was huge—probably bigger than a whole portion of ice cream. At first, I thought I could eat equal parts of ice cream and marshmallow and finish everything, but I was wrong. The marshmallow was so big that I ended up throwing some away—which was a pity. But I loved this combination, and I would definitely come back for the same or something else! Service: There was a line going out, but the service was very quick. The staff were friendly, quickly took our orders, and served us promptly. Atmosphere: The interior of the store is relatively small, and there aren’t any tables inside. There are also many sweets available around the store, which was interesting to see. There are seating areas outside, at the back of the store, with some small tables and chairs. Overall, I liked the fun and cheerful atmosphere, with walls covered with cassette tapes!

state: I was out of hope looking for a nice bakery in Charlotte to get my pastry fix when I stumbled on this one in the Noda district. Walking through the door you're greeted with an eclectic decor that I the only way I might be able to describe would be chic french hipster. They have an interesting and varied selection of pastries and chocolates that were fun to look at and delicious as well! I went for lunch with a friend and she had the ginger rice soup, and I had the asparagus leek soup. I'm not a fan of ginger so her soup was ok, but the asparagus leek soup was excellent! Creamy and smooth it was a dream. We also split a croque monsieur and it was done perfectly. Greasy, a little crisp on the outside, with the mustard giving a nice kick to the sandwich. Now for the dessert portion we had a strawberry and chocolate croissant, salted caramel brownie, and creme brulee with a small french press. I feel like the strawberry and chocolate croissants could have used a little more filling but they were quite good. The salted caramel brownie I really needed more salt to cut through the creamy sugar of the caramel, but then again I tend to like my snacks a bit less sweet. The creme brulee was the winner of the dessert round. Nice and crisply caramelized top with a not too sweet center. Amelie's was a great find in the Noda area and offers free wifi, a nice place to relax, and a varied crowd with pastry choices for everyone. It's now on my list of places to visit frequently!

state: A friend and I came here right before closing on a Thursday night. This was my first time going but I've always been curious because every time I pass by there's always a huge line! We waited in line and I tried to read the extensive menu through the window behind the counter, which was pretty difficult. My friend informed that there menu is actually online so that might be an easier way to look at the huge menu. I decided on a vanilla cone dipped in cherry. I ordered a medium and was surprised how big it was! However, the cherry coating left a little bit of a waxy taste in my mouth. The vanilla ice cream was delicious though! While I don't think think I'd try their dip cones again I'd definitely give it another go with one of their many other products. Customer service was great! Even though it was close to closing and still had a line the woman who took our order was super friendly and helpful. Also this ice stand only takes cash but there is an atm on site.

state: Wow, I’ve been here about 4 times in the last 2 weeks. It doesn’t help that the first time we brought all the kids, and now the oldest asks me every night if we can go back. The flavors are incredible. On my first night, I tried white chocolate with raspberry and coffee flavor (I don’t remember exactly what they’re called). They were delicious. The flavors are very strong and authentic. The coffee tasted like excellent coffee creamer with sugar. The raspberry had a strong, natural taste, while the white chocolate didn’t overpower the other flavors. My husband tried the watermelon ice cream; it tasted just like taking a fresh slice of watermelon directly from the freezer. The second time, I added homemade malvavisco to my sundae, and it was delicious. At first, the smell is a bit strong due to burnt sugar, but the taste was fantastic. I highly recommend checking out this little place. They also have standard flavors, as well as creative options (my favorite so far is “Netflix and Chill”). I know both owners, and it seems like they really enjoy what they do and the people they meet.

The ice cream was strange; it didn’t seem to be the same as when we were at 7th Avenue. I don’t know why they moved in and reduced the size of the place, but maybe they should have just closed down. state: There are problems that only ice cream can solve. The Melt is located in an artistic and unique area in the center of Phoenix, known as Roosevelt Row. The area is full of art galleries, vintage stores, and bookstores—it’s worth a visit just to experience the place, if you’re in the area. When we entered the Melt, we were greeted, asked if it was our first time there, and given as many samples as we wanted. The Melt has a display with 18 flavors of ice cream, all made locally at Superstition Farm in Mesa. The Melt offers traditional flavors as well as many creative ones, like “Fruity Pebbles”. The selection of flavors changes constantly, so there’s always something new to try. On my first visit, I tried “Super Farm”, chocolate and almonds mixed with Nutella. The ice cream was delicious, with the perfect level of sweetness. And the portion sizes are generous. At the Melt, you can choose to have your ice cream served in Chinese “takeout” boxes, along with a “fortune cookie” (a cookie with a prediction), between two cookies, or in a homemade waffle cone. The prices are reasonable, the service is excellent, and most importantly, the ice cream is delicious. If you’re looking for really good ice cream, try the Melt—you won’t regret it.

state: Wow, what great customer service! I own a business and even worked late as a owner, just to make sure my customers were satisfied. I arrived around 11 o’clock, which is supposed to be the closing time on Saturdays, and almost all the ice cream had already been stored away. They said, “I’m sorry, I’ve already put everything away and won’t make any more ice cream for you.” At 10:52, when I arrived, it wasn’t yet closing time. In my opinion, in the service industry, the customer always has the right to expect something. It doesn’t matter if you want to close a little earlier. Your job is simply to wait until 11 o’clock to collect everything. I’ve been here since they opened, and I’ve noticed a slight decline in the quality of work over time. It’s sad to see my ice cream shop with debris everywhere. I understand that there are good and bad times, and everyone should be happy. Right now, I’m not happy. I’m just glad my wife isn’t pregnant this time. I guess next time, I’ll go at 4 p.m. and wait until 11 o’clock to eat. Thanks again, Jeremy.

state: I’m very happy that they finally brought 85° to the Las Vegas area. The cakes and desserts here are delicious, adding an Asian touch to our small tourist town. From cheese bread with jalapeño to taro bread, and from milk buns to cupcakes, you really can’t go wrong when you come here. If you like salt, you might want to try the sea salt coffee, but usually I prefer an American coffee with ice. The best thing is that they pack everything in individual bags, which helps keep them fresh and preserves their flavor. If you have a birthday coming up, they also have great cakes and delicious tiramisu. Usually, it’s very crowded and noisy here because everything is so good, so I recommend considering that all tables might be occupied if you want to sit down. If you haven’t been there yet, you should go. It’s located in the new Shanghai shopping center, near some interesting restaurants. Of course, given the current situation, everything is mainly for taking home, but still, you’ll be very happy to leave this delicious place.

state: Mitchell’s is an institution in Cleveland—a must-visit place! Any fan of ice cream will love Mitchell’s, and appreciate the quality of the ingredients used in each flavor. I chose the coconut ice cream with chocolate chunks, as I’m a big fan of coconut, and also the “smores” ice cream. Recently, I tried several “smores” flavors that weren’t very good, but Mitchell’s managed to capture all the elements of this dessert and really made you feel like you were eating ice cream around a fire. I highly recommend trying the small containers, which allow you to try multiple flavors—it can be difficult to choose just one if you’re not looking for something specific. It’s great to observe and get to know the ice cream factory while enjoying a delicious ice cream.

state: We decided to try this place while we were in Las Vegas. The lines were long, and it took a while for our order to be processed. We bought a mini cannoli and a lobster. The only problem with this place is that it seems to be managed very inefficiently. It’s been a long time since I’ve seen Cake Boss, so I don’t know if the original location is managed in the same way. It shouldn’t take so long to serve a customer, pick up the items, and put them in a bag or box. It’s not clear to me why the process of ordering, picking up, and paying takes so long.

state: The girl who helped us is an evil, seductive temptress with her ice cream scoop. Here's the deal, I'm wicked lactose intolerant, I had just eaten a bunch of Mac and cheese and was already seriously regretting my life decisions. So of course, instead of just calling it a day, I suggest wandering over to Churn. Ya know, I hadn't been there before and I only want to LOOK. What's the harm in browsing? And then this girl, this adorably sweet and friendly girl behind the ice cream counter is all "oh, just try them! Here.. Have a sample of every flavor we have". So I do, I try them all. And then I order a brownie, and then shes all sweetly saying "why don't I top this off with a scoop of vanilla? And whipped cream with chocolate sauce? You cant just have a plain brownie.. That's just not right." And I'm like putty in her hands. I nod my head weakly in agreement, mumbling something like "no you can't have a plain brownie." And then I buy a bag of mini gummy bears, because, well because they're there.

state: This is my favorite ice cream place in Cleveland's west side. My most recent visit was specifically to try the ube ice cream. I also got taro so I could taste the difference between the two. I prefer ube, which was more flavorful and sweeter to me. Also, it is a pretty shade of purple! There are many other unique flavors here, and it changes weekly. Vegan flavors are available too. The best way to keep up with the ever changing menu is to follow their Instagram. I'm hoping they bring back the green tea soft serve soon. The shop is small, with outdoor seating and no indoor seating. Parking only has about five spaces, so it is easier to park on the street. The shop itself is super cute and has artwork of dogs eating ice cream on the wall and on the cups. It's just a perfect spot to hang out at during the summer.

state: It was very disappointing—it doesn’t meet the standards of Bouchon! My family and I have visited the Bouchon bakery in Yountville, California, many times, and this location in Las Vegas is inferior. We don’t fully understand why they don’t maintain proper quality control. But after trying to buy sweets there on our only day in Las Vegas, we felt it was necessary to write a review. We bought butter croissants and almond croissants, and both were stale and bad. They seemed to be at least a day old. In addition to having visited the Bouchon bakery in California several times, we’ve also eaten at the Bouchon Bistro in Yountville on various special occasions. We’ve never been disappointed there, and we always loved our meals. Maybe the Bouchon bakery in Las Vegas is managed by someone else?

state: took a trip to Jack Frost for a classmate's birthday... it was a little out of the way but the donuts looked too BOMB on yelp not to go. I came here around 7:00am and surprisingly there was a little line- a good sign! I ended up ordering a dozen for about $15. The donuts- I would guess they probably had 30 + different flavors when I was there. They had a variety of cake and yeast donuts, but it seemed like more cake donuts. Some flavors that I remember include salted caramel (counter lady said it was the best selling), maple bacon, german chocolate, pumpkin cheesecake, apple cinnamon, samoa, s'mores, fruity pebbles and captain crunch cereal covered donuts. The donuts are really well made. The texture of the cake itself is good, but the toppings were incredible and super fresh! Like people have said before, I have to take a star off for the unlabeled donuts. I would at least have a list or a sign. It got super tedious having to ask the worker what each donut was, and i noticed that customers in front of me just opted for a variety box where you don't choose what you get.

state: The location is the biggest challenge, but the execution of the delicious sweets is perfect. I started following them on social media, and all their creations seem impeccable. They put in a toasted marshmallow that was cooked right away, and I was thrilled. My companion chose a small portion of “Netflix and Relax”. We both voted for mine as the best, but her popcorn candy was different and fun.

state: I tried the Sprinkles cupcakes in Las Vegas. I bought one with vanilla flavor, but it was dense and dry. It had a lot of frosting, but no one liked it. I also tried the cinnamon and sugar cupcake; it was even drier than the vanilla one, and its texture was like a corn muffin. It was very hard to swallow. I still have the red velvet and banana cupcakes left to try, but after the first two, I’m not very excited. The red velvet cupcake wasn’t special either—it was dry again. The banana cake was wet, but it was very heavy. It’s better to save my money, since I can make better cakes than these.

The only thing I have to mention is that, to get your first free coffee at the Carmel location, you need to wait in line and wait for someone behind the counter to fill your cup. It’s a small price to pay for some of the best desserts and bread from Charlotte. The coffee is also excellent. It’s a great place for a breakfast sandwich or a light lunch sandwich (excellent paté), or for soup.

I really expected the ice cream to be more creamy. The birthday truffles were probably my favorites—a moist birthday cake covered with white chocolate. It was very creamy and delicious. And the “crack” cake was amazing. It’s truly unique. I haven’t tried the compost cookies yet, but so far I’m very excited. The staff was extremely informative, attentive, and friendly. Definitely a true fan!

Soon, I realized they gave us the wrong flavor, but I didn’t want to go back to the store and deal with the staff, nor did she. I’m afraid to go back due to my unpleasant experience during those two visits.

state: SHORTEST DONUT BAR LINE EVER (3.7 stars) It was shocking to see a 4 person line because the one in San Diego runs out the door and down the street. so many selections.... can i order them all ;P When you can't decide ALWAYS STICK TO THE ONE THAT CAUGHT YOUR EYE FIRST. And that delicious fattening fried batter goes to.... OHH MY BIRTHDAY CAKE OREO It was a very good donut but... I like my donuts with a little more fluff, a lot less sugar, and a custard texture in the middle. This was different. This was a donut with a reconstructed Oreo in the middle, with cake icing on the top with crumbles of Oreo and cake confetti. Sugar sugar and more sugar. If you strip all that and taste the donut, it's actually nothing special without that extra flavoring. The donut itself was dry. Again, good donut... I just have had a really good donut elsewhere that I hold high standards too. I'll be real honest though... donut bar seems to only be good because of the flavoring that covers the donut. Strip all that way and you have a boring stale and dry donut. Until the next review...

state:
Really? Am I really seeing this? I’ve reached the paradise of premenstrual syndrome. This lover of French culture has found a culinary paradise. My dear friend/companion, who is obsessed with food, shoes, and books, and I, we enjoyed our first visit to “Amelie’s” on Friday night. We were surprised by the energy, the efficiency of the staff (they kept things moving!), the original decorations, and the delicious dishes. We tried some desserts, and here’s what’s good, bad, and ugly:

**What’s good:** The “Creme Puffs” are filled with rich, sweet, and thick cream. There’s no watery cream here. I loved it! The “Salt Caramel Brownie”. If I had been with someone other than her, they would definitely have tried this delicious and sticky treat, and I would have stuck my fork in their hand. There’s almost a centimeter of caramel on this brownie, and a little salt prevents it from being too sweet. The “Tea Cakes” are very wet. The cranberry has a stronger flavor than lemon. The line moves quickly.

**What’s bad:** Well, actually it wasn’t that bad, but my husband and I tried the “Petit Gateau”. Although the “ganache” was rich and smooth (just like I like men, haha), the cake itself was quite dry. The line moves so fast that it’s possible I won’t get to try all the desserts. I like to analyze my options; calories are valuable, and I don’t want to waste them on mediocre snacks. There are many empty tables. No matter how fast they work, it seems like we’re losing some good options.

**What’s ugly:** There was almost a fight over the last “eclairs”, and that strange dummy that literally leans over your shoulder while you wait in line. I’m Leo, and I need my space. Although it sounds crazy, that thing scared me a little. Overall, it’s a favorite quick place to go, and a reason to visit Charlotte more often.

state: I have been the Vegas many times and every time we went by Carlos Bakery there was a huge line and even though I love sweets I couldn't stomach the line. Since we are staying at the Venetian it is now just a 5 minute walk away. This is a Thursday night and the wait was 10 minutes. We tried a little of everything and it was all very yummy. They have a lobster claw which is a cream filled pastry and it was great. I also tried the chocolate filled cream puff, the cannoli and two different cupcakes. Everything was fresh and delicious. They wrap everything up for you in a nice box with a gift-like presentation, very classy. The price point is such that everyone can afford to try "something" as most of the items are in the $3 to $5 each and I paid $11.00 for a chili dog earlier so in comparison this place is a deal. I still have 3 more days here in and I am certain I will be stopping by again to try some other delightful goodness. Update. I'm back several months later and this place is still rocking the sweets!! Make sure to add this to your list of must do's in Vegas! Enjoy!

state: In general: a wide variety of donuts, soft and delicious, pleasant atmosphere. This place is close to the ice cream shop where we had breakfast, so we decided to stop here for a snack afterwards. They have a great range of donuts and unique flavors, like the cream brûlée version. We ordered the blueberry-lemon donut and the cream brûlée donut. The cream brûlée donut had a layer of caramelized sugar and a vanilla cream filling. It was delicious! The donut had the perfect soft texture, and the filling was very creamy. The caramelized sugar gave a nice crunchy flavor. The blueberry-lemon donut was also excellent. I notice that sometimes cake donuts can be dense, but this one was perfectly soft, with just the right amount of filling—so it wasn’t overly sweet. To finish, their bathroom has adorable murals of Homer Simpson and his donut with pink frosting!

state: I love this place. Before I moved to Las Vegas, I used to come here every time I visited the city. I really enjoy the milk ice cream with cereal. I’ve also tried all their cookies, and I love giving them as gifts. The price is a bit high, but after all, you’re in Las Vegas, in a hotel, and that’s expected. Previously, they had other flavors like “red velvet” and their “cookie cake,” but due to the pandemic, they’re only serving milk ice cream with cereal, which doesn’t bother me, because that’s all I can find. I deduct one star due to inconsistency. Sometimes the staff are friendly, and sometimes the person working there is rude and not in the right mood. The consistency of the ice cream also varies. The ice cream I took photos of during my visit had a melted consistency, so it wasn’t very good. But I recommend trying it—it’s amazing how delicious milk ice cream with cereal can be! I love the Milk Bar and I love Cosmo too!

They have amazing cakes, but the ham and cheese croissant, which is more like a dry cake, is simply delicious. It’s always my favorite dish there. Their lavender lemonade is incredible and refreshing, and the staff are really friendly. You order the cakes first, and then the drinks. I loved seeing how welcoming this place is; I felt welcome from the moment I entered. Even though the staff were training a new member, they were very patient and attentive. This will become a place we’ll always visit when we go to Charlotte.

state: Wow, we were all tempted by their delicious Italian desserts and the variety of breads, cakes, and desserts! We were a little full after lunch, but there’s always room for us, especially for those irresistible desserts. We ordered “Ciccio” (a cream-filled pastry at $7.90), “Baba Al Limoncello” (a lemon-soaked sponge cake filled with lemon cream at $7.90), and “Terracotta” (chocolate mousse with butter caramel filling at $7.90). Also, we got a latte (I forgot the price?). All the desserts were delicious! 5 stars for the desserts! The price was a bit high; we spent about $36 in total, for 3 desserts and a latte. However, I would definitely go back, as they offer high-quality and delicious desserts.

state: I finally had my first Mitchell's Ice Cream experience. Many of my Cleveland friends have bragged about their ice cream, so I had some high expectations...and they were definitely met! My first time there I ordered the Caramel Sea Salt (caramelized brown sugar and sea salt). It was delicious. The prices are a bit steep for a scoop of ice cream ($3.35) but when you get to the front of the line and see how big the scoop is and how tasty it is, it's not such a bad price after all. My second time there I ordered chocolate peanut butter cup, again a heaping scoopful. The chocolate ice cream itself wasn't anything special from any other high end ice cream, but there were so many big chunks of peanut butter cup, enough for every bite. My boyfriend ordered the chocolate malt ($4.95) both times (btw he tends to consider himself a malt aficionado). The first time they gave him a chocolate shake by mistake. It was good, but it was made with chocolate ice cream (I guess chocolate malts are not made with chocolate ice cream) and wasn't the malt he'd ordered...so he was disappointed. The second time we finally got the malt (this time made with vanilla ice cream and chocolate syrup). He said he liked it, although not the best. To me the malt flavoring wasn't very noticeable and I think Sweet Moses makes better malts. Mitchell's put more malt flavoring in your malts! They use Hartzler's milk, I have never had their milk, but their egg nog is to die for (save that for another review) so I can only assume their milk is something special. Also it seems that most of the premium ice cream shops in Cleveland tend to use their milk. The store and building itself is also pretty impressive. You can go upstairs and view the entire kitchen from above, watching them make ice cream is cool. Also you know there's no funny stuff going on in there if you can see everything. Be warned, the lines can be long and seem impossible to get to the front in any reasonable time, but rest assured, there are a lot of people working the counter and those lines move really fast. Oh and they also let me bring my dog in with me to order my ice cream. I love places that are dog friendly! So many more flavors of ice cream still to try...a few blocks from home...I will be down there a lot this summer. Let's just hope my waistline can take all these visits.

state: Today, I visited Villani for the second time. I was planning to buy a bagel from Poppy’s at Teeter, but then I remembered that it was right nearby. I also bought a bialy for the second time. This time, I got the “Everything” version—with everything inside. Last time, I chose the “Sea Salt” version—with sea salt. I really like those slightly toasted ones. The edges are crispy enough, while the center remains soft. It’s a great bagel, without any holes, and the size is perfect. They offer dozens of beautiful macarons in various flavors, displayed like precious jewels in a window display! They also have slices of cake, muffins, cinnamon rolls, cookies (not as hard as some might think), scones like cheese and apple scones, croissants, and more. I’m sure I’m missing something. The chocolate-dusted cookie is special. It’s almost like a scone or cookie—it’s tall, fluffy, but crispy on the outside. When you open it, you can see some dough that seems to have been used to its best advantage by the oven. Check out my photos. Just to let you know, there’s a small table outside where you can sit, and I believe there are some tables inside too. It’s a place where you can come in and out quickly. That’s what I like about it. So, they have more space for baking. Other Yelp users said it’s more expensive than other bakeries, but I think the prices are fair considering all the effort involved. If it were cheaper, I would be fatter!

state: I was very lucky and ended up in a day when there were only 2 people in line behind me! Anyway, the bakery is absolutely charming! Located in the Venice neighborhood, it took some time to find it—we stopped at a parking lot and walked through the shops along the canal. But the walk to get there took us to places we would never have seen otherwise! It was really lovely. There are big windows where you can watch the cakes being decorated (but no one was there when we went…). It’s easy to understand why people get frustrated waiting—it’s a small place, and people tend to be hesitant and ask too many questions… When finally it was our turn at the counter, we ordered 2 cannoli covered in chocolate, 4 “Rainbow/Venetian/7-layered” cookies, and an original “lobster tail”. The total cost was just under $35!!! I don’t usually go to bakeries, but I’ve never spent so much on just 5 cakes and 4 cookies! But let me say this—they were really, really delicious!!! The cannoli here are huge and well-filled. The shells were thicker than usual, but they survived the trip back home! The cookies were exactly as I remembered them… I used to buy them from a small Italian bakery in my neighborhood when I was a child, and I rarely see them anymore—these were amazing! But the “lobster tail”—it was incredible and worth every penny ($5.50!!!). I was told that the cream contained bourbon, but I didn’t think I would recognize it, but it definitely was there! Secretly, it made my husband and me happy that we didn’t have to share it with the kids (LOL)!!! Definitely worth visiting once, if you’re a fan of the series or looking for Italian desserts. Probably I won’t go back, but I’m glad I tried it!

state: After watching the episode of Christina Tosi on “Chef’s Table” and trying the cereal milk in New York, I wanted to try the “crack” cake or the “compost” biscuit. The “compost” biscuit won my heart. Located inside the Cosmopolitan Hotel, next to Momofuku, I tried: – Ice cream with milk and “crack” flavors. They offered samples so we could choose between the two. The milk ice cream was better than the “crack” flavor. – “Compost” biscuit: a biscuit wrapped for $4. Overall, the ice cream (6 dollars) with corn flakes was just okay. Nothing special. However, the “compost” biscuit is probably the best (and most expensive) one I’ve ever tried. I ended up eating all 80g of the 340-calorie biscuit. I regret not buying more. The filling contains: coffee, caramel butter, chunks of chocolate, pretzels, and fried potatoes. What a salty-sweet combination! I’m sure I’ll try more biscuits next time.

state: Update: To better understand why the baked goods I bought from Carlo’s Bake Shop were stale and dry, I returned to this store just a few minutes before it closed for the night, in order to confirm my understanding of their business practices. It turns out that, at the time of closing, the shelves at Carlo’s Bake Shop were almost full of baked goods that hadn’t been sold that day. There was no “close sale” discount, as is common in other high-quality, freshly baked bakeries. When the store closed, the products continued to be sold at their original price. And when the doors closed for the night, the shelves remained filled with products that had to dry out overnight, losing their fresh taste and texture. It’s shameful for the owners of this store to allow customers to buy products from the previous day! Given the exorbitant prices charged here, isn’t it reasonable to assume that the products are actually baked on the same day? High-quality bakeries treat products left over overnight as “products from the previous day”. If these products aren’t sold at a discount before closing, or are simply thrown away, they’re removed from the main shelves and sold at discounted prices in other areas of the store. This practice isn’t applied at Carlo’s Bake Shop, where a selection of old products is combined with new ones. It depends on luck whether you get a fresh product when buying here. As for the numerous five-star reviews listed here, a reasonable explanation would be that they’re customers who don’t know better. However, it’s hard to believe that so many reviewers have never been to a high-quality French bakery that only sells freshly baked products. It’s not like there aren’t many fresh bakeries in the Las Vegas area (and many other cities), so I’m surprised by the large number of positive reviews for this store. It’s not yet recommended.

state: I’m a student in baking arts, so maybe I’m more demanding than an average customer. When I first came to Charlotte, I really loved it, but over time I’ve noticed that the quality of the products has somewhat declined. undoubtedly, the salty caramel brownies are incredible—they’re always my favorite dessert. They’re never bad, never disappointing, and always satisfying. Recently, I’ve been trying other desserts that are offered, and I’m a little disappointed. My friends who aren’t chefs love them, but I can see that some of the products could be really great. For example, the croissants don’t meet my expectations. The staff is excellent, the location is fantastic, and the number of seats is wonderful. Even if you can’t find a seat in the main building, there are extra seats outside, as well as in the courtyard at the back. I’ve gone at different times of day, and I always find a seat. I give it 3 stars because I can’t surpass the quality of the desserts. However, the food might be the most underrated part of the restaurant. The soup is delicious, especially the one with carrots and ginger, and the cheese creams are amazing. Finally, I can’t forget to mention that it’s open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. It’s an incredible place to visit in groups or alone. It’s important to observe people at different times of day, as the number of people varies depending on the hour.

state: Why haven’t I visited this place before, considering that I usually pass by here when I’m in the Matthews/Ballentyne area? It’s an experience you shouldn’t miss if you’re in Charlotte! This place is amazing, and you definitely need to try its matcha ice cream and other desserts. It’s a small café with limited seating due to the pandemic, but the staff are very kind and do their best, which I appreciate. The matcha ice cream is undoubtedly the must-try item for visitors—it’s creamy, delicious, and truly reflects the flavors of matcha I’ve tasted in Japan. Vanilla matcha ice cream is a good option if you’re not used to the bitter taste of matcha, but this combination is excellent anyway. I also tried hojicha (toasted matcha tea?), black sesame (seasonal), and ube (seasonal)—all of them are great. Hojicha remains one of my favorites, along with the matcha ice cream. Black sesame is also a good choice if available. Ube is much lighter than I expected, so if you’re looking for the intense flavor found in Filipino restaurants, you might need to adjust your expectations a bit. I’ve only tried the other matcha ice cream with all the toppings, and I recommend trying it if you’re hungry or want to share. I’ve tried it several times in Japan, and this place meets expectations as a dessert option. Parking is easy, and there are many food options nearby. Or, if you prefer boba, Kung Fu Tea is just a short distance away—my mother preferred boba over ice cream, so there’s plenty for everyone :D I recommend visiting this place if you’re in the southern part of Charlotte/Matthews/Ballantyne, but really, if you’re in Charlotte, it’s a place you should definitely visit. It’s unique and leaves a very positive impression.

state: I love the cake boss show and all of their spin off Shows as well. It's been a long time that I've been waiting to try Buddie's bakery goods, specially their red velvet cupcake as Carlos so many times teaches other bakers how to master it and it's staple cream cheese frosting. So, after 20 minutes in line my husband and I finally got to the ordering panel. By the time we got there, there was no tiramisu. So my husband ordered a strawberry short cake. I ordered the oh so famous red velvet cupcake. After another 15 minutes waiting for our order, we finally got our goods. Everything was just ok. I was NOT expecting just ok! The red velvet cupcake looked like a cupcake I can get at traders joe's. Tasted ok, nothing woow! My husbands strawberry short cake was tasty, but not tasty enough for that price. Even an amazing dessert at a fancy place is slightly cheaper!!!! I wanted to love this place! But, not impressed at all!

state: I had no idea what to expect from this bakery. My wife makes cakes as gifts, and I see her watching “Cake Boss,” but I must admit I’m not very familiar with all the details of the show related to the bakery. The bakery seems to be a replica of the one in Hoboken, New Jersey. The interior is very clean, but small. The line was long, but considering the place just opened and there’s a lot of anticipation around it, I won’t complain about the line. It was difficult for someone who just wanted a cannoli or a cookie. It was one of the things I bought for my wife, and seeing how fun she and her granddaughters were made it all worth it. We bought some boxes of sweets, and my wife ordered a special box for me, so she and the girls could try the sweets, and I could get mine. She knew this trip wasn’t what I wanted, so she was very thoughtful. I tried some cannolis that were filled on the spot. They have pre-packaged options, as well as empty cannoli shells, so you just say whether you want them filled or not. I think those who choose the pre-packaged option and don’t ask if they can be filled will end up with wet results. I tried a carrot cupcake that was wet and delicious. The lobster is amazing, and I can only imagine how the XL version of “Buddy V’s” must be—it’s across the street! My “cream puff” was the best thing after the lobster. I just wish it were bigger. I liked everything, but it seemed strange when my wife showed me the mug with “Carlo’s” written on it. But how? We’re in Las Vegas! Please buy mugs that really say “Las Vegas.” That makes sense!

It’s different from any other dessert where sugar dominates and you just feel it. I feel that this place is underrated and deserves more attention. The texture of their boba was also very good. Soft and not very chewy, but with an elastic texture. The woman in front who helped us was very kind! She gave us samples of ice creams and made sure we were satisfied. The black sesame and banana ice cream was delicious! In my opinion, their taro ice cream (a type of sweet potato) had a better flavor than the taro ice cream sold in Asian stores. I definitely recommend this store to my friends and family.

state: How could a famous and high-quality chocolate and ice cream store receive a 1-star rating? Read on… We really wanted to try the sundae with brownies and the melted chocolate cake. We had been here before, so we didn’t hesitate to come this way, from where we were staying. But we were wrong. After a very long wait (just one cashier serving customers), we were told that there were no brownies for two weeks, and no more melted chocolate cake either (even though there was a photo of it on the wall). We ordered the regular sundae, which is usually very good. But this time it wasn’t the same. Something was wrong. I understand the situation caused by COVID and the challenges it poses for employers, but the staff’s attitude was horrible. After making our order and waiting, we bought some chocolates. We bought a lot of candies in large packages—the packaging didn’t seal properly. We asked the staff, and their response was, “Yes, we know these packages don’t seal well, but we have a label.” I thought a label couldn’t keep a plastic package sealed, so I asked if we could use another package. They said yes, but it would cost extra. So they are deliberately distributing defective packages and then trying to charge for another package? What??? I think it’s another way of generating revenue, like the fees for express baggage services in airlines or resort fees in hotels. So I went over and waited to pay, but I had to go back to the line because they wouldn’t serve me at the “gifts” counter. After another 20 minutes in line, I got the candies, and fortunately, I put them in a bag… Why “fortunately”? Well, the label didn’t hold, and the candies fell out of the defective plastic package and into the bag. I don’t know what happened here, but we won’t be back. Residents and tourists, be careful!

state: Let me start by saying, THEIR ICE CREAM IS NOT SWEET. It's this weird salty sour concoction that I think is supposed to taste like corn flakes... don't make the mistake I did and make sure you go in knowing that. Now that we got that out of the way. I got the greatest hits sampler which included a slice of crack pie, compost cookie, 3 birthday truffles, and a small portion of their "cereal" ice cream. Compost cookie was interesting, pie was cold which was a bummer, ice cream was interesting once you get over the fact that it's not sweet, but the truffles... the truffles were pretty stinking good. If you come here for anything please get the birthday truffles. All in all, definitely come here for pastries. I feel like this place is overhyped and I really wish I had lower expectations coming here. People are friendly! Interesting experience. Definitely want to try the famous birthday cake but a 6 inch cake comes with a hefty price tag of $56.

state: After several visits to Las Vegas and staying at hotels on the Strip, my husband and I finally visited this branch of Ghirardelli Ice Cream & Chocolate Shop. A sudden craving for ice cream struck us while we were staying at a hotel on The Linq. After quickly checking what was open during Tuesday night, we found Ghirardelli Ice Cream & Chocolate Shop. We really had missed out on this opportunity, as our ice creams were simply amazing! Located on The Linq’s Promenade, the store was easily accessible on foot from the hotel. As we approached Ghirardelli Ice Cream & Chocolate Shop, we saw various groups of friends, families, and couples walking around with delicious ice creams. Even though we visited after 10 p.m. on a weekday, the line to order was almost just outside the store. Who would have thought that Ghirardelli Ice Cream & Chocolate Shop was the perfect place to go at night? My husband and I ordered our own ice creams: the “World Famous Hot Fudge Sundae” and the “Gold Rush Sundae,” respectively. Both were incredibly tasty and delicious. The “Gold Rush” combined all my favorite flavors in one ice cream: sweet, salty, caramel, and white chocolate. It’s a great option for those who aren’t very fond of chocolate and also enjoy the contrast between sweet and salty flavors. I highly recommend it. Just a note: the prices may be a bit higher due to its location right on the Strip. Don’t worry about ordering; honestly, these mini ice creams can be shared with someone else. In any case, our visit was very positive and deserves five stars.

state: Wow. This place is clean and modern. The people at the counter are incredibly polite, patient, and friendly! I tried almost all the flavors without any fuss. Here are some highlights: White Chocolate with Strawberry: White chocolate ice cream in the same container as strawberry sorbet. Delicious and creamy, combining sweetness and acidity… two flavors for one price! I really liked it, but those who don’t like white chocolate might not appreciate it as much. Salty Caramel: The staff said this was the most popular flavor, so obviously I had to try it. It was delicious, rich, and creamy, with the perfect caramel taste! Walnut Tartar: Delicious ice cream with irresistible homemade lasagna. I’m craving it now. White Roses: Pure and sweet. What a feeling! Lemon (Basis Lime): This was truly surprising! Sweet, tart, and incredibly refreshing! Two cheese options: This one is incredibly creamy. At first, it has a sweet, caramel-like taste with almonds, and then the cheese flavor stands out. At first, I thought it was a bit strange, but after a few bites, I fell in love with it! Brownie with Ice Cream: There’s no way to go wrong with brownies! This gourmet version is better than the classic! The homemade lasagna and cones were all fresh and tasty! My sister ordered a sandwich with ice cream and white chocolate, which I tried. It was fantastic. I can’t wait to go back!

state: There’s no better coffee in Las Vegas than this one. Moreover, its delicious pastries—oh, I love macarons!—make it the perfect place to take a break in the afternoon. They also have sandwiches, so it’s a good option for lunch, especially if you’re on a business trip and need to move around quickly. During my last visit, I tried an applewood-flavored latte that I’ll never forget. It had the perfect balance of flavors; not too sweet, with just the right amount of apple flavor. If you like Starbucks’ pumpkin spice latte, don’t buy this one—after trying what truly great coffee is possible, you might never want to drink at Starbucks again. This coffee might be a bit hard to find. It’s located in the Venetian, near the Phantom Theatre. You won’t see it until you get very close. But keep walking until you find it, because it’s worth visiting.
