state: After visit #2, I'm still not sure why this place is rated as high as it is. The decor, location and staff is 5 star, but the ice cream is just not that good. The first visit I sampled three different ice creams before deciding not to purchase any, since the flavors were not my favorite. However, my mother purchased the chocolate and it was just meh. We ended up throwing half of it out. I decided to give them another shot since we came at an odd time. My husband and I both got some ice cream. His pick was the vegan PB&J and he enjoyed it, but nothing fantastic and I got the Butter Cake in a cone. The cake tasted stale and the flavor was just off. I know that it is handcrafted ice cream, but I prefer to go to the grocery store and purchase some good old Ben and Jerry's.

state: Oh man!! This place is SO good! It's a little ice cream shop near downtown phx. It's a cute cozy place. The owner, Brandon, is super nice, and very helpful. You could tell he loved his shop. He gave my boyfriend and I suggestions, and told us what exactly was in each flavor. There's eight total flavors, half is limited, while the other half their signature flavors. I had a limited flavor which was the Black Raspberry Cashew, boy do I tell you, it is the BEST ice cream I've had in awhile! I was contemplating on getting it in a warm glazed donut until the Leslie Knope (love the name by the way) caught my eye. It's a warm waffle sandwich. You also get a free topping with it, so I got the basic sprinkle (boring I know) but it was so good! Thinking about it now makes me wish I had one. My boyfriend had the Leslie Knope as well but with the Cookie Monster flavor (one of their signatures). That was also delicious! It is definitely a must try! You will not regret it!

state: I used to go to Mary Coyle many years ago and loved it. I tried this new Mary Coyle now, and it was the greatest disappointment of all. First of all, there were no menus to refer to. I had to use my phone to look up the menu before ordering. I ordered a sundae with hot chocolate sauce. The chocolate sauce wasn’t hot at all; it seemed like it had been taken from the bottom of a burnt pot. It was horrible. When I asked about the chocolate sauce, the only employee said, “That’s all we have.” It’s obvious I won’t go there again, and I wouldn’t recommend Mary Coyle to any of my friends either.

state: Sprinkles’ cupcakes are generally delicious. Some flavors are significantly better than others. Most of the time, the cupcakes are very soft, which is always a positive point, especially if you prefer not to use glaze. Glaze has a good taste and isn’t overly sweet or sticky. Both would be serious flaws in my opinion. I was really impressed with the chocolate with peanut butter, chocolate marshmallow, and coconut flavors. The chocolate with peanut butter is undoubtedly the best. Definitely. I was disappointed with the black and white flavors and chocolate with caramel (this was a flavor not available on the menu). The atmosphere in the cupcake shop is very fun! Although, most of the time, there are more flavors available inside the shop. But it’s worth buying at least one cupcake from the shop, at least once!

state: DRIPPS is my answered prayer and biggest blessing to the Chandler area this year. I'm not kidding when I say I come here at least once a week. When they first opened in September, it was even more than that, taking advantage of their soft opening and grand opening discount and BOGO. They are an awesome company, from the owners over at Pokitrition. The star here is CEREAL INFUSED SOFT SERVE. And no, it is not just some cereal just sprinkled into the ice cream. It is generous amounts of cereal of your choice literally DRILLED in and it is the best cereal ice cream in the world. I am a huge fan of Christina Tosi's Milkbar cereal ice cream, but Dripps takes it to a whole other level. I can assure you your favorite childhood cereal is among their choices. They do have signature creations you could choose from and mix and match toppings, but what I love to do is just choose a cereal and use the same cereal as topping. Their "supporting actor" I would say is their matcha drinks. If you love matcha, you will be in heaven. They use real QUALITY matcha. Great flavor, good caffeine kick without the jitters. Next favorite is the rose milk tea. It's not too "flowery" it is more milky which I love. Their milk teas are good as well. The only one negative thing is the boba balls are not as soft as I would love them to be but I enjoy milk teas without boba so they get a pass. The whole concept is just amazing and I'll shout it from the rooftops if I could. I LOVE DRIPPS!

state: One day, as I walked down the street, my sense of smell detected a certain scent. Could it be a sandwich or a cake? I thought. Ah! It was the smell of a donut. My big kangaroo feet helped me get there as quickly as possible. I turned a corner and saw a large building. It looked like any other building, but inside, I knew there was something special. I entered and I was overwhelmed by smells I had never experienced before. So many pleasant smells in one place left me breathless; I screamed and ran away. Finally, I mustered up the courage to go back and crawled over to the counter. I ordered something, and when I tasted my first bite, I screamed so loudly that my cat heard me (she told me about it later). I jumped out in a hurry. It takes time to gain courage, but once you do, it’s worth it.

state: The traditional ice cream shop in the neighborhood offers delicious (and affordable) portions, perfect for enjoying outdoors. Finally, I got the chance to visit this classic in Cleveland after waiting all through winter—it’s only open during spring and summer. One of its main attractions—and probably the reason it won the “Best Ice Cream Shop in Cleveland” award in 2016—is the “Honey Hut,” which evokes nostalgia. Nothing is more reminiscent of the past than a small wooden cabin by the roadside. Fortunately, they anticipated popularity and have a large parking lot (entrance via Buechner Ave). The canopy over the cabin covers just a few meters, so on rainy or sunny days, it’s wise to bring an umbrella while waiting in line. When I arrived, there were two windows for ordering, along with some staff who handled more complex orders like smoothies, milkshakes, and sundae. When it was my turn, I was surprised to find that I had spent so much time choosing flavors, and I didn’t realize that my two generous portions cost only $3. It’s just a joke. I chose to enjoy myself in the partially covered patio, but keep in mind that if it rains or the weather is bad, the gaps in the roof won’t provide much protection. “Honey Pecan” seems to be the traditional flavor here, so I tried it and liked it, but I was a little disappointed because it was mostly nuts with very little honey. I preferred the seasonal flavor “Dark Chocolate Cayenne,” with its mild spicy taste at the end. The consistency was dense, but not the creamy texture I expected. It wasn’t as creamy as those offered at Mitchell’s and Piccadilly either, and there were some areas where the ice cream was frozen. Traditional and simple flavors, without many extras. I would be happy to spend an extra $3 for a reliable cone—although it isn’t top-tier.

state: Ice cream sandwiches made with donuts? Throw in your favorite childhood cereal? The Spice Girls are playing on the radio? I'm done... Just done... And in the best way yall. I am obviously on a major dessert kick right now... along with Zinfandel. My wife sneakily snuck me to Ninety's Ice Cream and Sandwiches a few months back and I ashamed that I have not yet been back. I got their famous donut ice cream sandwich and added cookie crisp to it. Kids, let me tell you the amazing adventure that my taste buds went on here. They basically cook it in something that looks like a grilled-cheese sandwich cooker and out pops this softball sized icecream that is encased inside a donut. The warmth of the donut against the cool, firm, ice cream is just a great experience for your mouth. Not as messy as you would think either. However, I really don't let food sit around long enough to melt.

state: I pass by here (ironically, to go to the gym!) and I’ve always been interested in taking a look. It looks lovely from the window. We were in that area because of something related to the dog, so my husband waited with the dog while I went in. My husband asked if I wanted anything for him, or warned me that he would eat whatever I bought. I’ll keep that in mind. The café has an old-fashioned atmosphere. It reminds me of a Viennese café. I went to the counter and saw lots of beautiful pastries. Unfortunately, pastries aren’t very practical for a quick purchase. The brownies were huge and could fit into the size of a shared dessert. Then, I looked up and thought I saw “whoopie pies” (a type of pastry popular in Pennsylvania). I read more carefully and found out that they’re cookies filled with peanut butter cream. Perfect! We sat on the bench outside and shared that delicious dessert. The butter cream was light and matched well with the chocolate-chip cookie. It was a bit difficult to eat, but it was delicious. The dog also loved sitting on the bench!

state: The ladies who were there were so sweet, serving us at 7:59pm when they closed at 8. I really appreciated that! Also the prices were extremely reasonable. That being said... the chocolate on the bonbons were all cracked and bubbly, clearly not tempered right. I ordered an espresso bonbon which I did enjoy. It oozed a sweet espresso goo in the middle, though the sugar granuals were present, having not been melted when mixed. The rum-dipped dark chocolate bonbon was the real displeasure. It was clearly milk chocolate, and dry at that. And the inside was so disappointing I had to write something. The "rum filing" was a congealed sugar solid that tasted nothing of rum. I've never not wanted to finish a chocolate treat. Maybe they had been in the case for too long as the bonbons definitely varies depending on ingredients. Their cupcakes are out of this world, though.

state: When I realized I was staying at the Venetian, I immediately knew I needed to visit this place and buy some sweets and macarons! When I found out it was close to the elevator entrance for the apartments, I was thrilled! It’s a pity they close at 8 or 9 p.m.; otherwise, it would be a great snack before going to the bar. However, I went there in the morning at 8 a.m., and there was already a long line! Since I was leaving that day, I waited and managed to get a raisin cake, bread pudding, 12 macarons (they were in pre-packaged packages, so smaller than those sold individually), and a chai tea! (Yes, everything for me, though not all at once!) The raisin cake was delicious, but it was too sweet. I thought the chai tea would go well with the raisin cake, but the chai tea was even sweeter. Definitely won’t order her chai tea again. When I got home, I tried the bread pudding—it was delicious!!! And the macarons? Absolutely amazing. We’re done here.

state:
A perfect place for taking photos for your social media :P The people and atmosphere are very welcoming and friendly, and the line moved quickly! Here’s how to order:

1. Choose the type of taiyaki (fish-shaped waffle) and the filling, if you want.
2. Select the ice cream flavor – just like you want the fish to eat the ice cream, hahaha!
3. When your order is ready, they will ask if you want any extra toppings on your ice cream. I don’t remember exactly, but I think we had options like: shredded coconut, oat cookies, cereals, and strawberries.

I ordered my taiyaki separately, because I know that both the fish and I will melt or fall apart with the taro filling (which is DELICIOUS!), and the Ube ice cream (which isn’t my favorite, but others liked it).

Enjoy!!

state: Visited The Vegan Doughnut Company today after much anticipation and hearing many rave reviews!! It 100% lived up to the hype! I tried the Fruity Cereal Milk and wow, it was delicious. The dough was so airy, fluffy, and light. It was sweet, but not overwhelmingly so. I also tried a few bites of their Easter-themed doughnuts, which were more of a cake doughnut consistency and also top-notch. The quality of these doughnuts is truly unmatched. I've heard a non-vegan say that these were the best doughnuts they've ever had. The location of the Vegan Doughnut Company is extremely convenient, on the main street of Lakewood. There is ample parking space in the lot for the shopping center behind the shop. Love to support this excellent local business.

state: I went to Sprinkles store on the opening day. I feel very lucky because I thought the store was already open for some time. I believe I waited in line for about 20 minutes (maybe less). While waiting in line, there were staff members who were ready to give me information about the flavors and answer any questions. I arrived around 2 p.m. (Holly Madison was there to start serving cupcakes). I talked with about 3 staff members while waiting, and the line wasn’t very long. I got detailed information about the cupcakes’ flavors, which was helpful. The staff are really friendly and helpful. This was my first time visiting any Sprinkles store. I thought the decor, both inside and outside the building, was nice. There’s an outdoor rest area. Two separate doors: one for buying cupcakes, and another for ice cream. The line for cupcakes was longer than the line for ice cream. I really liked getting to see the menu before ordering (I could decide which flavors I wanted while waiting). I bought 4 cupcakes: Black & White, Strawberry, Lemon with Coco, and Vanilla. They have options with or without frosting. Each cupcake costs $3.75. If you buy 4 cupcakes, it’s $15. They also sell cupcakes in sets of 12, which cost $24 (I think that’s the price). Before the staff writes down your order, there’s a display showing what’s being sold that day (the menu also indicates which items are available that day, so you won’t have too many expectations). I like that the cake isn’t too sweet and is soft and moist. There isn’t much frosting either, like in other places that sell cupcakes. My favorite flavor is Lemon with Coco: the lemon cake and coconut frosting have a balanced taste; none of the flavors are too strong (I love it!). If you like lemon, it’s definitely worth trying. I also like that the flavors aren’t too intense, but you know they’re there. A perfect cupcake. I rarely say this about any place that sells cupcakes or desserts, because I make cakes myself and don’t like very sweet desserts. They have cute wooden spoons and knives you can buy before leaving the store (I LOVE IT!). They also sell cupcake mix and t-shirts. I was thinking of buying the cupcake mix while waiting, but I quickly found out that each mix costs $15. I think it makes sense, since Sprinkles is basically a brand. I decided not to buy the cupcake mix. I parked free at Flamingo Casino, which is a short walk from The Linq. I’m not sure if The Linq has its own parking lot. They accept credit cards, like most places in Las Vegas. They also accept Amex.

state: I always start my reviews by telling people that I’m a talented chef and baker, so I know well about good food. That’s why I decided to start reviewing restaurants. Amélie is a bakery that’s completely overpriced; it offers French pastries and bakery products. What bothers me the most is the price of its macarons. As a baker, I know how much it costs to make them, and yet they shouldn’t cost more than $2.00 per unit. That’s absurd. Additionally, they have many flavors, but very few of them have a taste that goes beyond sugar. In my opinion, this means they’re cutting back on the extracts and ingredients that give them flavor. Still, their lime tart is really good—one of the best I’ve tried. I also think their pastries are pretty good too. The rest just isn’t great.

state: Only two stars, because the fact is that yes, I have experienced better than the pastries at the Las Vegas Bouchon Bakery. The best of what I sampled was the chocolate croissant: it had two ribbons of chocolate in it, which was quite nice. However, the pastry was just a bit too tough when it should have been tender, and it was too greasy. I also took tastes of four different macaron flavors: chocolate, vanilla, raspberry and lemon. The chocolate was far and away the best of the four, but it was more like a brownie than a macaron. The weakest were the raspberry and lemon, which had too much oozy filling. Worst of what I tried: the pain au raisin. Pain au raisin is supposed to be a custard raisin roll, not a raisin danish. Flat, extremely greasy... I will only grudgingly acknowledge that there were enough raisins and that they were soft and tender, but that couldn't salvage the thing. I don't know, maybe I'm holding this place to unfairly high standards, but I know that pastry can be better.

state: I’ve been to Novel many times, considering that the store hasn’t been open for very long. Novel is a small and delicious ice cream/donut shop, located very close to my house. They offer a decent variety of flavors that change frequently. Their ice cream is really delicious… even the simplest flavors are excellent (vanilla flavor is incredible… strawberry flavor tastes like fresh strawberries). My favorite flavor is “Fat Elvis”: bacon and peanut butter—a delicious combination! My only concern is that they don’t tell us where their ice cream comes from… they don’t make either the ice cream or the donuts in the store, and when asked, they say they buy them from a local person who doesn’t want to reveal their identity. That’s a bit… strange. Besides, the ice cream is good… the dough for the donuts is incredibly good too (and personally, I don’t really like donuts very much…). My husband likes “Leslie Knops”. The prices are reasonable (5 dollars for a “Leslie Knop”, which includes two ice cream flavors and a topping). I’ve brought many friends here, and I recommend they try it too.

state: Finally! A 24-hour open place in Charlotte. A friend recommended it to me, and I’m very glad she did. I go to Amelie’s once a week to meet up with friends, have coffee, and enjoy delicious (and hearty) cakes and desserts. I love that it’s always open, and that the staff are incredibly friendly and helpful. They offer a wide variety of freshly baked cakes and desserts. There’s also bread, sandwiches, and soups. A few weeks ago, I bought a baguette, but the next day, it wasn’t there anymore! It’s a really unique and fun place to visit with friends. They’re always busy, so be prepared to wait in line, but it’s definitely worth it. One warning: although everything is made in the bakery and available 24 hours a day, not all items are as fresh as they seem. The cakes are refrigerated to keep them fresh and cold, which may make it difficult to eat them right away and not always pleasant. I would probably avoid those cakes unless I see them coming out of the bakery and know they were made recently. I recommend the tarts and small cakes. They offer a lot of small desserts, so it’s easy and affordable to try many things at once without feeling overwhelmed. Amelie’s is definitely worth the trip, even if it’s just for a coffee break.

state: Last year, I saw the “rope skipping” game in the farmers’ market, and I bought lavender honey and baby cake from their tent. I liked the honey, but I didn’t like the baby cake. Now, after a year, I thought about trying it again, as I found out that the tent was located inside an art market. I bought nut caramel bars, brownies, baby cake with champagne, and sticky butter cake. I wanted to try some of them before writing a review. My rating for each item is as follows: Nut caramel bars (2/5): It wasn’t overly sweet, which I liked. There was a good amount of nuts. But the overall taste wasn’t very good. Brownies (3/5): Again, not very sweet; it had a more bitter taste. I liked the caramel on top. Overall, it was okay. Baby cake with champagne (2/5): Very sweet, not moist, seemed heavy. Sticky butter cake (1/5): Extremely sweet. And that was the only thing I could feel. I couldn’t eat more than one bite.

Once inside, it seems that Carlo’s Bakery is divided into a gift shop section and a bakery section. Many shelves are filled with T-shirts and ceramic mugs. During my visit, I didn’t find any bread or rolls; most of the baked goods were cupcakes, cookies, and some Italian desserts like cannoli and lobster rolls. We shared a lobster roll with walnuts. The dough was extremely crispy, like raw spaghetti. The inside was filled with cream. Although it wasn’t clearly identified as walnuts, it was still creamy. I gave it three stars because, overall, it’s a rather mediocre bakery.

state: There are a variety of pastries that you can choose from. They bake it there at their bakery. All pastries are individually wrapped. You take a tray and grab whatever you want and place it on the tray. Then, you stand in line to pay for it. They also have drinks and whole cakes that you could buy as well. I got a marble taro bun, guava strudel, and a Hokkaido custard. All where amazing! The marble taro bun was very soft and chewy! On the inside there's a thick taro filling that tasted so comforting! It went so well with the bread! The guava strudel was very tasty! The guava filling was strong and the breading on the outside was very flaky, crunchy and not too sweet. I wish there was more guava filling! But, it was yummy! The Hokkaido custard was delicious! It tasted like a milk cheesecake! It was soft and creamy and the crust was baked to perfection. Soft and crunchy at the same time. I definitely would get these items again. I will be back here to try the other pastries!

state: Jeni’s is exactly what Charlotte needed. It’s located in South End, a great area with many residents and a popular spot in the city. The ice cream is absolutely creamy and smooth, refreshing, tasty, and really delicious. There’s a wide variety of flavors, and they’re all unique. It’s completely different from other ice cream places in Charlotte. Jeni’s is a bit expensive, but you pay for the quality, and I think it’s well worth it. The waffle cones are amazing and made right away. My favorite flavor is Brambleberry Crisp – you really should try it, especially if you like red fruits. Definitely go to Jeni’s if you’re in the area and looking for a cold, delicious dessert.

state: This was such a cute little ice cream place, although it was a little difficult to get to because there was construction on the nearby roads! I really liked the swirly mural on the exterior of the building. The interior isn't anything special and very tiny -- no places to sit inside (there were several outdoor tables though), which was disappointing because it was 110 degrees outside. The ice cream: The flavor selection was definitely varied and featured several unusual flavors, like Thai tea, fruity pebbles, and ricanelas. I got the fruity pebbles and red, white, and blue sky (I visited on July 5th -- it consisted of strawberry, blueberry, and lemon) flavors and both were awesome! I especially liked the fruity pebbles one because it reminded me of eating cereal as a kid. The red, white, and blue sky was also delicious and not overpoweringly fruity, which was nice. My mom said that the ricanelas and Thai tea flavors were good, although she was miffed because the female cashier gave her less ice cream than the male one did! Side note: The male server was very friendly! My dad got the blueberry muffin flavor, which wasn't anything special, and my brother got the chocolate and cherry flavors, which he said were good! Presentation: I thought it was cute how they serve ice cream in Chinese takeout containers with fortune cookies instead of the standard cup! I found it kept the ice cream from spilling as much as it does when it's in a cup and the servers can be more generous in portion sizes. Price: For a double scoop, it was $5.25, which isn't too bad for such cool flavors! I would definitely come back!

state: I missed my favorite donut—a simple one filled with maple cream and topped with chocolate frosting. After reading all the positive reviews about Jack Frost here, my partner and I went shopping this morning to get a dozen of them and enjoy our “sugar addiction.” I hoped to find my favorite donut, but unfortunately, I didn’t find it. They don’t label anything, which was what I expected, but even though they weren’t very crowded, they were quick and efficient, which made us feel like they really wanted our order and wanted to get it out quickly. So we didn’t ask many questions. In short, these donuts are good. They’re not exceptional, but they’re fine. The only problem is that their “filled” donuts aren’t really filled at all. They just don’t make holes and don’t put any filling on top. We’re not fans of that. I ordered a donut filled with maple cream, and indeed, it was covered in white cream. There was so much cream that I had to remove half of it to be able to eat it. The other donut I ate was a chocolate-frosted cake donut, which is my other favorite. It was good, but the ones I can get at Sheetz are just as good, at least for me. Anyway, we might look for another bakery that suits our tastes better, but they’re better than Dunkin, and we have more options too.

state: He’s come here about ten times. Six times just to get a coffee, and four times to buy donuts. I don’t understand it. I try, but I can’t get excited about them. We saw this store when it opened for the first time, and I thought, “Their temperatures/measures aren’t adjusted for Las Vegas’ altitude.” After all, it’s a store based in San Diego, if I remember correctly. If you order a plain donut—one that isn’t filled or covered with cookie dough—all of them are dry:(. The worst part is that they’re very expensive. A plain donut costs $2. In any other place, a donut with frosting costs less than $0.99. The more “creative” the donut, the more expensive it gets. The French toast donut is actually good, but it doesn’t need syrup or extra raisin topping, since the donut already has powdered sugar and frosting on it. When you’re very hungry, it seems perfect. The only other advantage is their Kona hazelnut coffee—I think I found the same product online, so I can avoid the trip, paying for parking, and the disappointment of dry donuts.

state: I like to think of myself as a cookie/baked goods connoisseur, so when I found out about The Batch Maker I couldn't wait to go. I stood in line opening morning with my twin boys and enjoyed my treat and Tres Leches coffee. Since then, my boys and I are weekly regulars for many reasons: 1) This is hands down the best treats I have ever consumed. The Smore's Brownie, Cookie Dough brownie, Oreo Truffle cookie and the pop tarts are all worth every penny. I still have many treats to try. 2) THE STAFF and CRIS- they make you feel at home, greet you with a smile and take time with each customer to ensure he/she gets exactly what they need. 3) Kid-friendly- There are definitely some coffee places that make you feel awkward when you roll in with two toddlers, but The Batch Maker welcomes kids with open arms. They have a kid cart, which includes toys, games and everything to keep your toddler busy while you enjoy your coffee/latte HOT. They also offer storytime on Saturdays in the space next door with additional treats. 4) Tres Leches Latte-get it! The Batch Maker is the highlight of our guests' trips to Charlotte. I always recommend our Airbnb guests to stop in, and when they do they rave about it... as I do. Kudos to Cris and her absolutely incredible team and staff for making The Batch Maker such a special place for our family to visit every week. It's our favorite place in Charlotte!

state: During our last trip to Las Vegas, we discovered this bakery. But we were too full to try anything. For our next visit, I wanted to make sure I tried at least one of the delicious cakes offered by this bakery. It’s the bakery of Buddy Valastro (the face of the TV show “Cake Boss”), but that didn’t really matter to me. What really caught my attention were the desserts. They’re impressive and offer a wide variety. I also liked how they reinterpreted classic desserts, like the Boston cream pie, which they serve in a small circular mold instead of as a single piece of cake. I ordered the “Lobster Tail,” which is their specialty. It’s a croissant shaped like a lobster tail, covered with powdered sugar and filled with fluffy cream. I loved it, and it seemed like an extreme version of a “cream puff”. My husband ordered the “Oreo cake tower”. I’m not sure if it was mentioned in the description, but it turned out to be a cheese cake, which my husband doesn’t like. I didn’t get a chance to try it, but judging from the size of the dessert, a cheese cake would be quite large. We had to wait in line when we arrived, but I know this isn’t unusual at this place. What I didn’t like was the appearance of the employees; they seemed bored and indifferent. They completely ruined the fun atmosphere of this place, making you feel like you’re in an episode of “Soup Nazi” from “Seinfeld”. They work with delicious desserts all day long; just smile!

state: I visited to find the perfect French macarons in my area. Bouchon’s macarons are about 3 times larger than a regular macaron, but they cost around $3 each. However, if you buy 5, you get one free. They have the perfect texture: a thin, crunchy outer layer covering a perfectly chewy center. The filling is just right, but it’s the filling that prevents them from getting 5 stars instead of 4. They’re good, but their sweet butter filling, even in the cranberry flavor, isn’t very appealing. I prefer a fruit-filled filling with a slight acidity. Overall, they’re delicious and I would recommend them. If you also prefer a fruit-filled filling with acidity, I suggest visiting La Belle Terre bakery in W. Sahara.

state: Bouchon bakery is conveniently located in the Venetian near a public dining area. I was craving breakfast pastries and decided to try my luck here. I read a lot of good reviews and was prepared to wait in line if need be. To my pleasant surprise, there wasn't much of a wait! I got the chocolate almond crossaint, which I loved! The crossaint itself was made to perfection as it was extra flaky... so delicious. I also got the ham, egg, and cheese crossaint. Again, so very flaky... yummy. The only con for the ham, egg and cheese crossaint is that it is too salty. Takeaway: -A bit on the pricier side, but it's Vegas! -very good crossaint texture -convenient

Additionally, they offer slices and quarts of ice cream to be taken home and enjoyed on the sofa. They also provide water at the counter for customers to use, which is great… Mitchell’s makes me return here over and over again, at least once a week.

state: My sister found this place on Yelp, and it seemed like an amazing place to visit. She was right! They welcomed us upon entering, as well as anyone else who came in. And believe me, the place filled up quickly, even though when we arrived, there were just a couple of people before us! Now I understand why. They have countless flavor options and combinations, and I really liked it. Also, they had a wide variety of cereals to mix with, which was incredible! In the end, I ordered a combination with vanilla ice cream as the base, and my choice was Lucky Charms—they mixed those into the ice cream! I also asked for an extra topping and chose “marshmallows,” and it was delicious! My sister ordered some kind of milk tea with matcha and boba. Definitely, it’s the best ice cream place I’ve tried so far. Without a doubt, it’s a place worth visiting if you're in the mood for ice cream or drinks.

state: I’m a big fan of “Cake Boss” and Buddy Velasco. So when I heard there was a branch of Carlos Bakery in Las Vegas, I had to go! Carlos Bakery is located at the Venetian hotel. It’s at the far northern end of the shopping area. The line wasn’t very long when I arrived that night. Everything looked delicious! Many people were ordering cakes, but I wanted to try the cannoli and “lobster tails”… those are the things I always see on his show. Wow, the cannoli were really good… A cannoli can be shared between two people, since it’s quite large. The “lobster tails” were even more amazing than the cannoli. They were crispy on the outside and tasty inside. Hmm, delicious! One day, I really hope to try his cakes. The prices were a bit high for everything. I bought 6 cannoli and 3 “lobster tails” for about $45… but I got a mug as a gift! :)

state: This place has everything delicious and decadent you can imagine. From chocolate candies to smoothies, and all kinds of chocolate treats. Just entering and seeing what they have is a pleasure in itself. My favorite treat is the “turtles” – chocolate candies shaped like turtles. They’re absolutely delicious. Other fun items they offer include black chocolate and milk “s’mores” (Graham cookies covered with marshmallow and chocolate), bacon covered in chocolate, and various other fancy treats. They’re located on the street behind my office, and it’s very hard not to go there every day to buy something. The staff are very friendly, and the prices are quite reasonable. A generous portion usually costs around $2.50. They calculate prices by weight, so the larger the item, the more expensive it will be. If you’re eating at Penn or in the city center, make sure to stop by here for dessert. In fact, I think I’ll go there after lunch today to buy a almond “turtle”.

state: It seems that my reputation for consuming a lot of sugar hasn’t preceded me to Amelie’s yet. When they said, “Wow, someone needs to go around more times!” I appreciate the “sugariness,” but it’s been a long time since I was here last, and I must admit that my eyes were bigger than my stomach… But shouldn’t that have made you happy with the great offer, rather than making me feel guilty for buying so much? Besides, I’m someone who prefers things that are fresh and new, so this lasted for days… But the most important lesson I learned is that I should read through my own reviews again—I let myself be tempted by sweets that seemed delicious, but actually weren’t that good… Then I realized I had already tried those sweets, so I’ll keep that in mind next time. Well, the lesson is learned! The downside of this visit was: Salted caramel brownies – the brownie layer remains very thin and gritty due to the sugar – it didn’t fully dissolve during baking, and combined with the soft caramel layer, the result was gritty and greasy – definitely something I’ll avoid next time. Peach tart – I’m looking forward to the peach season, but I didn’t read my note about the minimal peach flavor, and my initial assessment was still correct: there was plenty of lemon, but very little peach. Chocolate cake with salted caramel – this was a new temptation for me, and it was fantastic! Take a cookie brownie with chunks of chocolate (or a Toll House cookie, if you like), add a layer of whipped cream in the middle, then add a small layer of salted caramel on top, and you get a really delicious tart. Cream cheese muffin – the dough part was pleasant, crunchy, and easy to break apart. It would have been better with more cream cheese. Double-baked croissant – only one remained when I arrived, and the croissant wasn’t crunchy or easy to break apart at all – it was too soaked with the liquid used before the second baking, so it had flavor, but it wasn’t really almond or croissant-like. So, for those less fortunate day-old desserts (my stupid choices) and sarcastic comments, this experience was simply perfect.

state: Incredible!! If you hadn’t come to this small place of just 60 square meters—a real dreamland, creamy and perfect… stop what you’re doing, save what you’re eating, and go to Novel as soon as possible! I really appreciate you sharing the best ice cream experience there. Here’s the info: it took the owner two years to find the perfect ice cream machine, and another year to perfect their donuts. So, in short: the perfect donut is filled with perfect ice cream. There are 12 flavors of ice cream, along with a wide variety of toppings and cereals to complement your ice cream. I tried all the flavors before deciding which, in my opinion, is the best combination in the world: strawberry ice cream with balsamic vinegar, and a honey-lavender donut. I swear, it’s the best! My son ate a donut filled with “Cookie Monster,” and my husband ate one filled with “bourbon toffee” with “cinnamon crunch” cereals. It might sound too sweet, but actually, it isn’t. It’s perfectly balanced, and makes you want more. It’s magic, right? The owner and staff were exceptional, offering incredible service and products. I’m grateful while writing this review! See you tomorrow!

state: I always buy from Buchon Bakery when I’m in Las Vegas! During my last visit, we stayed at The Venetian, so it was perfect to pick up some things to take with us when we left! This store is located close to the elevators for guests, on the first floor. Since I don’t have the chance to visit Las Vegas frequently, I always buy the same things: Kouign Amann, macarons, and almond croissants. This time, I also bought a ham and cheese croissant for my husband, but I regret not buying more French macarons too. I think we learn from our experiences! Hahaha My husband was impressed with the ham and cheese croissant, which I asked to warm up first. He said the egg was soft, and the croissant was crispy—simply delicious. The macaron was soft and creamy, and I wish I could have eaten it alone. Honestly, I think their macarons are even better than those I ate at LaDuree in France! There aren’t any bad cakes here, and I also had a delicious latte. However, I would like to mention that during my last visit, there was only one line to order. And when I went to order a sandwich for breakfast, the staff looked at me disapprovingly and rolled their eyes because I took some time. So, I gave it one star.

state: A pleasant spring afternoon took us to Little Italy last Saturday. After walking through the streets of Mayfield and Murray Hill, we stopped at Presti’s, a charming Italian bakery/café, to have lunch. They serve pizza, stromboli, antipasti, Italian wedding soup, panetone, gelato, tiramisu, macarons, cookies, cannoli, cassata cake, espresso, cappuccino, and much more. This place has it all. I ordered a slice of pizza with sausage and bell peppers. The sausage wasn’t cut into small pieces or arranged neatly. It was just a slice of pizza covered with red and green bell peppers. Eating it meant bending the pizza like a hot dog bun and eating everything up quickly. The idea was simply great. They also have an outdoor dining area right in front of the café, with a view of Mayfield Road. It’s a great place to observe people.

state: It’s rare to find ice creams better than those at Mitchell’s. The place is charming—an old theater. The sign outside announces the seasonal flavors. At Mitchell’s, you’re always allowed to try all the ice creams you’re interested in. My favorites are the “key lime pie” ice cream, the coconut chocolate ice cream, and the “porter” chocolate ice cream. If you buy a tin or a gallon for takeaway, they also include free ice creams. You can enjoy your dessert on the second floor, with a view of the kitchen, where chefs work constantly to prepare ice creams. Moreover, their hours are excellent. They’re open late, so you can stop after dinner, at a bar or at a concert. Mitchell’s is a place everyone should visit when they’re in Cleveland!

state: It’s great to have a ice cream shop with locally made ice creams! I haven’t eaten ice creams made here since I lived in our small university town in California. After doing some shopping at the vintage stores around Roosevelt Row and sweating a lot, my friend and I stopped by Melt. We tried several flavors of ice creams and sorbets, including chips and salsa (with Tapatio on top). The cucumber ice cream was really refreshing. But in the end, I got a small portion of peanut butter ice cream. My friend also tried Mexican hot chocolate and said it was very spicy. Mmmmm, mmmmm, mmmmm, creamy! It was simply wonderful. The ice cream, produced by Superstition Farms, is incredibly creamy, smooth, and perfectly sweet—without being overdone. All the flavors I tried were very natural, which is a big plus. You really should love your ice cream tubs, which come in Chinese “take-out” boxes with a lucky cookie on top. Even better, if you don’t like your lucky cookie, they have a full bottle for you to exchange. Ha! We saw your snack cookies in the window when we left, and we were very curious. But we asked the girl who worked there that day (she was a bit strange and didn’t listen very well) what they had, but she couldn’t tell us. Ummmmm, okay? The cookie was huge and seemed to be some kind of mixture of peanut butter, oats, potato chips, and pretzels. I wish I could have taken one to try. Maybe next time! My friend and I had a great time sitting in their spacious outdoor area. It was a pleasant and peaceful Sunday, and Roosevelt Row is a great place to relax and enjoy.

state: Sloan’s offers a solid variety of ice cream flavors, so it’s definitely worth visiting if you’re looking for something different. We ordered the cookie with chocolate and coffee with biscuit flavor – note, you need to order two scoops (we tried asking for just one, but they’re generous). The main downside is that the ice cream didn’t seem very fresh or natural, as advertised. My ice cream had pieces of ice, and the texture was like frozen ice cream that stays in the freezer for a long time. Maybe it’s because we went there near midnight, on Thursday, right before closing time, but still, it’s disappointing. It’s not a bad place to eat ice cream late at night, if you’re feeling hungry while at the Venetian/Palazzo casinos!

state: I just discovered this delicious place!! I was lucky to find it, as Dairy Queen was closed, and I really wanted to eat ice cream. I had no idea what would be available next, and it was a surprise! I was especially surprised to learn that they offer red bean taiyaki – a kind of fish-shaped waffle filled with your choice of filling. The fillings include cream, taro, red beans, and more! Red bean taiyaki was one of my favorite dishes when I lived in Japan, and I never found anything similar in the US until now. I also tried AH-BOONG, which is a fish-shaped waffle with cream and ice cream, filled with your preferred filling. I chose cream, and I was very happy with my choice! Both items were simply delicious! I can’t stop thinking about them just by writing this review, so I think I need to go back and try more!!!

state: Where should I start talking about Sweet Republic? It was also one of the first places I discovered when I moved to this area, thanks to a brochure I received at an event. It’s a bit far from me, but it’s always worth it. First of all, the ice cream and sorbets are incredibly delicious. There’s no words that can describe the quality of Sweet Republic in a review. However, I’d like to mention a friend who tried the ice cream for the first time during a “First Saturday” event recently. After trying several flavors, he looked at me and said, “Now I understand why you travel so much just to get here. This is the best ice cream I’ve ever tasted.” The atmosphere there is very fun and pleasant. They have outdoor and indoor tables, games to play (including the connection game), and free Wi-Fi. The decor with mint and orange cream gives a very refreshing and comforting feeling. However, one of the things I like most about Sweet Republic is the opportunity to try new things. I recommend that everyone try some different flavors before deciding what to buy. Also, try something you never thought of trying. You’ll be surprised, because not only will it have the flavor you imagined, but it will also be delicious! The owners spend a lot of time and effort preparing the ice cream, and I love trying out new flavors and hearing their stories about how sometimes they think the idea is crazy, but in the end it turns out to be fantastic. Sweet Republic is definitely worth the trip, no matter where you live in the area. I don’t know anyone who has been there and been disappointed.

state: After visiting this place several times and wondering what a “bakery consortium” meant, we finally went in and discovered a beautiful café and bakery. The space is decorated like a traditional tea room from the era, with glass display cases for cakes, iron-finished chairs and tables, and eye-catching wallpaper. What my husband described as a “hipster interpretation of 20th-century jazz music” could be heard in the background. There’s a impressive variety of desserts on display, including vegan options—Unfortunately, there were no gluten-free options that day. The barista was excellent and took great care in preparing my American coffee and my husband’s pour-over coffee; the results were delicious. If you plan to visit quickly, don’t miss out on this cozy place for chatting and enjoying a dessert. I recommend improving the signage, as at first we weren’t sure if we could enter. But yes, go ahead and enjoy a pleasant afternoon drinking coffee and eating something!

We talked with Austin while placing our order and he gave us a few great suggestions. I liked the Nutella filled cookie, Pistachio Biscotti, butter cookies, Cannoli, and the Boston Cream. The Cannoli sweet, with chocolate chips, a great filling and a fresh crunch. I hate soggy ones, so this made my day. We waited to pay as he wrapped our purchases in boxes and even tied them shut with a string. It wasn't a speedy transaction and it can be a little pricey for some (I got a lot of stuff for $26.00), but it's Vegas. Live a little. For great Italian baked goods, service and attitude, this is the place!

state: When I arrived at the Donut Bar, the sign in the window announced that they had the best donuts in the world. Well, I must say they might be right. Since this was my first visit, I wanted to try out various options. I ordered the “French toast” donut—it was delicious and big enough for us both to share. We also ordered the “strawberry shortcake” donut; it was very good too. The “bacon maple” and “bacon cinnamon roll” donuts were also great, combining the salty flavor of bacon with the sweetness of the donut. The staff, including chef Jeff, were very kind and attentive. I definitely will come back when I visit Las Vegas again.

state: I just recently found out about Butterwood Bake Consortium and had to check it! It's essential a cake shop. The interior is rich and inviting. I love the red velvet chairs and benches. It's a pretty small space but it feels very comfortable. I almost overwhelmed by the amount of sweets options in the display case. I was also surprised to see multiple vegan options. After looking at all my options I decided to try the lemon poppy seed cake with a black berry buttercream and a hot chocolate. My two friends and I sat down and waited for desserts. The staff person was friendly and quickly brought out our cakes and drinks. The hot chocolate was a tea cup filled half way with melted chocolate that you poured cream into. It was delicious and rich! Definitely would recommend it to anyone who goes. The cake on the other hand was just okay. It was just a little to dense for liking but still a quality cake. I can't wait to go back and try more of their wonderful selections!

state: Graham Central Station - enough said. Homemade daily, quality ice cream with the BEST mix-ins. I can't even tell you what's in Graham Central except that it is by far the best one we've tried. I'm not a graham cracker lover either. It's seriously just the best - try it. Not that any of the others are not good- they're all INCREDIBLE. It's only that I dream of Graham Central and try to find ways to "reward" my children (myself) by bringing them here. There's also $2 Tuesday where you'll get a GIGANTIC scoop of ice cream (when they say single scoop, it's pretty much the size of a double or triple) for $2. Lastly, we once ran into Dan Reynolds (lead singer of Imagine Dragons) here and I really really wanted my kids to say hi (ID is their favorite band and they know every song off of both CDs) but were too shy. So, next time you're in the mood for ice cream - come here, get a Hot Fudge Sundae with Graham Central & nuts. You're welcome!

state: It would have been great if 85 Degree Bakery had opened in Las Vegas decades ago, around 2009. But since they waited too long, during all my trips to California and back to my country, my enthusiasm for this bakery disappeared before it even opened in Las Vegas. Finally, today I got the chance to enter it for the first time. Why? Because whenever it opened, there was always a very long line, and I didn’t want to waste time waiting. So today, seeing that there was no line, I decided to go in and see how it was. First of all, they didn’t even have the most popular and common bread, “Buttermilk Boroh Bun”. I couldn’t find it, so I decided to ask someone who worked there—I think her name was Jasmine. Here’s what our conversation was like: “Excuse me, but do you have…?” Before I could finish my sentence, she said, “I’m sorry, but the bread will be available soon.” Wow! Does she read my mind or something? Other than that, that wasn’t what I wanted to ask. I just wanted to know if they had “Buttermilk Bun”. However, I must admit that she apologized, but wow! We give them two months, and this is the level of customer service they offer? Just ignoring customers with generic responses? Anyway, to my surprise, they don’t even know what “Buttermilk Bun” is (they should know, since it’s a Asian bread!). And by the way, it’s not a pineapple bread (a stupid name they used at JJ Bakery!). The correct translation is “Buttermilk Bun”. For me, that’s enough. The customer service has completely disappointed me. I’m glad I spent only 5 minutes there.

state: I read about this place on The Pioneer Woman blog, and when Peter and I planned a visit to Ikea we decided to make a stop. We split a Croque Monsier. It was tasty, but next time we come here (the will be a next time for sure!) I'd probably try something else, or skip lunch altogether and just pick up some dessert. We got quite a selection of baked goods, and would order most again. We had some macarons and a salted caramel brownie at the actual restaurant. We both loved the pistachio, but the orange and lemon tasted a little bit like Fruit Loops and seemed stale compared to the pistachio. We took home a box full of goodies (another brownie, an eclair, a chocolate croissant, two more macarons, and a petit four) that we ate over the next couple of days. All were delicious. Peter said the eclair was exactly what an eclair should be. My favorite was the salted caramel brownie, it was heaven. I am a sucker for anything salty, especially sweet and salty, so this is no surprise. It was totally worth a stop, but I wouldn't make a special trip to Charlotte just to eat here.

state: We arrived right when they opened on Saturday, as we were expecting freshly made donuts. The staff were friendly and helped us decide what to buy. We chose a Boston cream donut, a raspberry “pop-tart” donut, a cinnamon roll with maple bacon, an Oreo cake donut, a cheese sandwich donut, a “creme brûlée” donut (donuts with caramelized topping), and a Nutella donut. The Boston cream donut was average—nothing special, but it was still good and had a proper amount of cream. The raspberry “pop-tart” donut was interesting, but not particularly outstanding. The cinnamon roll was slightly burnt, but the center was good. The Oreo cake donut was fine, as long as you got a full piece of Oreo. The cheese sandwich donut was huge and overall quite good. It came with a Sriracha sauce to dip in. I forgot to take a photo. The “creme brûlée” donut was disappointing—it just tasted like a regular donut with filling. The Nutella donut was okay, but I didn’t notice much of a Nutella flavor. I gave this place 2 stars because I expected much more given its good rating, but overall, it was disappointing. Maybe I just aren’t one of those people who eat donuts.

state: Okay, to start, this place has an amazing smell! (At least that’s what I imagine the paradise should smell like.) The line for the sweets was quite long. I waited about 20 minutes before my turn came, but it was worth it. There are so many options for sweets, but I chose a traditional cannoli, a chocolate cannoli, a white chocolate mousse cake, and a almond cream candy. I really wanted a black and white biscuit, but unfortunately they were out of stock. Everything I ordered was delicious! My favorite was the white chocolate mousse. At $9.95, I was a bit skeptical whether it was worth it, but I would love to pay again. Maybe I ate everything by myself… I don’t regret it. The cannoli were great. They had a homey flavor, just as they should be. I preferred the traditional cannoli over the chocolate one. I recommend letting them sit at room temperature for about 10 minutes before eating, because when they’re right out of the fridge, it’s a bit hard to bite into. They were much better after thawing :) It’s good that I don’t live near Carlo’s; otherwise, I would be super fat (but I would be happy!).

state: Donuts are the perfect dessert for morning time. Yesterday was the perfect day to visit Donut Bar. This donut shop is located right next to Fremont Street, and it’s fantastic from the moment you enter. As soon as you walk in through the main door, friendly staff greet you, and there’s a wide variety of donuts—probably the most beautiful ones you’ve ever seen. They have a great selection; when I arrived around 7:30 in the morning, there were about 20 or 30 different varieties. In the end, I tried three types: the large birthday cake-shaped donut, the small birthday cake-shaped donut, and Oreo with an Oreo piece in the middle. The third donut was similar to a “Rocky Road” donut (I think so, please forgive me). From the first bite of the “Rocky Road” donut, I knew I had found my new favorite donut shop—there’s no comparison. Then I tried the birthday cake-filled donut—it was delicious. The dough here is super soft, and the Oreo cookie inside makes it a truly special donut. The last donut I ate (literally 10 minutes ago) was the large birthday cake-shaped donut. It wasn’t just big and soft, but the ingredients and cream made it the best birthday cake-shaped donut I’ve ever tasted. Overall, Donut Bar is definitely my new favorite donut shop. The staff are incredibly friendly and helpful, the place itself is great—with an aquarium decorated with donuts, and the donuts themselves are of top quality and absolutely delicious. If you like donuts, this is the perfect place for you.

state: No wonder this place made one of the top 10 ice cream places in the country! It's a little taste of Heaven!!! I got the Campfire S'more sundae with the Madagascar vanilla and chocolate scoops. I'll admit that I got it just to see the marshmellow on top get slightly toasted with the dessert torch. It felt and tasted like eating a creme brulee marshmellow on top of a giant ice cream s'more. My husband got the Peanut Butter Brittle sundae, which was also nothing less than perfect! It was hilarious because there were two visitors from Atlanta in front of us in line, who has just come straight from the airport to Sweet Republic because they had to try this ice cream!! I guess that show "The Best Thing I Ever Ate" truly does help recognize this unique ice cream shop and the ice cream speaks for itself. I really wanted my husband to try the jalepeno avocado bacon brittle ice cream, but unfortunately this flavor was unavailable on Friday, so I'll try to check and see if it's there the next time we return. On the up side, we were able to purchase a bag of bacon brittle to take home with us. Of course, we didn't wait until we got home to try it. We broke off pieces of the bacon brittle and stuck them in our sundaes. Un-freaking-believable!!! Man! I love this place!

state: During a recent trip, a friend suggested I go in and try the donuts, and ask for their opinion… well, neither of the donuts I tried impressed me at all… First, the size of the donuts surprised me—they were huge. Almost too big… I don’t know if they can really be called donuts… “Doughnut Planet” in New York has large donuts, but these were even bigger. The variety was interesting, but the two donuts I chose had no flavor. “Vanilla bean” and “Boston creme”… both cookies had no flavor, but the filling in “Boston creme” was delicious. The store is quite pleasant, and the people are friendly, but please, “Donut Bar,” invest in paper bags for the donuts. Leaving the store with two donuts in a box seems like a great waste, and it’s not what the world needs.

state: I was very excited to visit after seeing so many photos of Jeni’s ice cream on social media. The ice cream shop itself is very charming and modern. I love the elegant design of the outdoor tables and the well-lit signage that make it stand out! Additionally, it’s conveniently located near the train line and around many restaurants, making it a great place for desserts. When I entered for the first time, I was immediately overwhelmed by the delicious aroma of freshly made ice creams and desserts. I would like to capture that aroma and turn it into a candle that I can light every day at home. The staff were very helpful and knowledgeable about all the flavors! They allowed us to try a few options before we chose one. In the end, I chose Bumbleberry Crisp and Salted Peanut Butter in waffle flavor. It was really delicious, and even though those two flavors might not go together, with any Jeni’s ice cream, you can’t go wrong. You can also buy a package to take home and enjoy throughout the week!

state: Ah, Sloan’s. Their cute plush animals and fun decorations were enough to attract me, but the ice cream, though delicious, is incredibly expensive. A portion of two flavors (as shown in the photo) contains the smallest flavors possible, and it cost me almost 9 dollars. This not only left me disappointed, but I also felt hungry! If I go back someday, it will be to hug a giant Squishable. Even if Sloan’s had the most unique and fascinating flavor selection I’ve ever seen, I simply couldn’t justify paying so much for such small portions. The other desserts on display seem more interesting, but I’m not sure about their prices—maybe they cost 20 dollars per donut! However, if you’re looking for fun decorations for the kitchen or soft toys for kids, it might be worth a look. The choice is up to you, but be careful.

state: oooooooooh man am I SO GLAD this place isn't near my house, I would gain 20 pounds in no time! My sister took me here for the first time a couple weeks ago and my mind was blown by all the unique flavors they served! The shop itself is very cute and modern. I like that they have a section in the back with a bunch of board games, very cool. As for the ice cream I got the dutch chocolate and the horchata. The horchata was so so good, I cant stop thinking about it! The following week I took the husband there. Again the ice cream was very good but the service was terrible. It was an older lady behind the counter and she really couldn't care less that we were standing there. She let me sample an ice cream and then I just stood there for a good 5 minutes while she did other things behind the counter. We did finally get served but my husband wasn't impressed with the serves one bit. This time I got my ice cream in a waffle cone, the cone was so light and airy, I loved it!

state: We came here for a sweet bite after eating across the street at Federal Pizza. The line was out the door, but no one seemed to mind waiting. I was too busy looking at all the retro candy from my childhood, so when I got to the front of the line...I had no clue what I wanted and didn't want to hold the line up. So, one of the gals suggested the Peanut Butter ice cream (score!) and the pretzel cone I had already planned to try...because...it's a pretzel and a cone! I loved the creamy natural tasting peanut butter ice cream, but the cone was a bit of a let down. It was a tad too salty and not light and airy like a regular pretzel. It was thick and on the crunchy side. So, I think I'll skip it the next time I go in. We enjoyed sitting out back though! Make sure you make your way back there instead of sitting out front where the line is a bit in the way.

state: Whether you like the Parisian atmosphere or not… I know they’re selling it… But I’m not sure if I really believe it. The front fence is pretty nice, until you look beyond it and see the reality: it’s just a fence in a wire fence at a parking lot in Charlotte. There’s a wide variety of cakes and desserts. If you can’t find something you like, it’s simply because you haven’t tried enough. The furniture is a bit strange, especially when trying to seat a group of people. state: Everything from Mason’s is delicious, and it’s unusual to visit without trying something you never thought could be as tasty as ice cream—think about the flavor of Froot Loops or whiskey nogotine. It’s not a place where you can just order chocolate or vanilla, though there’s always a similar option to the standard products for those who refuse to challenge their taste buds. And the best part? They prepare everything from scratch, right there, even upon request. If you really love a flavor and don’t mind buying in large quantities, you can order it at any time of year, and in a few days, they’ll prepare a batch just for you to take home and enjoy. So far, I haven’t taken advantage of this option because I was afraid of bringing it home, closing the door, and eating it all at once. I’ve been a fan of Mason’s since those kind-hearted owners started their shop at the Cleveland flea market. Jesse and Helen are what I would call a calm and efficient couple. After enjoying their atmosphere for a year, I can say I have a strong preference, but I can also assure you that, despite my enthusiasm, they haven’t disappointed me yet.

state: I went there for the first time today. I told one of the employees that I was new. She seemed annoyed at having to explain what kind of donut each one was. Maybe if they had labels or descriptions, it would help reduce the hassle of people asking what each donut was. The donuts were okay, but honestly, they didn’t impress me much. My husband and I tried the glaze options: Samoa, maple, peanut butter, and Lucky Charms. Maybe they were freshly made, but I’m not sure. Especially the Lucky Charms one—it seemed like it had been there for a while. The dough of the donut is thick and more like a cake. I expected the glazed ones to be similar to Krispie Kreme, but the flavors are completely different. They’re not light or fluffy at all. Overall, they’re good donuts; the concept is interesting, but I feel that advertising makes them seem better than they really are.

state: So today was my first time going to Mason’s, so I can only talk about their ice cream. But as for the ice cream itself, it was fantastic! We arrived right when they were opening, and thank goodness we did, because it was already full when we got there (it’s really popular). We just had to wait a few minutes, and then we could place our order at the window. Additionally, they follow COVID protocols well: there are marked areas on the floor where people need to wait, and masks are required. I ordered matcha and Oreo ice cream in a waffle, with almond-flavored whipping cream (I’m not sure exactly what flavor it was), and it was delicious. My roommate ordered lemon and ricotta flavors, and he also enjoyed it very much. A bonus: the spoons change color. It’s not something very important, but it’s a lovely detail that shows their attention to detail and their love for fun things. Overall, both I and my roommate really enjoyed the ice cream and the experience, and we definitely will go back soon.

state: I had high expectations—perhaps too high. I was very excited when I heard that Sprinkles would open in Las Vegas. I tried to go to the one in Los Angeles, but there was a long line, and we didn’t have much time. There was also a line outside this place, but we (along with other people waiting) didn’t realize it was only for ice cream. We just wanted cupcakes. The “doorman” didn’t help solve this problem either. Once inside, the people working behind the counter were talking very loudly (there were about 4 or 5 of them), so the person who took my order didn’t hear me. After all that, the cupcakes themselves weren’t very good. For $3.75 each, I expected something better. 4 stars for presentation, 3 stars for taste, and 1 star for service.

state: A fantastic ice cream that offers everything you could wish for in a ice cream shop. They have excellent ice creams, waffle cones, ice cream desserts, and delicious smoothies. You can choose something simple like vanilla, or more interesting options like matcha or salted caramel ice cream. In addition, they make wonderful ice creams too. The watermelon ice cream was incredible—I ordered it alongside the dessert I bought! The staff are also very friendly, and they allow you to try many samples using their cold metal spoons. In the end, I ordered a banana pancake dessert, which is a mix of bananas and caramel with salted caramel ice cream as the base. I would recommend ordering a second dessert, as mixing all the ingredients can be a bit messy. But hey, it was delicious! Everything was very satisfying and perfect as a dessert. The waffle cone bowls make it even better. Although I’m not really a fan of orange wallpaper, the interior design isn’t important. What matters is the ice cream—so don’t miss out on this ice cream shop!

state: On the second floor of Cosmopolitan, there’s the Milk Bar, owned by Christina Tosi. It’s a sister bakery to the Momofuku restaurant owned by David Chang. Tosi used to work as a baker for David Chang. Her specialty was turning baked cornflakes soaked in milk into the base for ice creams, panna cotta, and ice cream desserts. In 2008, she opened her first Milk Bar in New York. Now, there’s a branch here in Las Vegas! We looked at the menu and really didn’t know what to order. So, the kind young man behind the counter offered us samples. First, we tried Crack Pie, and then the milk ice cream with cereal. It was amazing! We decided to order a portion of Crack Pie to take home, a glass of milk ice cream with cereal, covered with Crack Pie, for sharing, and a glass of individual ice cream with a cornflake texture. The milk ice cream with cereal flavor tasted exactly like the milk in your cereal bowl, but frozen. Very interesting! It was light and airy, not too sweet. I liked it. But adding the individual portions of Crack Pie made the dessert a little too abundant. The “pint” size glass for two people turned out to be a generous portion, and we couldn’t finish it. A half-price individual glass would have been perfect. On the other hand, the portions of cornflakes in the individual glass were a lighter dessert with a pleasant crumbly texture. I might order that next time. Crack Pie itself is very rich. It’s a cold portion of whipped cream, made with butter and dark sugar, on top of toasted oats. It’s like a mix between baklava and granola bars. Very substantial, but also satisfying in just a few bites. Probably better served with a cup of coffee. There’s so much more to try, and I’m sure I’ll come back with friends and family to share! Cookies, cakes, breads, smoothies, sophisticated smoothies: plenty of sweetness there!

I was a little put off by the fact that it was $8.00, but let me tell you, it was worth every penny. I got Captain Crunch ice cream (yes, you read that right). It tasted like the milk at the end of the bowl, and had some chewy Captain Crunch pieces throughout. The girl behind the counter let me sample it first, so if you're skeptical, give it a try! THEN, I sandwiched it between two salted caramel oatmeal cornflake cookies. You can't see the second cookie, but it's under there somewhere. I can't even begin to explain how amazing this was. You could definitely split it with another person, but why would you want to!

state: I woke up this morning... 7 AM... because I was going to go try The Donut Bar. There was so much hype about this place from USA today to the food network to Ellen. I was energized and ready to go! I got there at 7:50 in the morning and it was easy to find parking. There was already a line of at least 40 people ahead of me who were also waiting for a shop that was about to open at 8 AM. The wait time to get in once the shop opens at 8 AM was 30 minutes in line outside. Luckily, it was a pleasant day. As I approached the inside of the store, I was surprised to see that I wasn't all that excited. I saw many very large looking donuts with hard tacky frosting that weren't at all appealing. The oversized amount made them less appealing rather than to appear yummy. The smaller donuts looked good and, by smaller, I mean normal size like Dunkin' Donuts regular donuts. The service was just OK. Whoever chose to run this place really doesn't seem to understand what the best environment for customer service is. It was glaring super loud music over the speakers where I could barely hear the person helping me and I'm not sure if they could hear me. I had to order several donuts for a party and thought this is a good place to try because it gets so much publicity so it has to be good. I decided to put my instincts aside because so many people were waiting in front of me and behind me to get into this place and it has gotten all these reviews. As I ordered, after two dozen donuts, the server just went off to help somebody else without even asking me if I was finished with my order. I couldn't believe it! I was very friendly during the whole interaction which is why this shocked me. I did not bother calling her back because I am not confrontational and simply will let something like this go, but won't let it go during a review. The donuts range from two dollars that are very small to some pastries that are upwards of four dollars. I ordered several donuts including the Twix, Samoa, blueberry with lemon, chai, Nutella, Red velvet, and the crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e. Here is what I have to say: firstly, you have to eat these donuts the day of because they are not as good the next day. With that being said, most of the donuts were not that impressive to begin with. They were just ok or disappointing. In fact, the crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e donut, which gets all of this amazing hype, was one of the worst ones of the bunch. The hard sugar/Caramel crust on top of the donut was so burnt that it carried a foul aftertaste. The donut itself had a yummy crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e center within the dough. The topping of the crunchy burnt sugar/Caramel ruined it. I also did not like that many of the donuts were grossly over sized with a great deal of tacky frosting on it which was glazed and dried off. I did order a couple of those and they were not very good. This place is OK. I did not try the coffee and I wonder if that would've changed my mind and increased their ratings. The donuts are so so. They aren't that much better than other places or don't cost a lot less so I do not know what people are talking about. Also, the wait time and price just isn't worth it. It is a very popular place and a lot of people come here. Not sure if there are people that love donuts so much that this is considered great quality??? I love food and have been very fortunate to taste some phenomenal food internationally at some of the best places. I know donuts and sadly, the donut bar does not have anywhere close to the best donuts around. The two stars are because it is expensive, the service was disappointing, the wait time to get the donuts was way too long for this,and the donuts did not impress. I am glad I tried it just take the hype away and I should have gone with my instincts.

state: A very spacious coffee shop in Urbana. I wish such a place existed during most of my undergraduate studies – unfortunately, I only discovered it when I was nearing the end of my graduate studies. The decor is fun, and many of the desserts are also delicious. There are huge cakes filled with fruits and big BingSu! The coffee shop has Korean origins, so it serves sushi and spicy tuna onigiri, as I understand. The coffee is good. My last visit was before the students returned to the campus, so the atmosphere was pleasant and relaxed. I think throughout the year, there probably isn’t much space to sit here, which would be inconvenient if I just wanted to have a coffee. There are signs on the doors saying “no food or drink allowed.” I feel this should be obvious, but clearly several customers didn’t follow this rule!

state:
We were getting ready to go to the airport, and we wanted to eat something at the hotel before leaving. It was close by, on the way to the airport, and we thought it would probably be better than any food you can find at an airport. Here are the dishes we tried:

Pork and Brie Sandwich: Brie, lettuce, grilled pork, and mustard. The bread had a ciabatta texture when heated and pressed, which was nice. The creamy texture of the brie became a bit sticky and liquid in the sandwich after heating, but I liked the aroma and texture of the melted brie in any form. However, I must admit it wasn’t exceptional—it was good, but the flavor wasn’t different from a sandwich I could have made myself.

Vegetable Gardener Sandwich: With portobello mushrooms, eggplant, fennel, caramelized onions, poblanos, fontina cheese, and pesto. My partner ordered this. Oh my! This is the sandwich I should have ordered from the start. It’s a vegetarian sandwich, but the juiciness of the mushrooms, the texture of the eggplant, along with the aromas and crunch of the fennel. Every bite was almost a unique and satisfying experience, with a mix of caramelized onions, gentle warmth, and the texture of the poblanos and melted fontina cheese, which sat nicely on the edge of the knife. The flavor and texture were rich, but they also kept the delicate nature of the sandwich intact. Really, my partner loved this sandwich so much that I couldn’t eat more. I even offered her a swap in our sandwiches, and she just smiled and continued eating. It was a fantastic sandwich, even for me, a huge fan of meat, who feel like it would be a sandwich I’d like to eat regularly.

Chocolate “Bouchons”: Their name comes from the fact that they’re shaped like wine bottle caps. They definitely taste much better than real caps. These small bites were rich and juicy, with tiny pieces of chocolate inside. It reminded me of a brownie—an excellent brownie!

Chocolate Eclair: This was my dessert. As someone who loves chocolate very much, when I saw it in the shop window, I didn’t have any chance. The choux dough was light and airy, with a soft and subtle sweetness. The chocolate cream was decadent and smooth, and there was a generous layer of more chocolate on top, creating a perfect balance with each delicious bite.

Lemon Tart: My partner’s choice. Honestly, once again, she exceeded my expectations! The lemon filling reminded me of a lemon curd; with all the shredded lemon, you could really taste the fresh lemon, with a wonderful balance of acidity and creamy texture. What’s most remarkable is the crust—instead of just a tart or Graham cracker crust, they used fresh pine nuts. The pine nuts created a wonderful aroma, a crunchy texture with nuts. Each bite of both elements, with their contrasting flavors and textures, combined to create an absolutely incredible dish. It’s an experience that should be tried, and I’d like to try it again next time.

Parisian Macarons: Esthetically, they were impressive. I bought some packages to take home as gifts. Although they were sold out at first, the staff was kind enough to go back and prepare the rest to complete our order. The presentation and colors were wonderful. They said each one had a different flavor (lemon, orange, strawberry, vanilla, mocha, and chocolate). Basically, we had a delay, and eventually, a canceled flight. So my partner and I might have tried one of the packages. You know, we wanted to try the gift we were going to give, and we wanted to make sure it was fresh, since our next flight was the next day. So we tried one package. Rich, chewy, and very dense, with a wonderful flavor enclosed in a thin layer of cream. If I had to describe it, it would be: vanilla, coffee, lemon, chocolate, strawberry, and orange. It goes well with a simple cup of coffee!

state: I have driven by this ice cream shop tons of times all year. I finally decided to go check it out on a chill sunday evening. I parked and saw a long lone so I figured that was a good sign it must be good. There is a ton of unique dun flavors of ice cream but I decided on just getting a single scoop cake cone ($4) & my guest got a hot fudge sundae w whipped cream n a cherry on top (bday cake & coolie dough ice cream). The single scoop was pretty big-I am not really a desert person and it was a lot for me. I want to try the "4 scoop sampler" next time (@&4.55). Friendly staff, and they all wore masks for covid safety measures. I will be back next time I have a sweet craving! Great flavored ice cream and big portions for the prices.

state: Incredible!!! I love the “Cake Boss” program, and I was very excited to learn about the bakery in Las Vegas. After reading the reviews here, at first I was a little hesitant, as it seemed like I might have a bad experience. But I’m very happy that I went. Initially, we went on Saturday night, and we waited just about 15 minutes—that’s the total waiting time. There wasn’t much variety, but it’s a small bakery, and I didn’t expect to find everything there. We ordered a mini half-sweet chocolate cake and a brownie. Oh my God, they were amazing! It was worth every penny. So, if you rely on reviews, I hope this helps—my experience was exactly what I wanted!

state: It’s an essential place in Madison. It’s a large store with few seats, but offers a wide variety of salty and sweet pastries. Their Gruyère-filled croissants are literally the best croissants in Wisconsin. Their garlic-and-cheese bread sticks are big, greasy, and I absolutely love them. My favorite quick-meal option is buying one of their large meat or bean-filled bread buns. The options change daily: sausage, mushrooms, and cheese; beans, pesto, and cheese; bacon, white beans, and Parmesan. All of them are incredible, though you’ll need two to be satisfied. I haven’t tried the desserts yet, but I can assure you they are also fantastic.

state: If the vegan experience is like this, why aren’t we all vegans! I keep hearing about TVDC, and today I passed by them and decided to stop by to buy some products. I found a new favorite place. The two dishes I tried were tiramisu and strawberry shortcake. Seriously, this place is incredible. Visit TVDC as soon as possible, because it’s a small local business owned by women and African Americans.
