state: My girlfriend and I went there a few weeks ago because the name was attractive, it was close by, and the photos were interesting. However, I quickly became worried when I ordered something very simple—a vanilla ice cream ball and a strawberry ice cream in a glass. The employee seemed unsure of how to proceed. They made the order much more complicated than necessary, and the result was so small that I think even a child would be disappointed. I didn’t say anything because it didn’t matter to me, and I asked them to prepare whatever my girlfriend wanted. She ordered one of the frozen ice creams from the menu. It had three ingredients, plus ice. The employee had to look at the menu several times; clearly, they had no idea what ingredients were used. Moreover, she said she could barely distinguish the flavors, and it cost five dollars for just a bowl of crushed ice. The prices are a bit high for what you get, and there wasn’t much flavor that interested or appealed to us. I felt bad for my friend, because she agreed to go there because online it said they offered frozen yogurt. Well, actually, they don’t offer frozen yogurt. She can’t eat frozen yogurt. I’ll say that the interior is visually pleasing, and it might be a small and unique place if they were more precise with their menu, knew what they offered, and had the ability to prepare the dishes they serve. I hope I have better luck next time.

state: Finally, The Milk Bar has arrived in Las Vegas, bringing all the excitement that comes with Christina Tosi, “Crack Pie,” birthday cakes, and cereal milk flavors. I was really excited; in fact, I even watched videos of desserts to lift my mood. But when it came time to go ahead, I felt both surprised and confused. The experience was disappointing—like Wile E. Coyote falling off a cliff while chasing Road Runner. The portions seemed small for the exorbitant prices charged for the products. $7 for a child-sized ice cream, and $6.50 for a small piece of “Crack Pie” – that’s ridiculous. I think both desserts were delicious, but not at that price. The worst part is that they were served in paper cups and cardboard boxes. For a moment, I thought I was at McDonald’s. I would have liked to try the birthday cake, but they only offered the whole cake. Also, there wasn’t enough space to sit. I saw some sofas in the area. It was very crowded; people were sitting down drinking cocktails, and I felt uncomfortable eating ice cream among them. I can’t imagine this being what Christina had in mind, as this experience doesn’t resemble the nostalgic feeling that ice cream usually gives. Thankfully, there are other options at Cosmopolitan that I actually enjoy.

state: If you're looking for ice cream, this is the right place! I have only three things to comment on: I give the ice cream a 5 stars rating, but 0 stars for the food. My favorite is the traditional ice cream in a cake cone, with “Scooter Crunch” topping. The ice cream is creamy and delicious, and the “Scooter Crunch” topping really enhances the experience. Classic! My husband ordered the sundae with chocolate cookies, which was delicious, but a bit too much for me. It consisted of vanilla ice cream, hot “Nancy B” chocolate cookies, and chocolate syrup. If you have dessert and a big appetite, I recommend it. During my last visit, I tried the “arctic swirl” blueberry cheesecake. If you’re not interested in the cheesecake part, just order the blueberry ice cream instead. It’s worth it. Ignore the food – my friend ordered fried potatoes, and they were raw. Don’t let the line get you down; it moves quickly.

state: Attention ice cream and donut lovers! Out in Phx. off of Grand Ave & 11th. ave. behind the Third Space green building. You gotta try this very tasty homemade ice cream and floats at Novel Ice cream! Fun and eclectic flavors to choose from! From Honey & Lavender, pistachio, cookie monster (blue), tangerine sherbet, and many other delicious mouthwatering flavors. Including chocolate, and strawberry. Even their award winning Madagascar vanilla! You can choose to have any flavor ice cream filled in a donut with or without cereal toppings. Or a waffle filled ice cream sandwich! An ice cream float with your choice of soda. Or just the simple ice cream scoop in a cup or a cone. Friendly employees and the prices are not so high. Plenty of space to sit out front and enjoy your tasty treat and the warm sunshine. Now off I go and burn off this ice cream.

state: I visited Churn after reading the reviews, and I wasn’t disappointed. I tried the version with two scoops: one with Vietnamese coffee, and the other with nut and butter flavor – both were delicious! I added whipped cream to enhance the taste… I also tried the chocolate with malted milk, which was tasty, but the nut and butter flavor impressed me more. The Vietnamese coffee was my favorite flavor, both for me and my husband. The only reason I didn’t give five stars is because when I checked the menu online, I saw that there were many amazing and diverse options, and I was very eager to try them. But in the store, there were only about 6 to 8 flavors to choose from – and no matter which flavor I tried, they were all excellent! Additionally, I thought that my husband and I wouldn’t be able to finish the two-scoop portion at once (which we did eventually), so I asked for a lid on the bowl. But they only had a bowl with a flat edge, not a dome-shaped one, which wasn’t ideal.

state: A great recommendation for ice cream I received! I had heard of Jeni’s before, but never had the chance to try it. I’m very happy I finally got to try it! They have a quite wide range of flavors, with at least one-third being unique and something I’ve never seen or heard of before. They offer options where you can basically try different flavors, which is great for sharing with friends and/or family. One option is the “trio” set, where you can choose up to 3 flavors according to your preference; another option is a “menu” with 10 of their most popular flavors (with possible substitutions). If you’re a big fan of ice cream and want to try almost all of their flavors, the 10-flavor menu is definitely worth it. When I went there, they had 13 flavors available… But with the menu, you can basically try all of them. My favorite flavors were probably lavender and walnut butter with whiskey. The lavender flavor wasn’t too strong, which I really appreciated. It was more subtle, and it complemented well with another flavor, almost citrusy, which made the tasting experience truly unique and wonderful. The walnut butter with whiskey flavor was exactly what it says on the label. The alcohol taste wasn’t overwhelming at all; it really enhanced the walnut butter flavor. The quality of the ice cream reminded me of handmade ice cream shops. You can definitely tell the difference between their ice cream and, say, ice cream bought from a store (though it’s a bit impious of me to compare them like that). They even describe their production standards on their napkins, which I think is very creative. If you haven’t tried them yet and are passing by, you definitely should make a stop to try their ice cream here.

state: I went on a trip from New York to Charlotte to visit friends. I’ve been coming here for some time now, and I was really excited to try it out. I was also very happy to see that the inventory was full! The atmosphere is very charming and welcoming. The dishes they serve are excellent. My friends and I bought some items to try. We tried banana bread with Nutella, cereal muffins, OCP, and brownies with marshmallows. The best part was the banana bread, though it was a bit too sweet. The latte I drank helped balance the taste. I hope they get a microwave or toaster. I thought some items would be better if they were warm. For example, the brownies with marshmallows would have been great if they were heated up. The texture of the cold marshmallows didn’t satisfy me much. OCP was my least favorite option. The biscuit itself wasn’t the best. The filling was too sweet and had a slightly sandy texture. Overall, it’s a very charming place with friendly staff.

state: Red velvet anything, french macarons, and toasted marshmallow are basically in my personal book for favorite desserts. So when I saw that this place has all 3 in one convenient cup I knew I had to have it. I got a bowl with passion fruit ice cream with purple rain (blueberry muffin), with a red velvet macaron topped with not one but two toasted marshmallows. The guy who scooped it said he had never stacked two toasted marshmallows before but I saw in his heart that he had potential to be a jenga world champion and he did not disappoint. Both the passion fruit and blueberry muffin ice cream were great but the perfect bite to me was a spoonful of the chewy macaron with some gooey marshmallow, and blueberry muffin ice cream, followed by the passion fruit for some contrast. It's amazing! Really great place with nice people and especially excellent sweets.

state: What a delicious ice cream! The texture is incredibly creamy, and the flavors are rich—covering both classic options and many creative flavors, such as orange blossom flavor (impressive!) and honey and Graham cracker flavor—all at excellent prices. The staff is patient and friendly. There’s plenty of space to sit outside; there are no seats inside, since it’s a large ice cream shop, but most seats are under a canopy. My only complaint is that, like in other places I’ve seen in Cleveland, it seems that only some flavors can be used to make smoothies (and I often forget to ask why). It’s a pity, as many of the other flavors would make great smoothies.

state: FYI, this is review is of their truck that was at First Friday... I would like to state that I am observing no-meat Fridays during this Lenten season. I managed to avoid meat at the other food trucks, but decided to break it for dessert. It was sinfully delicious........ Some of the flavors they had on hand were Belgian Chocolate, Mint Chip, Salted Butter Caramel, White Rose and I Heart Bacon. They also had a pomegranate sorbet. I think it was blueberry pomegranate. After reading reviews of Sweet Republic, I knew they were known for their gourmet flavors so my choices on Friday were between White Rose and I Heart Bacon. I'm not a big fan of rose flavor.. so I ordered a single scoop ($3) of bacon flavored ice cream. The initial bite was confusing. My mind knew I was eating ice cream, but didn't understand why there was a hint of smoked bacon with my dessert. It was an unusual flavor, but after about 3 bites it grew on you. In the ice cream were pieces of bacon and I think some maple flavored toffee. Those sugary, maple-y pieces were a really good accompaniment to the bacon. All in all, trying this bacon ice cream was worth the three dollars, plus a few Hail Marys.

state: I love Handel’s! I always go there with my friends. I’ve been here three times already, and the quality remains consistent. I really like the four-flavor sample because it’s affordable and allows me to try different options. The birthday cake flavor is delicious—it tastes exactly as it should. The cookies and cream have Oreos inside, and the flavors are clearly visible. My favorite is the sugar cotton candy, as it’s been recreated perfectly in a ice cream. The cheese cake with strawberries is also delicious, because there are small pieces of cheese cake inside!

state: I was very excited to finally try Milk Bar when I was in Las Vegas. I ordered the milk ice cream with cereal and cornflakes, as well as the milk ice cream with cereal and fruit. When I tasted it, my first impression was that it was too sweet. In fact, it took me a long time to finish it, and I’m someone who really likes sweet flavors. The cereal flavor was just like regular milk, and the fruit ice cream reminded me of Fruity Pebbles. Although it’s a bit more expensive, I recommend ordering the cornflake ice cream. The salty taste of the cornflakes contrasts nicely with the sweet ice cream. Even though the photos make it seem like a small ice cream, it’s easy to share with someone else, and it’s enough. This is a expensive place to buy ice cream, and my expectations weren’t met.

The bathroom has a theme inspired by “The Girls of the Cable” – what an original idea! I ordered a vanilla ice cream latte, but currently they only have caramel. The caramel was delicious. Fortunately, they also have oat milk. The owner allowed me to take some photos of the store so that all Yelp users can enjoy them. The parking space is small, but there’s parking on the street nearby. Today was its opening day. This Saturday will be its grand opening, and I can’t wait to see what they have prepared.

state: Delicious, creamy, with nuts and soft—that’s what my mother used to describe the maple and nut ice cream. “Creamy, salty, sweet, and soft” was how my husband described the caramel ice cream with salted butter. “Incredible!” would be how I describe the basil and lime sorbet. Fresh, light, sweet, with just the right amount of sweetness. I asked the woman behind the counter what the ingredients were, and she said: basil, lime, ice, and sugar. I ate it with a small spoon and enjoyed every bite. I know I’ll come back to Arizona during my next visit to see my mother, because I still can’t stop thinking about that sorbet. Congratulations, Sweet Republic! Congratulations on creating a solid approach, without additives or preservatives, based on “whole foods” for sweet desserts! Delicious!

state: Impressive! I’m very impressed by how delicious, fluffy, and easy to chew are their donuts. I bought the cake batter, raspberry cheesecake, Nutella, “Samoa” donuts, “Homer” donuts, and “red velvet” donuts. I arrived around 11 a.m. during opening hours, and there were several interesting options available. Unfortunately, the strawberry and Oreo donuts were sold out, but it doesn’t matter—what I bought was delicious! Compared to other donut shops in town, “Donut Bar” stands out for its huge donuts (4 dollars each), as well as unique options like Oreo inside the donut, “pop tart” inside the donut, and hopefully, donuts with ice cream soon (that’s what they announced on their Instagram). The batter is extremely easy to chew and moist; the ingredients are well-balanced and proportionate. And most importantly, the glaze isn’t too sweet. I definitely recommend this place—just come early to get more options!

state: After watching “Chef’s Table” and hearing about the Milk Bar, we decided to visit it during our stay in Las Vegas. Located at the Cosmopolitan, the Milk Bar is actually an outdoor kiosk with no tables. We chose the “favorites” package, which included a compound biscuit, milk cereal ice cream, a slice of “crack” cake, and a pack of three birthday truffles. I was disappointed to find that, aside from the ice cream, all the items were pre-packaged. The slice of “crack” cake was too small for the price, but it was delicious. The compound biscuit and milk cereal ice cream were just okay. However, I really liked the birthday truffles. Overall, it was a fun and indulgent menu, but I was disappointed that the items weren’t more fresh, considering the price.

state: After dinner at their restaurant, we walked down the hallway to this place. My husband and I were very eager to try the desserts at Buddy’s. There was some waiting time, but everyone was very organized and helpful, which made the experience pleasant. I gave this bakery three stars because the desserts weren’t as good as we expected. Additionally, the prices were too high. The cream pie was amazing! However, the cookies and the salted caramel cupcake we bought were quite bland. We don’t really like overly sweet desserts, but these had almost no flavor at all—a little sweetness would have been helpful. I really don’t like giving three stars, but to be honest, we won’t go back.

state: Delicious ice cream, friendly staff, and a charming local atmosphere. We really love Churn, and we’ve been eating ice cream more often than necessary lately! The staff are very helpful and pleasant, and trying out different flavors is actually encouraged—excellent! Peanut butter ice cream is amazing, and the available flavors change regularly. There are two things to keep in mind: 1. Parking. There are few parking spaces, and they’re reserved for valet service, which is a bit inconvenient considering the location and the level of the businesses (they’re not luxury establishments). 90% of my visits were by bike, so I didn’t notice the difficulty until recently. Park on the street or in the restricted parking area north. 2. No tables inside. I usually feel like eating ice cream when the weather’s nice, so it hasn’t been a problem for me… just a note:).

state: Okay… actually, there’s a 24-hour cupcake vending machine right in front of their building! Amazing! Who hasn’t had the urge to eat a cupcake at odd times? I just finished my breakfast after our first day in Las Vegas, and I saw the vending machine. My fiancé said we probably didn’t have room for a cupcake at that moment. So we continued on our way. But 5 hours later, on our way back, I couldn’t stop thinking about the cupcake vending machine. So we went back so I could make my first purchase. It was an amazing experience! I got a vanilla cupcake! A perfect vanilla cupcake! It was wonderful! When you’re in Las Vegas, you really need to try it out!

state: I arrived here after the bar/club at 3 a.m. I like it when it’s open 24 hours a day, but it’s a pity that there aren’t many options at night. I felt sad because we couldn’t order the crème brûlée. The macarons were good, and the salty caramel brownies were also good, but they were a little too sweet for me. The block of salty caramel brownies was excellent. I didn’t like the strawberry petit gateau, but it was okay. The coconut and macadamia coffee was fine, though. There were only two staff members, and the line was long. I will come back earlier and try other items on the menu. 19/08/2019: I came back here with my daughter. We ordered red fruit macarons, vanilla macarons, caramel cake, two crème brûlées, and coconut and macadamia coffee. The red fruit macarons can stain the tongue and teeth/lips for a while, but they’re delicious. The crème brûlée is okay, but it has a slightly eggy taste.

state: We arrived around 1:30 p.m. on a Sunday, and they were closing up. We wanted to get the last donuts left. We had two options: “buy one and take another” or a box for $10. The option of a box was much more convenient, so we ended up buying 16 donuts for $10!!! An incredible deal! Also, if you check Yelp, you can get a free American coffee or filter coffee. #win Blueberry Lemon – Pretty good, but I liked that it wasn’t as sweet as I thought. Strawberry Split – Regular. I wouldn’t order it again. The donut was just cinnamon flavor and was dry (probably because it had been outside all day), and the whipped cream inside was dry too, tasting like something from a can. The strawberries were also very basic; they would have been better if they were coated with frosting. Crème brûlée – My favorite among everything I tried. The crunchy frosting on top was great, and I love stuffed donuts. After eating half of it, the cream inside started to taste artificial, like cheap cake frosting, so I had to try it again. Buttermilk Bar – I really liked the texture of this one! Soft and similar to cake inside, and crunchy on the outside. The other donuts seem amazing, so I definitely will try other flavors again. I agree that I’ve tried better donuts elsewhere, but this place opened just 3 months ago, so maybe their quality will improve. The parking lot on the street was easy to find.

state: I love Sprinkles. I used to go to the store in Scottsdale, and I was very excited when I heard that one location was coming to Las Vegas. It’s at Linq, so it’s a bit inconvenient to have to go there unless you’re already nearby. We’ve already tried the product; these are my favorite cupcakes, but they also have Sprinkles ice cream. I haven’t tried them yet, so I can’t comment on that. Recently, we passed by during closing time and decided to try the Sprinkles ATM after a group of young people almost emptied the place. It’s an self-service machine where you choose your flavors. We chose “red velvet” and “white chocolate with milk.” We entered our order and waited for the cupcakes. The door opened, but there was nothing inside. I was sad… confused, so we called the guy who was moving the chairs, and he explained that there’s a scale inside the machine, so if no cupcakes come out, no charge will be made. We tried again, and this time he said that the “white chocolate with milk” I liked the most was gone, so I chose strawberry. We tried a second time, heard some strange noises, and then saw an error message on the screen. Since we work in IT, we found it really fun. The guy confirmed it was a mechanical issue and went to get our cupcakes. He found the “white chocolate with milk”! I was very happy, and my order wasn’t charged, which made me feel good. We kept trying to pay the guy, but he said it was our responsibility and kept apologizing because we couldn’t use the cupcake ATM. A very kind guy, great customer service, and I hope the ATM will be fixed, because I would like to get cupcakes using an ATM.

state: The ice is really delicious. It’s a super cute/vintage/nostalgic/entertaining/charming store. Hello, I’m a lover of high-quality ice. As such, I need to know where to find the best ice. Churn is one of my top choices in Phoenix, due to its unique flavors that aren’t absurd or terrible. They also have a creamy and smooth texture (although I would like it to be even more creamy and velvety!). The store itself makes me feel like a child in a candy shop, partly because of the retro atmosphere, and also because they sell candies… and other fun products and toys. For a small store, it’s possible to spend a lot of money here. My younger children love this place. The staff (most of them) are friendly and helpful, and seem genuinely happy to give samples. The most memorable flavors I’ve tried are: pecan with butter, chocolate, Vietnamese coffee, cookies and mint, carrot cake. Everything has been excellent, and it seems like they use high-quality ingredients. In addition to the classic options, they also have a fun pretzel cone that’s quite unique and delicious. There are some tables and chairs in front, and a shared dining area at the back, next to the nearby restaurant. But note: during peak hours (i.e., after dinner/at night on Fridays and Saturdays), the line can get very long, and the limited space can be a problem, since the store is small.

state:
I had heard of Sprinkles for years, but never had the chance to try their products… until yesterday! After visiting Gordon Ramsay’s restaurant, we went here to buy cupcakes. My wife loves cupcakes, and she was really looking forward to this stop in our culinary adventure in Las Vegas. We entered, and a cheerful young woman greeted us, and we made our orders. We chose a chocolate and peanut butter cupcake, a upside-down pineapple cake, and a cupcake with three layers of cinnamon. Each one cost $4.00. Here are the ones we ordered:

*   **Chocolate and peanut butter cupcake:** This was my wife’s favorite! She loves the combination of chocolate and peanut butter. It was very rich, sweet, and had an excellent texture and flavor with the peanut butter. 5 stars!
*   **Upside-down pineapple cake:** It was also great. It had a moist pineapple cake base, filled with pineapple jam/custard, and covered with butter frosting. This was my favorite out of the three. I think it was one of her monthly/weekly/daily specials. It was delicious, and if you like pineapple, don’t hesitate to try this! 5 stars!
*   **Cupcake with three layers of cinnamon:** This was our least favorite among the three, but still, it was quite delicious! It was a spiced cake with milk, cream cheese frosting, and cinnamon. It had a denser texture than the others, and seemed a bit “old-fashioned”. However, even so, it was still quite delicious. 4 stars.

The service from the young woman who prepared the cupcakes in the box, and the kind staff member at the counter, was excellent. $4.00 might seem expensive for a cupcake, but they are large, and the quality makes it worth it! Definitely would go back.

state: This review is short and lacks photos, as I ate my dessert too quickly to take a picture. The cereal milk ice cream with corn flakes really tastes like cereal milk, but obviously it’s sweeter—and, of course, much better, since sweetness always implies better quality, in my opinion. The “milk bar” cake… Hey guys! If you like nut cake, you’ll love this one, because it tastes similar to the filling in nut cake. No nuts involved. It’s delicious, and I felt embarrassed that I ate it so quickly. Also, don’t waste the cookies! My husband loves the birthday cake version, and I do too. I prefer “compost” type cookies—made with graham crackers, pretzels, fried potatoes, coffee, oats, and caramel butter. I’m from New York, and I used to go to the “milk bar” a lot when I lived there. There’s no difference in flavor, quality, or service here. So, if you’re looking for dessert in Las Vegas (which is pretty common for me), please come here.

state: After seeing this on Food Network a few years ago, I had to try this place myself. If Alton Brown recommends something, it’s definitely something special. The store was clean, and there was a line. After going through the line, there wasn’t immediate seating available, but that didn’t stop us from enjoying a Toffee Banoffee and Smores around the fire. The Toffee Banoffee really offers a great combination of flavors. The textures blend well together—there’s the crunch of ice cream and caramel, the softness of bananas, and a delicious sweet touch. I must say that I actually preferred the Smores around the fire a little more. If you close your eyes, you can even smell the fire. I don’t know how they add that smoked flavor, but Alton Brown should definitely try this too. Eventually, we managed to get a table and could relax and enjoy these magical creations. There’s also drinking water available—it would be great if they offered free milk too! It’s worth making the trip to Scottsdale just to try this ice cream shop.

state: Yes, this place deserves all the stars I’ve given it… and all the stars others have given it too. I’ve tried the donuts before (when my coworkers bought them), and I always wanted to buy some for myself, but I never got the chance until this morning. I know some people have trouble with the location or the old building, but… people care only about the quality of the donuts! And that’s obvious—they’re really delicious! I bought six donuts this morning… and a apple pie… (don’t worry, I’ll share them with you). The donuts include: raisins, pumpkin, peanut butter and chocolate, apple with caramel, Reese’s, and salted caramel. The apple is amazing. The raisins are incredible. The apple pie is the size of my head… or even bigger! The six donuts were in a smaller box… the apple pie was in a box designed for twelve pieces (even though it didn’t fill the whole box, still… huge!). In total, I spent $9.25, mostly on the apple pie. Six donuts cost less than $6! Incredibly fresh donuts… incredibly low prices… friendly staff behind the counter… what could be better? (PS: Bring cash or check– they don’t accept credit/debit cards.)

state: Without a doubt, the best ice cream in Phoenix! Don’t let its small location and size deter you—this place is worth a visit. They constantly innovate with flavors, and there’s always something truly unique! Everything is made in-house, so you can try everything. They offer ice cream sandwiches with donuts—yes, ice cream sandwiches with donuts. It sounds amazing, but it’s actually perfect! They aren’t too sweet, and not overly large either. They’re even pressed using a hot panini machine, which warms them perfectly before you taste them. The last time I went there, I tried vanilla ice cream—it seems simple, but it was undoubtedly the most flavorful and fresh vanilla ice cream I’ve ever tasted! It won awards for its taste (and that’s true!). They don’t advertise; they rely solely on word of mouth. They’re very friendly and attentive to all customers. I absolutely love this place.

state: The famous “sprinkles”… when it comes to decoration, cupcakes are definitely minimalist. This makes you rethink your childhood cupcakes. My husband ordered those with sugar and cinnamon (without icing), while I asked for those with double sugar and cinnamon with icing. I really loved the icing, but the cake itself didn’t impress me (usually, on the contrary, I do). My husband, who isn’t very fond of sweets, enjoyed the cupcake. This makes me wonder: is a cupcake really a cupcake if it’s sold to people who aren’t very fond of sweets? Maybe I’ll try the “sprinkles” again, but probably I’ll order cupcakes as a novelty, or maybe I’ll add the ice cream function of the store to my order.

state: This place is a real gem, hidden behind a bridge. I pass by Page Dairy Mart every day after work, and there’s always a long line at 3 p.m., even on rainy days. Finally, I stopped in one day, and it was delicious… now it’s become a habit for me. I chose something simple: creamy ice cream with some candy soda. It was very tasty and nostalgic. They have a wide variety of flavors and toppings, so I hope to try more in the future. Maybe I’ll even try one of the many sundes they offer! There’s no service inside; you order through the window. They don’t accept cash, but there’s an ATM nearby. The menu is quite extensive, so make sure to check all the options while waiting in line! The parking situation is good, with several spots around Page’s.

state: Located near ASU downtown campus, Melt. is a perfect addition to the Arts' District. I mean, why didn't we have a local ice cream parlor in PHOENIX yet? The small shop is ran by a nice youthful and friendly couple and the ice cream is made with local ingredients. You can grab ice cream and take it next door to Lost Leaf and make a beer float, take it across the street to the bookstore and watch the open mic, or just sit on Melt.s incredible front patio. At first I was a little scared of their 7 dollar milkshake until I was reminded that it was made using local dairy products (and it was the most delicious shake I have ever put in my face). Melt. It's a First Friday must stop venue too!

state: I first discovered Milk Bar when I tried its truffles in a gift box. I really liked the concept and the overall packaging. However, the truffles were a bit too sweet for my taste. So, I expected the cereal ice cream to be better—and it was! The ice cream tasted exactly like what one would expect from cereal milk ice cream. It wasn’t too sweet, and I liked that the cereal topping (at an extra $1 cost) provided a pleasant crunchy texture that complemented the soft, creamy ice cream. But I wish the cereal topping could be less salty. I don’t know what they do with it, but if they kept it as it is, it would be much better—crunchy, cornflake-like. Please don’t remove the cornflakes! I can’t give this place full 4 stars just because of the price. Paying $7 for a very small ice cream is simply crazy and not worth it.

state: My daughter and I went during the opening period, on a Sunday. It was our first time there. Although it was busy, everything worked well, and the lines moved relatively quickly. The only thing that ruined the experience were the careless customers. They constantly blocked the way for staff who tried to bring fresh bread and sweets, or left their lines (instead of waiting until they reached the area) to pick up bread and sweets themselves, making things difficult for everyone. There were also those who started taking items directly from the staff’s trays as they passed by. What a lack of courtesy! Despite all this, the staff remained professional, friendly, and helpful. Everything we ordered was delicious! The bread and sweets were tasty and soft. The tea with milk was good and smooth, with just the right amount of sugar. Definitely a place we will visit often :) Overall, a great Asian bakery that lives up to its promises.

state: Can I give it 3.5 stars? The baked products were decent. We bought a large amount of cookies and some breakfast pastries. I would say that the breakfast pastries we got—an apple tart and some butter-lime pastries—were really good. If I had to rate this place only based on the quality of those two items, I would definitely give it 5 stars. We also tried another type of cookie with walnuts; for me, it was just okay. The worst aspects of this place are the prices, the unhelpful service, and, to a lesser extent, the overall confusion. When we arrived, there were two very long lines, so which one should we choose? No one seemed to know. It turned out that one line was for placing orders, and the other was for paying. It’s not very intuitive, as the payment line seemed clearly marked as the starting point. They need to put some signs! The service was relatively quick, but the staff weren’t very friendly. We were buying things for ourselves and for someone else, so we asked for separate boxes. Yes, that didn’t seem to work well with the person who served us. They had a annoyed expression on their face. In fact, everyone at the restaurant had that same annoyed look. And finally, the prices… unbelievable! In the end, maybe it was our fault for buying too many cookies, but overall, we spent $50 on just a few pastries, one cookie, and maybe a bag of cookies. In a place where prices are usually high, that would be only about $20. If I could buy the breakfast pastries (5 dollars each) without having to wait in line, I would do it. On the other hand, I’m definitely interested in trying Buddy V’s restaurant, also owned by Carlo.

state: A macaron ice cream sandwich with a Fluff It marshmallow on top? Yes please! There are so many options too, including some very unique ones such as Fruity Pebbles macarons and Netflix and Chill ice cream. The cookie cup consists of two large macarons of your choice (They had strawberry, vanilla, Fruity Pebbles, and red velvet when I was here), four scoops of ice cream, with a marshmallow that is bruleed with a torch in front of you. We got ours with Fruity Pebbles and red velvet macarons, blueberry muffin and white chocolate raspberry ice cream. The entire cup was a beautiful sugary sight to behold. We dug in with gusto. I loved the chewy texture of the macaron with the creamy smooth ice cream and fluffy pillowy marshmallow with caramelized crust. We were definitely satisfied and full after sharing it. The cost was $6.25 pre-tax. Service was very friendly and warm and everyone seemed very happy to be working here. I would be too if I were surrounded with all this delicious bounty! The location is definitely a bit odd as it's hidden in the back of a shopping plaza right next to a residential area. Thanks to Yelp though we were able to indulge in a unique and tasty collaborative dessert we probably wouldn't have been able to see from the street. I'll definitely be back again for more delicious dessert.

Every time I visit, I buy a whole box of baked goods because they are so good. state: After hearing so much about this place, and being someone who loves desserts, I really hoped it would be good to me. It’s open 24 hours, and the brownie with caramel and salt is quite good. However, after three visits, I’ve tried several pastries and desserts, and in reality, they’re at best “acceptable” – at worst, they’re bland and heavy. The desserts are cold, and some of them, due to this, aren’t as good as they could be, like anything that’s supposed to be crunchy. The lovely décor doesn’t make up for the mediocre desserts. I haven’t yet tried their lunch or breakfast options, so maybe that’s what keeps other critics so enthusiastic.

state: I had never heard of Milk Bar until it was suggested to me on social media. I'm apparently easily influenced when it comes to food ads, because I started thinking about their cake often! I considered ordering it to be shipped from New York, but I'm actually glad I didn't spend the money because what I tried at the Vegas location wasn't the greatest. I got a slice of birthday cake, which was straight out of the fridge. Do people like cold cake? I really dislike it. I debated letting it sit out for a while, but decided to just go for it. It tasted like week old refrigerated cake, heavy and overly moist. I did appreciate the icing though, it melted in my mouth! I wasn't able to eat more than 1/4 of the cake slice, but I did eat a bunch of icing because it was pretty good. I'd love to try a fresh slice of their birthday cake! For $14, I just expected so much more. I left feeling pretty disappointed.

state: While continuing my search for the perfect macaron, I ended up in Las Vegas to try those tiny macarons the size of a palm leaf that I’ve seen on Yelp. Being quite demanding, I always buy two macarons first to try them out. Bouchon Bakery was a success… I tried the salty caramel with strawberry filling, and ended up buying five more (the sixth one was given away for free). The macarons (costing $3.50 each) are light but have a pleasant texture, just as I like them. The salty caramel filling also has an interesting texture, which I enjoy, while the strawberry and other fillings had a normal texture. We also tried the chocolate and pistachio flavors, but I don’t think I would order them again, because they didn’t have much flavor. I went to Aria to see the macarons from Jean Philippe, but they were only available in pre-packaged boxes of 6 pieces. Plus, they were very small. I wasn’t interested at all; if I can’t try one or two first, I don’t buy anything… yes, I’m quite demanding. I think you’ll really like them at Bouchon—the service was attentive and helpful… but most importantly, the macarons were amazing!

state: Novel Ice Cream is truly a unique experience. Located in a charming establishment with a country-style atmosphere, they offer a small outdoor space where you can enjoy their ice cream. They have various toppings—including your favorite childhood cereal, homemade ice cream flavors, and the option to put ice cream on a sandwich with a donut (yes, you heard that right) or with a vegan cookie stuck in the cup. The staff was incredibly attentive and helpful. They allowed us to try several flavors before we chose our combinations. I ordered lavender ice cream with honey and a crispy cookie on top, plus the cookie itself. I would like to see more types of cookies, but the cookie was good—more like the texture of a sweet cookie. The flavor of the ice cream I ordered was strong (not for everyone), but I love lavender in anything! If I visit Phoenix again, I will definitely go back to this place’s ice cream. A fun place with original options!

state: I tried the macarons here when I had the pleasure of buying the six-unit package. For $17.50, I had high expectations, considering Bouchon’s reputation and everything else. The macarons are twice the size of those I’ve tried before, which I found great. Despite their larger size, the taste and texture weren’t compromised. The creamy part wasn’t too sweet, and the cookie was soft and not dry. It would be great if the head chef or the team were present at the tent in Venice where I bought them, because I would give them a “high-five” for making such delicious macarons! It’s a pleasant and luxurious treat, but it’s expensive. For me, it’s a delightful reward to wait for at the end of a typical and busy trip in Las Vegas! Next, I’m really going to try out the Bouchon restaurant!

state: We stopped for dessert with friends and thought Butterwood was such a quaint little bakery with really unique flavor combinations. The atmosphere was super cozy and more like being a guest at someone's home than being in a bakery. The employee was friendly. The desserts were like nothing I had ever had before. Typical bakeries have chocolate and vanilla, but Butterwood uses unique flavors that were delicious. We tried the mini chocolate cake with Strawberry whipped cream, the olive oil orange cake with strawberry icing, the fig cake and apricot cake with pistachio icing. The cakes are definitely denser than what I was used to, more like pound cake. Everything was very flavorful. The cakes were moist and the icing wasn't too sweet. Such a nice little place to stop and loved that they are open late!

state: I really love discovering such amazing places, and I was disappointed to read the previous reviews. I heard that customer service wasn’t good, and the desserts weren’t of high quality. I was very happy to find out that these reviews didn’t reflect my experience at Amélie’s NoDa. The woman who helped me was very kind and helpful, which surprised me, considering the large number of orders she handled in just ten minutes when I was there. Yes, it was busy, but the line moved very quickly, and it took me just a few minutes to reach the counter. I was tempted by the delicious desserts, but I only bought the French macarons, which were my goal. The prices made me a little sad (as a university student), but I understand that you charge for fresh and high-quality ingredients. I took millions of photos of the beautiful “biscuits” before trying them. I bought various flavors, and they cost about $15 (approximately $1.45 per unit). My favorite flavors were honey and raspberry. The red fruit flavor was amazing, and combined with the peanut paste taste, it reminded me of a peanut paste sandwich with jam. I liked the peanut paste, but the only flavor I didn’t like was orange. For someone who usually doesn’t like orange, it wasn’t very good for me. But I wasn’t sad about buying them, because they looked great in my photos…

state: We searched tirelessly for a place that could bring joy to our days. We passed by the Pepper Forest, climbed the Gum Trees Mountains, stopped in the Lollipop Forest, and finally took a boat across the Frozen Sea to reach our final destination: the Candy Castle. This was our reaction when we found Sloan’s ice cream shop. In fact, we walked near the canal that led us to St. Mark’s Square in the Grand Canal Stores, where we found Sloan’s ice cream shop. Entering this bright, colorful, and charming ice cream shop brings back happy memories from our childhood. If you’re a heartfelt child, this place will surely bring you a lot of joy. The staff were very kind and helpful. Even though they were busy, they worked efficiently to make sure everyone was well taken care of. The ice creams they offered came in various flavors—from circus flavors to café flavors—all the usual flavors you would expect from an ice cream shop. There was also a variety of “sundae” types, including the extravagant “Tracy’s Kitchen Sink,” which consists of 18 ice cream balls and plenty of toppings in a sink. We ended up buying a “sundae” made of circus ice cream: an ice cream ball, hot chocolate, gummies, whipped cream, and cherry, all packed in a fun and reusable plastic container. The circus ice cream was sweet, but the toppings made it even more enjoyable to eat. The brownies and candy bars we also bought were equally delicious, as they could be heated up. They were soft, chewy, and quite large for a single serving. In fact, many of the products offered could be shared among two or three people. Another great thing about Sloan’s is her waffle cones. They are made fresh every day in the store. Overall, it’s a fun place to enjoy the scenery and become children again. An excellent addition to the ice cream shop in Venice’s Grand Canal. I will try other products if I’m in the area again. Yelp review #11 from 2018

state: Ok I normally would say 4 stars but because the amount of chaos to have someone help you made me not want to return for a while. I like the pasties and desserts and they are pretty good but I timed it and I had to take a number (#11) and they were on #1. It took 25 mins for me to get a small box of cookies. They must have had at least 40 people standing around waiting to order or waiting for an order. There was only 5 people working behind the counter...seems fine right? But what I noticed is there was NO URGENCY what so ever by any of the counter staff. Next in the middle of the chaos of of the counter staff takes a large circular tray/plate to arrange cookies to take across the street (maybe for a restaurant or something. She then walked them out and walked down the street. I wouldn't say that is the appropriate time to arrange a plate and do deliveries especially when the place is jam packed. It went to 4 people behind the counter. Might have been smarter to handle customers in store and have deliveries handled another way. Sorry but no cookies are worth 25 min wait. And they should drill their staff to serve a customer within 3 min. They would give much better customer service if they considered doing a retraining and changed it up a bit. I've been coming here for a few years and it's always the same. Time for a change

state: I was in Las Vegas celebrating my 27th birthday with a group of friends, and some of us found this great place on Yelp. We arrived for brunch, and the restaurant was full, with a wait of 25 minutes. That wasn’t a problem, as they offered to send us a message when our table would become available. We sat at a large table with velvet seats, and our waiter came quickly, serving us cold water and giving us some recommendations. Two of us ordered the “Petit Déjeuner American,” while another ordered a special dish whose name I don’t remember. But it contained mushrooms. We were served quickly, and the drinks were refilled without having to call for a waiter. The food was amazing, and the desserts were simply delicious. I learned that Beverly Hills has a bakery, and I can’t wait to visit the local branch. I recommend this place if you’re looking for delicious food that melts in your mouth.

state: Jack Frost Donuts is your old neighborhood donut shop in Cleveland. I literally came in early one day and a police officer was having a mentoring conversation with one of the young employees. Anyway, you'll never be disappointed eating fried cake and coffee and I wouldn't miss out on Jack's if you're looking for a Cleveland staple. My recommendations are the German Chocolate, Salted Caramel, and Maple Bacon. The coffee is self-serve and is pretty good.

state: Due to the jury service at the beginning of this month, I had the opportunity to visit the Donut Bar for two consecutive days. First visit: 11:30 a.m… among the remaining options, I tried a strawberry cheesecake and a Boston Creme. Both had an acceptable taste, but the chocolate glaze on the Boston Creme wasn’t just overly sweet—it also seemed dull, lacking the shine found in other donut shops. Additionally, the dough was a bit denser than I preferred. I gave the Donut Bar a chance to improve, so I decided to return the next day, earlier. Second visit: 7:30 a.m… arriving with a full selection, I checked the menu and ordered three types of donuts: Matcha, Blueberry Meyer Lemon, and The Samoa. I also ordered a Creme Brulee donut and the special donut of the day, Strawberries and Cream. The best of the three were the Creme Brulee donut and Strawberries and Cream; they came right after each other. The dough-based donuts here aren’t as light and fluffy, but they’re denser and darker than those in other shops in town. The dough-based donuts seem better than they really are—I only tasted a piece of each, but I was impressed by how dry they were. I couldn’t identify the flavors of matcha or Meyer lemon, but they were overly sweet (and I arrived half an hour after opening). Service was okay, and the prices are a bit uncertain, as there are other shops in town that charge less for products with better flavors, and won’t leave you feeling disappointed. As the song says: “I like classic donuts…” I prefer donuts with a classic style—light and fluffy, not covered with thick glazes, and not requiring Oreo or Pop Tart additions. For me, less is more. Maybe on my third visit, I’ll be lucky, but for now, I’m not in a hurry to go back. HELLO!!! Shaka’s measurement: \uuu/ \uuu/ \uu. 2.5

state:
Dripps is a small and modern ice cream and tea shop that belongs to Pokitrition. The atmosphere: A wall with artificial plants displays bright letters with the sign “Dripp it like it’s hot”. It’s definitely a perfect place for Instagram—it attracts millennials, including me. Customers waited behind to enjoy their ice creams and take great photos with this attractive background. Within a few hours of opening, many people already posted photos on social media. I think they did a good job promoting the new place, and many social media users became aware of it.  

Opening: Dripps opened last Saturday, September 29th. The store was open from 4:00 PM to 10:30 PM. My friend and I didn’t want to wait in line so long, so we arrived after dinner, around 8:30 PM. The line was still very long! So, congratulations to Dripps Co. on this successful new venture. Their colorful ice creams and teas are a success. All products have the promotion “buy one, get one free” and will remain valid during the first week after opening.  

Ice Creams:  
1. In a glass or with a stick (only one size available).  
2. Ingredients: All ice creams are vanilla-based, and you can choose your favorite childhood cereal, such as Lucky Charms, Cap’n Crunch, Frosted Flakes, Honey Bunches of Oats, Honey Nut Cheerios, Cookie Crisp, Froot Loops, and many others. These will combine with the vanilla flavor.  
3. Toppings: You can choose from a list of toppings offered. Most are dry cereals, but there are also some common toppings like cookie dough and crushed Oreo cookies. You can pay an extra 50 cents for other toppings, including fruits and other delicious options.  

Ice cream in a glass with a topping: I ordered an ice cream in a glass, mixed with my favorite cereal, Cap’n Crunch. I added pieces of cheesecake as my preferred topping at ice cream shops. The combination was amazing. The ice cream is rich and creamy, and the amount served is just right. The mixed cereal was slightly crumbly and granular, but still very delicious. I highly recommend the ice creams. I think even the regular ice cream would be delicious.  

Teas and Coffee: They also offer matcha teas, rose milk teas, matcha coffees, and Thai tea. You can add boba if you want. I still need to try them, but I’ve heard from other customers that they don’t disappoint. Next time I visit, I’d like to try the rose milk tea or matcha coffee. Everything looks beautiful, and I’m sure the taste matches the beauty of these drinks.

state: I was there at the grand opening at 9. got there around 8:00am and was one of the first 25 people . They had UNLV cheerleaders to cheer and had a great opening. The bread was nice and fresh. Respect for the managers to have crowd control and not let it look like a Hong Kong protest inside with people grabbing bread off the trays before they hit the shelf. They handled that pretty well. I got everything I could on my tray. two mugs and the yardstick for the first 100 customers. The above review is 5 stars worthy for the morning. the reason why I put a one star is for people who are curious and for the managers to look at how they did cause they care about the business and need customer feedback. I went back there at night because I gave most of the bread pastries away to my coworkers since we had a birthday celebration. I did not have a chance to try the matcha custard bread, milk pudding bun, the croquette bun. etc. I went back hoping there was still more at night. instead it was mostly subpar items like muffins and the egg tarts. None of the premium items I saw in the morning or mentioned above or the ones you see in the morning review posts. It was just pumping out the same bread and put it in three different places. I saw the berry tart like in three different shelves and muffins that anyone can go get at Starbucks. It was just selling bread at that point for profit since there was a demand there, but also because they probably ran out of ingredients for the other items. Here is the reason where they screwed up. Since the morning. it was pretty chaotic with all the excitement. I forgot to ask if the free yardstick was refillable or not. I heard the regional divisional manager say this is the first of its kind for Las Vegas since it has Vegas themes on the free items. I could not hear if he said "free" refills or " no refills for the yardstick. I went back at night to ask and clarify. I asked three employees and they did not know. Till I asked the lady at the drink section kindly if it was free refill or not. The cashier next to her heard me and said in an angry tone. NO REFILL. then mumbled to her coworker " they brought it up in the meeting." the one I asked kindly went to her manager and asked and she came back and told me no without yelling No REFILL like the other cashier did. I accepted it since i wasnt sure due to all the noise in the morning. The one star is for the rude cashier at the front. All it takes is one thing to ruin the whole experience. the customers are the driving force for the business, but if they have cashiers not able to handle the customers, then people reading should be aware to expect it. Bread was perfect, grand opening was perfect. Ask a question and get an angry response from another employee and I am willing to spend the time to write this one star review. Do yourself a favor. Dont go there at night and grab the leftover inventory. Wait till the hype goes down and they train their employees to be nice and courteous to the customers.

state: Apparently, many of you don’t know the difference between macarons and macaroons. They’re two different types of cookies. “Ninety’s” specializes in ice cream sandwiches with macarons, and they’re delicious—but also very difficult to eat! My first visit was about a year ago, before the renovations and menu updates at the store. At that time, the ice cream sandwiches with macarons seemed to have been prepared in advance and stored in the freezer. There were several options for each sandwich, around 15–20 flavors. I chose the pistachio flavor, mainly because I like the green color, and my friend chose the birthday cake flavor. The macarons were a little dry, as they had been stored in the freezer, but still, we both loved them! They were huge, and a great choice at just $5.95 each. I returned during summer, after the renovations were completed. I would say I was a little disappointed to see that there were only 4–5 flavors of macaron sandwiches available (maybe prepared daily?). But now they’re making them on order, instead of preparing multiple items and storing them in the freezer. This way, the macarons won’t be dry, and this time they looked very fresh. My last visit was a few days ago. I was in the area and wanted to try all my favorite places before driving 30+ minutes home. There were more macarons with unicorn themes on the menu, but that day they had ice cream sandwiches with Thai tea macarons… Seriously? Vanilla ice cream with Thai tea syrup, along with macarons with Thai tea flavors. It was everything I, as a food lover, could desire… Thai tea integrated into an amazing dessert! They also have other options that aren’t very appealing to me… “Yum-ee” breads (I don’t like donuts), cereal milkshakes, and even a menu with salty dishes? Hmm, maybe one day… But let’s be realistic… The macaron sandwiches are amazing! Anyway, seriously, if anyone has tips on how to eat those ice cream sandwiches with macarons without feeling like I’m learning to eat, please let me know. I’ll try it during my next visit to “Ninety’s”!

state: Presti is an ideal place to enjoy a snack and coffee: they have plenty of seats, both inside and outside, and operate efficiently using a “store ticket” ordering system. I love coming here and sitting in one of the windows-side seats to study and watch people chat around me. They offer an amazing selection—everything you could imagine you’d find in an Italian bakery. However, most food is prepared early in the day, so especially in the late afternoon, after the pastries have been displayed for a while, it might be better to look elsewhere. You can never go wrong with ice cream or any pastry there: it’s definitely the perfect place to order a custom cake for a special occasion (my favorites are, of course, tiramisu and pistachio ones). Also, it’s perhaps the only place in Little Italy that sells pizza slices, and they also have a great selection of hot and cold foods.

state: During my first visit a few years ago, I really loved this place. But my last visit wasn’t as good. It’s a fun place with a very interesting atmosphere and a beautiful display of sweets. We tried several candies, and my husband also ordered a latte. I really wanted to try one of their lattes, but unfortunately they don’t have decaffeinated coffee, so I couldn’t have it. My husband enjoyed his latte very much. I tried almost everything, and everything was very sweet. Like many candies, I expected them to be sweet, but these were so sugary that I couldn’t eat much. They were all good, but far from the best I’ve ever tried. The tables were full of crumbs, and they weren’t cleaned properly, which isn’t very pleasant. The service at the counter was attentive and quick. I would say it’s worth visiting if you’re there and want to do something different.

state: I loved this ice cream place in California, and when I saw it here, I cried! I’m pretty sure it was a very cold winter night, but that didn’t stop me from ordering. The variety here is incredible, and each flavor is creamy and delicious. There’s something for everyone. I always order the 4-flavor tasting because it’s an excellent offer. 4 large servings for $4.25. If you try to order 4 servings at Cold*****, be prepared to pay a lot of money – #just saying. You’ll definitely want 4 servings, because you won’t be able to choose just one. If you think you can’t finish it, bring it home and freeze it. Your future self will thank you, I promise. Some of my favorite flavors are Graham Central Station, Blue Monster, and Blueberry Cobbler. The line might seem long, but it moves quickly. The staff and how the place is organized are very efficient. Plus, they allow you to try samples, so don’t be shy.

state: It's really hit-or-miss at Milk Bar, but for the most part their desserts are way too sweet. I saw the chef's episode - Christina Tosi - on Chefs Table on Netflix and have been to Milk Bars across the country and I don't recommend anything really, which is a shame because I have lots of respect for the chef herself. Here's what I've had: It was our friends bday so they brought over these Milk Balls to Momofuku to end the meal. The only cute thing about it was the candle. It was just a crumbled up former-cake dusted with too much powdered sugar. I'd be embarrassed to serve this to people if I was the owner, even if it was free (it wasn't, we paid for this abomination) 1/10 Crack Pie - (now it's known as the milk bar pie) - again, too sweet, but edible. 5/10 Compost cookie kit - this is the only reason I'm bumping up my review. I brought home a tin with the ingredients from my trip to DC years ago and it was really fun to make and not bad at all! 8/10 Assorted cookies- got these for my bday this year and couldn't finish them. Way too sweet and hard/crumbly! 4/10 Overall everything is way too sweet at Milk Bar. I heard their cereal milk soft serve is good, so maybe... the 5th time I visit one of their locations... I can try it one day.

state: 9/21/21 - CLARIFIED DIRECTIONS TO GRAB AND GO BAKERY: 1. Park in the Venetian Self Park Garage 2. Take Elevators to Food court /shops level 3. Take the escalators down and make a sharp right or left to join line for the shop counter (line window started right across JUICE FARM) Idk if they recently changed the location, but previous reviews mentioned near the palazzo theater, guest elevators etc, but If you don't know where those places are then you might get frustrated like i did. I done lost my mind looking for this counter right behind the escalators that take you up to coffee bean(food court) /parking garage. Pastries were just as good as I remember from the restaurant and the boxes flew home well on my flight home. Standouts- kouighamann : the closest texture I've tried in the states to the ones in France. Dense and buttery- should not be flaky or falling apart into crumbs. Almond croissant: so toasty (even when cold) with good buttery almond filling. Bouchon: a hybrid between a brownie bite and toasted cannele lol. Got a few chocolate chips on the bottom too.

state: Wow! Talk about heavenly baked goodness! I love tje smell of baked goods... i couldn't resist! The smell just draws you in... From outside the shop you can smell the yumminess but when you walk in you just get overwhelmed by not only the smell but the shop is full of all the bake goods... I wanted ot all... We walked around at least twice before started to pick out our goodies to take home... The shop itself was very retro and clean... the set up was very easy to follow and well set up... all the staff was busy hustling around stocking, cleaning, or helping customers... For a weekday in the middle of the day was pretty busy but the shelves were constantly being refilled... i had the bacon buns which was really good the bread was so soft and the bacon made it so much more tasty... i also had the strawberry shortcake it was so light and dreamy with the fresh strawberries... yummy! My daughter got the milk bun which is her favourite... oh and the pork bun that was onolishous too... we have to go back for more...

state: Before, I used to go to O Face Doughnuts for their “maple bars”. So I decided to try this place out. I was surprised by the variety they offered. It was almost overwhelming, but it didn’t stop me from trying different things. There might be too many items to list all of them, but what really stood out was the “French Toast Donut”. They only serve it on weekends, but do you really need a donut every day of the week? For a while, I ordered it weekly with my partner. It came with Vermont maple syrup, whipped butter, and homemade raspberry jam. Usually, it was enough for me, but he is bigger, so he also ordered the raspberry cheesecake donut, which he said was the best sweet treat he’d ever tasted. Additionally, they have homemade chocolate milk and cold coffee available, which makes the trip worth it. The staff are excellent, and the experience is quick and simple. I recommend coming before the donuts run out.

state: I was so excited for Milk Bar's arrival. And, I was So disappointed. I got 3 cookies, a shake, and a soft serve ice cream. Everything was OK, but for $26 I expected to be blown away and I wasn't. There are off Strip places for way less money turning out a much better product. I wished that this location was more bakery and less walk up counter. I think when you SEE items in a bakery case... It's part of the experience. Everything here is already packaged to go or, with the frozen treats, you don't see them until you get them. Also, there is no seating anywhere. The Birthday Cake shake was tasty, but fairly small for $10. The soft serve cup is one size, but they do fill it up. I got the cereal milk flavor with the cornflake topping. It definitely tasted like it was supposed to which I enjoyed, bit the ice cream had a weird texture that was off-putting...like the cream was curdled or something. I threw it away about halfway through. Cookies was an OK size and a chewy texture, but 3 for $8?!?!? Completely overpriced. I can cross this place off my bucket list, but I won't likely be back.

state: Opening day… initial impressions… the prices are quite high compared to what’s offered. On opening day, there wasn’t much waiting time; I quickly reached the counters after coming down from the Cosmo elevator. To try out different flavors, I chose the “Most Popular” combo and the strawberry-millet milkshake. The service was quick, though there was a mistake with our order, resulting in a free sweet potato milkshake. These milkshakes are supposed to be similar to Dairy Queen’s Blizzard or McFlurry. To my surprise, none of them were overly sweet, and the flavor was quite pleasant. What didn’t satisfy me were all the pieces left at the bottom of the milkshake. A straw is provided, but the pieces are too big for it, and unfortunately, there are no regular spoons available; only wooden spatula-like sticks can be used. Additionally, the consistency between the two milkshakes was very different: one was too thick to drink with a stick, while the other was too liquid. As for the milk soft serve with cereal, it didn’t seem very impressive. I haven’t tried the nut cake, birthday truffles, or composta cookies in my combo yet. However, I don’t think I’ll go back to Milk; there are cheaper options elsewhere at VEGAS! Unfortunately… too much advertising.

state: A small and cozy ice cream place. It definitely has a special atmosphere—the interior with its 80s cereal theme takes you back to another era. We asked our friend for a bowl of “Cosmo & Wanda,” which contains fruit cereals and “Captain Crunch” mixed with almond milk and ice cream—and it was delicious! In fact, the almond milk added an extra sweet touch, which was surprising. It was a perfect combination. I ordered a smoothie and “Mucha Lucha.” It was a very sweet horchata smoothie, with a perfect balance of cinnamon and sugar. Both of us loved it. They were very thoughtful in helping to arrange the line as quickly as possible, paying attention to every detail. I think we had to make some changes at the last minute, but they communicated well with us and acted quickly to solve any problems. They definitely wore gloves, which made the place feel very clean and well-organized. The staff smiled a lot, and we really enjoyed being there—we felt comfortable and happy.

state: It’s located right next to the stairs on the second floor, alongside the Momofuku restaurant. That’s where the Milk Bar is! I never had the chance to visit New York to try these delicious desserts, so I wanted to try them while I was in Las Vegas. I ordered the “Greatest Hits” combo for $19, along with three cookies for $8. The “Greatest Hits” combo included a cereal milk ice cream with corn flakes, a portion of “crack pie,” a compost cookie, and a package of 3 birthday cake truffles. I also ordered another compost cookie, a chocolate cookie with corn flakes, and a raspberry and cream cookie. The ice cream was small, but it was delicious! In fact, you could taste the cereal flavor in the ice cream, just like when you finish eating your Frosted Flakes. The corn flakes that came with the ice cream were slightly salty, which provided a nice crunch and contrast. “Crack pie” was a creamy and sweet dessert. The compost and chocolate cookies were okay, but the raspberry and cream cookie was amazing—it had exactly the same flavor as the top part of a raspberry muffin! However, the best thing I bought were the birthday cake truffles. They had the same flavor as “funfetti” and weren’t dry, despite their appearance.

state: The food is excellent, as far as Italian bakeries go they know what they're doing. I love that they serve lunch and provide a variety of options through the week, pizza, stromboli, pasta, pasta salads, all very solid. Three stars due to service. We went on a Wednesday for lunch and I waited as the next in line for 10 minutes for my number to be called. 10 minutes in line easily feels like 30, especially when you're on your lunch break. They have it set up that one employee serves one ticket from order all the way through checkout, it's a very inefficient process during peak hours. I consider myself very patient as I used to be a waiter, but I was really close to walking out, especially when the employees started bickering about tips. Finally, when I was ready to check out my server had to wait for the sole cash register as it was being used by another employee. As Marcus Lemonis would say, the process is broken. I recommend the food, but I doubt I will return, I can't give up that much of my lunch hour just waiting....

state: I saw them recently on Food Network, and I wanted to try the Toffee Bonafi sundae. It’s a bit far from my house, but I have to say it was worth the trip. There are few things that meet expectations, and this is one of them. It’s basically the perfect sundae, and it’s worth every gram of guilt. Usually, I’m not a big fan of sweets and ice cream, but the caramel with almonds in this sundae is really delicious. The salty caramel and vanilla ice cream from Madagascar is even better than I expected. The store employee was very kind and did an excellent job preparing my sundae. I felt a little guilty before eating it all up. (But I quickly forgot about it.) If you live far away, it’s worth the trip. If you live nearby, I recommend taking some time to go. Try it: – Toffee Bonafi

state: I’m a huge fan of donuts, and believe me, I’ve been to places where they have amazing donuts. This is undoubtedly one of the best places I’ve ever tried for donuts. It’s like a hidden treasure right in the center of the city. The store opens (on Sundays) at 8 a.m. (Pacific Time). You’ll see a line forming by 7:30 a.m. At 8 a.m., the store opens, and someone goes out to count how many children with their families are in line at that time… The chef and his assistants come out with a tray of freshly made donuts for the children and hand them out one by one. The assistants also give each child a balloon. Then they start serving customers. When you enter the store, you’re greeted with a smile and the wonderful smell of donuts, cream, and coffee. They take great care to serve you, answer your questions, and prepare your order. By the time you reach the checkout, your order is already ready! The place is clean, with a cheerful and pleasant atmosphere, excellent service, and amazing donuts. It’s absolutely essential to visit this place and try the donuts!

state: I went to Ohio City on a Friday after dinner. There was a line, though not very long, and service was quick. The flavors displayed in the window were interesting, but none really caught my attention. However, there were several flavors on the “idea board” that seemed great, so maybe it was just a bad night for me. I ordered a ice cream sandwich with churros, with vanilla ice cream. But I asked for just one portion of ice cream instead of two, since it was already quite full after dinner. The churros were very good—hot and freshly made from the freezer. The ice cream wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t exceptional either (for me). I’ve also tried their ice cream at other festivals and such. Maybe it just isn’t my favorite. But that doesn’t mean all their flavors are very interesting or fun. It’s just a good idea to check out what they have and see if something suits your taste.

state: I really love Sprinkles. Their cupcakes are always delicious, so you never have to worry about a bad day. I also liked that they have their new ice cream shop. I haven’t tried it yet, but I plan to do so soon. They make sandwiches with pieces of any cupcake flavor you like—biscuit sandwiches, milkshakes/malt drinks, frozen hot chocolate, even “red velvet” cones! It’s amazing. The evening menu is a bit limited, so try to arrive earlier during the day if possible. We stopped at the High Roller (next to them) and bought two mini cupcakes (lemon and vanilla). My favorite flavors are vanilla and cinnamon, as well as banana and the vegan “red velvet” flavor. As someone who isn’t vegan, this says a lot. There are also seasonal flavors available all the time (currently caramel and pumpkin), and they also make dog cupcakes, which our girls love. They also have a free rewards program with many interesting benefits: a cupcake as a gift on your birthday, free items from the menu whenever you accumulate 15 points, access to exclusive events, “buy one, get one free” promotions, and queue-buster passes. The ice cream queue is usually longer than the cupcake queue (since it’s a dessert), so you should be able to enter and exit quickly if your goal is just getting cupcakes.

Be careful, folks… be careful…

state: Can you guess what I discovered today? This ice cream shop, or rather, this boutique selling handmade ice creams, has a chef working there. So, at the time I wrote this review, there are already 259 reviews that tell everyone about the delicious ice creams available. Therefore, I’ll just write one review myself, but their ice creams are really good! I ordered the chocolate with salt and caramel ice cream. Usually, when ordering hot chocolate ice cream, you expect a generous portion of hot chocolate that will melt some of the ice cream. But here, the portion is lighter, as the hot chocolate comes in a square bottle-like container, and it’s stored in something that looks like a pot filled with water. I get it—they don’t want to ruin their handmade ice creams, but I wouldn’t classify what I ordered as hot chocolate ice cream; instead, it’s more like “a portion of ice cream with a little bit of chocolate sauce”. Anyway, I enjoyed the ice cream along with one of the three free options they offer: sea salt flakes (which were black so you could see how much was used), which made the ice cream a little more special, followed by their homemade cream. By the way, the other two free options are colored sprinkles and extra virgin olive oil. I chose to enjoy the “ice cream with a little bit of chocolate sauce” in a bowl of freshly made gofret, which was very creamy and delicious. But honestly, butter makes everything better. The first half of the ice cream was enjoyed on a super uncomfortable chair, but with a modern design. When my stomach started to hurt, I went to their table, which had a relief pattern on the back, thinking I might get a massage, but unfortunately, I couldn’t read it :( In any case, it’s good ice cream that’s worth trying at least once. So save your money, since they’re expensive.

state: Wow! Really. Bless the cattle whose milk gave rise to this ice cream. It’s a small shop located in one of the restored cabins from an old prison camp. So, be prepared to be patient if there’s a lot of traffic at times. The ice cream is surprisingly delicious, creamy, and creative. As someone who is simple-minded, I tried the caramel with bourbon ice cream. It’s fantastic! Bring your dessert and sit in the courtyard. Watch how the sun shines on the charming restored cabins. If you’re people who enjoy the night, watch how the moon appears. If you’re hungry, buy pizza from the street next to the shop first. The owner is also very kind. It’s great to meet people who enjoy what they do.

state: This gem is located near the university and close to the airport. It’s in a corner plot, on the inner side of the parking area, so we almost missed it. Thank goodness we found it! Definitely on our list of places to visit when we’re in Phoenix. The chocolate ice cream was, without a doubt, the best ice cream I’ve ever tasted. No, I wasn’t very hungry—it was creamy and delicious. The fact that it was inside a donut and covered with Oreo cookies made it even more amazing. And we’re on vacation, so zero calories, right?

state: I have tried their products before, but this was my first visit. What was best was getting complete and accurate responses from the staff. The staff really deserve praise. The cake I chose had an excellent texture. The only thing that prevented it from achieving the highest rating was the raspberry topping—good taste, but with a gummy and elastic texture. It’s not easy to serve this kind of cake in a coffee shop setting. I chose a blueberry and cream cheese muffin. The dough wasn’t too sweet, and the topping had a good balance. The blueberries tasted delicious, but there were too many inside the muffin, so some sections were too wet. I ordered a fruit cake, and my server recommended a fresh strawberries cake, which I accepted right away. The cake was perfect, very impressive. The cut strawberries had a pleasant freshness, which complemented each other without being overwhelmed by frosting. The cake had a light and crunchy texture, and the edges had that satisfying crunch. A+. My happiest moment was when I asked my server, expecting a response like “Of course,” if they had “French press coffee”. Almost no one knows this, and I was looking for that answer. The response was that they showed me two different sizes and asked if I preferred dark or medium coffee. French press coffee from staff who know what they’re doing. A+. If you don’t mind carbohydrates, you should visit Amélie’s. If you need to control your carbs, you can do it like me—try out the baked goods and give others more portions.

state: Welcome to The Republic. The Republic of rich and delicious ice cream! They offer unique flavors, including special flavors for celebrations like mint, ginger, and egg punch. After reviewing the flavor options, I decided to try an ice cream sandwich (4.50 dollars) with ginger ice cream. The cookies that come with the sandwich are chocolate or honey-based, but you can also choose premium cookies (a mix of oat and chocolate cookies) for 10 dollars. I wanted something different, so I ordered a chocolate cookie and a honey cookie. The ice cream itself was excellent, and I really liked the pieces of ginger mixed with the ice cream. However, the cookies were too sweet for my taste. When I tasted the sandwich, I only felt a generic sweetness, not the actual ingredients. Also, although the honey cookie had a pleasant texture that made it easier to eat with the soft ice cream, the chocolate cookie was more hard. The service was friendly and attentive. If I’m in the area and have an urge for ice cream, I would definitely go back here.

state: I've come to the conclusion that I'm not a huge macaroon person but I had to check out Bouchon because of the rave reviews on Yelp and since I had time to kill... I was hoping to try one of their carrot cake cookies but unfortunately they were out by 2pm :( Not to worry, they had plenty of their famous macaroons beautifully lined up. I was buying them for me and my sister and her friend so I decided not to get any crazy flavors they may not like. I got a vanilla for myself, one coffee, and one chocolate. They were HUGE. yelp.com/user_local_phot¦ Holy moly. I had more fun taking the picture than eating it I think. No, but they were good. The cookies had a crunch to them while still keeping an airy texture to them. The filling wasn't overly sweet and each had their own distinct flavor. They weren't cheap, I think $3.50 ish for one but heyyy these are some seriously awesome macaroons for the macaroon enthusiasts so check em out. You won't be disappointed! YELP 365: 175/365
