state: Popcorn has always been a somewhat common snack for me. But generally, adding butter, salt, or chocolate makes it edible. However, thanks to an unplanned afternoon at the western market, I probably won’t ever go without one or three bags hidden somewhere. You won’t have to buy popcorn in the microwave anymore! I know I won’t. All those years wasted… I highly recommend popcorn with cherry soda flavor! Yes, Yelp folks, popcorn with cherry soda flavor. It’s worth a visit. If you’re looking for traditional desserts, caramel popcorn is always fresh, made right away! A great value option is their large gift boxes, containing 2 or 3 of your favorite, unique flavors, and you’ll have enough for 3 nights of movies! TIP: Although they have a tent at the western market, they also have a store right across from it. So you can avoid those ridiculous lines.

state: I love this place. What I like best are the “cupcakes” with ice cream. You get two servings of ice cream, plus a macaron on top and a toasted marshmallow. You can choose two servings of the same flavor or two different ones. The size of each serving is perfect—enough to serve one or two people. The ice cream is delicious and has a very rich texture. I bought a Nutella ice cream with strawberries and guava, along with a “fruity pebble” macaron. I paid about $7.50 for the “cupcake”. The place is located in a small shopping center, but it’s still a great place to visit. You can try any flavor of ice cream, and the staff are very friendly. This place is one of the few unique places that Arizona has to offer.

They’re basically slightly sweet bread, but in large sizes or with excessive decorations. I’ve probably tried all their donuts, and in my opinion, they’re not good. Their donut cone ice cream is good, and their cream brûlée donuts used to be good too. I’ve probably been here six times because their Instagram account is very popular, but I have to say that their donuts simply aren’t good.

state: I was very happy that they came to the city. It’s an excellent bakery, considering the price. Most products cost between $11.50 and $3.00. The staff at the counter is always busy, as all their locations are popular. However, I’m very disappointed with their salted sea salt coffee. I really like it, and every time I’m in California, I usually buy three cups a day. I go there every day. In the Las Vegas location, they add some coffee and then water to the coffee. Diluted coffee? Really? It’s like ordering a “venti” at Starbucks, but they use just one dose of espresso and water for the other two doses. When I asked about this, the employee said that’s how they prepare it. Then she asked the manager to explain it too. I’ve seen how it’s prepared in California, and they don’t dilute the coffee. That’s why I like it—it’s strong, but not anymore. Thanks for the diluted coffee. To get salted sea salt coffee without dilution, go to BREW TEA BAR.

state: I stayed at the Palazzo, and I saw on Yelp that there was a highly rated bakery right next to it, at the Venetian. This bakery is just across from the Grand Luxe Café at the Venetian. I ordered a vanilla macaron, an almond croissant, and a raspberry muffin. The macaron was really large but of very poor quality. It was cold and hard, and it felt like I was eating something that had been in the refrigerator for a week. I took a bite and threw it away. Since I usually eat macarons across the United States, a regular macaron is at room temperature, not hard, and usually has a soft texture. Avoid this macaron at all costs. On the other hand, the almond croissant and raspberry muffin were good, but not particularly outstanding.

People can grab a number by the entrance and wait inside/look around until they hear their number being called. Once the Presti's employee shouts out their number, customers can go to the front to place their orders. Presti's employees will loudly shout the number twice before moving on to the next number. We ordered some strombolis but they were adequate! Definitely did the job for some Italian food, but I wished there was something that wowed me more.

state: This is the first Sprinkles branch I’ve visited that offers cupcakes, cookies, and ice cream. I’ve already tried their cupcakes before… generally, they’re good, but there’s too much frosting, according to my taste. As for the cookies, they’re delicious! My only complaint is that I didn’t buy more than one cookie. The chocolate sparkle cookie wasn’t very sweet, and there was a lot of chocolate sparks. The cookie was a bit crumbly, but very soft, with a buttery flavor in the middle. They were really tasty! I also tried a little of the peanut butter cookie with pretzel sparks, and to my surprise, I really liked it. Generally, I’m not a big fan of peanut butter cookies, but mixed with chocolate sparks and pretzel pieces, I love them! The service was friendly, and the person who served us was quite patient as C decided what ice cream, cupcake, and cookie she wanted. If the line inside gets too long, this branch has a “cupcake dispenser” that can be used outside (open 24 hours a day).

state: As a coffee addict, I can be pretty critical of bakeries/coffee shops etc. Amelie's impressed me. They offer an array of hot and cold beverages that are artfully crafted but available in limited and small sizes. The ambiance is great for socializing, studying, or just sitting and people-watching. I love that it is open 24/7, 365 days a year - you can't beat that convenience! The pastries are too numerous to review individually here, but are all delicious. I have dreams about their twice-baked croissants and their Neopolitan pastries are perfect to share. They are adding more gluten-free options (like the salted caramel brownies) but right now there are only a few. Overall, Amelie's is an awesome venue for pretty much anything (you can also rent out the back rooms for bridal/baby showers etc.) and is only on an upward trajectory. I would definitely recommend it for people of all ages and walks of life :)

I ordered a chocolate croissant and a cheese Danish to share with my boyfriend. The chocolate croissant was fresh and crispy, but oh, that cheese Danish was special! So creamy and crunchy, with perfectly smooth and sweet cheese filling. I’m drooling just writing this! Really, it’s worth trying. And actually, baked goods here are extremely affordable for such a famous bakery in Las Vegas.

Definitely going back next time I’m in Las Vegas!

I see some people complaining about prices here but you pay for what you get and its not like u cant see the prices on the menu before paying. What I didn't love was seeing flies in the case with all the desserts. I guess I expected controlling the flies to be better when in a bake shop in Little Italy. That was so much of a turn off I had to give Presti's 3 stars. However, the case that didn't have flies were the cakes. I had the tiramisu which was so creamy and light! I took some hazelnut biscottis home and paired them with a chai tea. Despite the flies, (I'm sure it was just a busy or off day) I will definitely go again because honestly, you just can't find delectable Italian baked goods in many places in Northeast Ohio that are sold at a very reasonable price.

state: The best thing about Mitchells? Their vegan chocolate ice cream is literally better than any dairy-based ice cream I've ever had. Hands down. It is so creamy, velvety, and chocolatey - and all of my friends have said the same thing once I make them try it. That being said, I've also never had a bad flavor at Mitchell's. Their seasonal flavors are always on point (e.g. the coffee porter, the mint chocolate truffle, etc), and their classic flavors can't be beat (black raspberry chocolate chunk, pistachio, peanut butter, cookies and cream, bing cherry chocolate chunk, etc). Their staff are also super nice and knowledgeable about the flavors, which is fantastic when I can't decide what new flavor to try. Case in point: one day I wanted to try a new non-dairy combo, and per the staff's suggestion, I got the best smoothie I've ever had - a vegan chocolate, raspberry sorbet, and banana smoothie sent from the heavens (picture attached). When you come here, you honestly can't go wrong!

state: Strawberry muffins are the real reason I travel to Las Vegas every year. (Well, my boss pays for the trip, pretending it’s an invitation to the Electronic Consumer Hall of Fame, but really, he’s just trying to keep me employed by paying me to enjoy my Bouchon muffins.) It’s a small bakery in The Venetian. You can find several locations scattered around. There are two (one upstairs, one downstairs) at the northern end, where there’s a raised hallway that connects to the IT and Mirage areas. Usually, I go to the one upstairs, as it’s on my way to the exhibition center and the CES buses heading to LVCC. I’ve seen some rooms that are larger than the one I frequent, but as long as it’s big enough to store the muffins (and a clerk to sell them, along with a cup of coffee), that’s all that matters. The muffins seem a bit expensive (but what isn’t in Las Vegas?), but once you try one, you’ll immediately realize you’d be willing to pay more. They’re delicate yet chewy at the same time. They’re not too sweet, but just sweet enough to satisfy a craving for pastries. The outer layer breaks apart pleasantly, and the inside is creamy and firm. I dream of these muffins. You need one. Go get one, or a dozen.

state: Carlo’s Bakery in Las Vegas was a delightful experience! No, it’s not in New Jersey, and the place is small, so don’t expect a huge variety of products. For a small local shop located inside the Venetian Hotel shopping area, it was really fun to visit! My favorite desserts were the eclairs with chocolate on top and the “pecan white puffs”! They also sell souvenirs, which added a perfect touch for me! The desserts aren’t cheap, but they aren’t expensive either. You’ll probably have to pay around $4.00 for a dessert. But you’re in Las Vegas, so almost nothing is cheap! You can watch the staff prepare the desserts while waiting for your packaging and bag. I visited the place twice during my stay in Las Vegas, and even brought some back with me in my suitcase!

state: The desserts are incredible, and the fact that they’re available 24 hours a day is a great advantage. Amelies is always on my list when I visit NoDa. French press coffee: 10-10; salty caramel brownies: 10-10; 100 dollars for a baguette with cheese: 10-10 (that extra zero isn’t an error… it’s the best budget-friendly food in the city). The only reason I give it 4 stars instead of 5 is because sometimes there aren’t any tables available, and it’s so crowded that it takes 30 minutes to get to the counter and get food… but I guess places like Amelies can’t avoid crowds because the place is just so good. If you visit Charlotte, don’t miss this place—it’s essential. Amelies also designed and baked all the cakes shown in the movie “The Hunger Games”, which I found to be a curious detail. It’s also worth mentioning that this place is perfect for a first date, as it’s quite casual. Go check it out!

state: I haven't left a review on Yelp in forever, but after our awesome experience today, and reading Sherise M's review...I had to. 1.) My wife and I commented after leaving Novel, that Brandon and the other employee there were some of the kindest food/beverage workers we've ever met. They were pleasant, patient, helpful and knowledgable, and sincerely thanked us at least 5 times. 2.) It was fast service, even with a few people in front of us. But then again, I don't have a warped/dramatic view of time like someone else seems to (Sherise M). 3.) The ice cream was amazing, and if you think $5 is overpriced for a nationally recognized scoop of ice cream...then A.) Check the prices ahead of time, B.) Buy the cheapo grocery store plastic tub of ice cream, C.) Realize that "wasting" $5 on ice cream YOU felt wasn't worth it (but countless reviewers and media outlets think IS)...is no reason to blast a business and its owner in such a petty and immature way. I weep for the people that have to listen to these diatribes from you on a daily basis...which I say because.... 4.) Take one look at her Yelp profile and you'll see exactly the kind of person she seems to be (let's hope it's only in the Yelp-a-Sphere). How many 1 star reviews can you give that deem a place as having THE WORST SERVICE? Maybe it's time you have a wee look in the mirror and recognize that your level of negativity, entitlement, and lack of empathy are the culprits of your bad experiences. Not the businesses. Not the business owners. TL;DR: Check yourself and grow up, please, for your own sake.

state: Before the coronavirus quarantine period, I had the opportunity to enjoy this wonderful and small bakery. They really have everything you could wish for. The staff was also very kind and helpful. It’s a bakery that can be taken away, with a constant stream of customers. They offer a variety of sweets, cakes, and sweet and salty treats. I chose the Oreo cheesecake (mmmm), and my girlfriend picked the pistachio cheesecake and macarons (all flavors, 12 units). We enjoyed our desserts and are really looking forward to going back! The only negative point is that there’s a huge variety of cookies, sweets, and bagels displayed on the counter, without any protection for customers who pass by and touch or talk about them. state: The Butterwood Bake Consortium is a wonderful place—exactly the kind of spot that Upper Lawrenceville needed. Just one year ago, there were no good places to have coffee, tea, or desserts other than on 52nd Street. With this option for desserts, coffee, and tea, plus the B52 Coffee nearby, the area now has everything it needs. I came here with a friend who wanted to try it out with me. I arrived a little early and was greeted by a friendly staff member. I ordered a strawberry vanilla vegan cake and asked about the tea options. She let me try different types of tea, and I chose mint tea—I thought it would go well with the cake. The walnut tea had an excellent aroma, and I plan to come back to try it with a dark chocolate cake. I sat at a Victorian-style garden-themed table, and my order was delivered in less than five minutes. The cake was warm, and the tea came with a small timer for preparation. Everything tasted delicious! At that moment, my friend arrived and chose a chocolate mousse and an espresso. She was also very satisfied with the quality of the dessert. I was offered more water for a second cup of tea, and we sat there and talked for over an hour, as the place became increasingly crowded and lively. (There was even a reading club!) I loved seeing how people were having fun. Eating sweets here will become a habit!

Nothing is cheap, but everything was delicious and tasted just as good as it does in NYC.

state: An excellent “daily life” bakery right in the heart of Little Italy. I stopped by in the middle of the afternoon after visiting the art museum. The place was still lively, but all the staff at the counter were very friendly. There was an irresistible offer, but I chose the “Napoleon” and a coffee au lait. Despite a little internal debate about moderation, I ended up eating almost the whole cake. It was wonderful—a bit different from the other “Napoleon” cakes I’ve tried before. Yes, I know what people say: I ate a French cake in an Italian bakery. My stomach knows no boundaries. But still, the layers of the cake were light and delicious. What’s interesting is that the cream layer was quite solid and creamy—not particularly elegant, but very tasty. It gave me the energy to walk from Murray Hill back to my neighborhood in Coventry. A must-visit in Little Italy.

state: MACARONS MACARONS MACARONS! When you're in Vegas, do yourself a favor and go to the Venetian and get yourself a box of these macarons (maybe even two boxes). They're $17.50 for a total of 6 macarons. It might be a little pricier than most but they are delicious! They got the texture pretty perfect. Delicate flaky outside and chewy inside. YUM! My favorite was the coffee flavor (which I usually don't like in macarons but this one was excellent)!! But I still think Euro Pane's salted caramel macaron is #1! I have yet to find one that beats that! although Chantilly comes close. But this is a very close tie for 2nd! Get it get it get it!

state: We stopped in at Presti's for the first time. Great selection and we looked forward to a great dessert. After taking a number we began the wait. There were approximately 8 customers in front of us so I expected a bit of a wait. After 35 minutes I was on the verge of walking out, as others had done. Although there were 4 employees there only 1 was helping customers. After ten minutes he left, went to the deli area, waited on 2 customers, chatted with them awhile and left the bakery customers waiting. One employee at the bakery counter was wrapping loaves of bread into bags for future sale, never thought to ask the group of customers if they needed help, just kept wrapping and ignored the group. Finally, made my selection, and walked out. The products were great but I would not go again. Amateurs all.

state: The neon sign and the window for the Milk Bar are easy to find on the second floor of the Cosmopolitan, right in front of the stairs and next to Momofuku. I’ve heard many opinions—“too sweet,” “overdone,” “perfect nostalgia,” etc.—and from my experience, we liked what we tried. Nothing was truly transformative—but still, I don’t necessarily want my life to be changed by a candy. The milk ice cream with cereal had the taste of milk with cereal, and the caramelized cornflakes on top were fun. The chocolate cake ice cream was really intense, like a thick, frozen chocolate cake. We tried the confetti cookie, the corn cookie, the compound cookie, the corn/marshmallow/chocolate cookie, and the chocolate/chocolate cookie. My favorite was the corn/marshmallow/chocolate cookie, because the combination of sweet, salty, soft, and crunchy flavors was perfectly balanced. Then there was the confetti cookie, which tasted like a delicious vanilla cake. The chocolate/chocolate and corn cookies were tasty at first, but eventually became forgettable. And the compound cookie was controversial—some didn’t like the coffee grains, while others had trouble with the unexpected crispy potato chip/pretzel pieces. Someone really enjoyed the pleasure of eating a cookie made from waste compost. Yes, the prices are high—the cookies cost $4 each.

state: I had the pleasure of visiting the LV Sprinkles Cupcakes & Ice Cream in April 2014, soon after they opened. It's always neat to see how each Sprinkles location differs, and this particular store just screamed "VEGAS," from its light-up signage to the attention-grabbing cupcake ATM. This was the first Sprinkles store that I had seen actually joined--cupcakes and ice cream were not separated--which was neat but also confusing. I think that, because the store had only recently opened, they were still trying to figure things out. I entered from the ice cream side, but I was directed to stand in the line for cupcakes (when I wanted ice cream, not cupcakes). Hopefully by now, the Vegas store has everything a little more under control, because with two entrances, it can be easy for customers to get confused/not know where to go when it comes time to order. I was surprised to see that I didn't have to wait in an enormously long line to order my ice cream (there was a line, but it moved along). I appreciated the fact that there was a good seating area outside the store for customers to enjoy their cupcakes and ice cream -- more seats and tables than I have ever seen at a Sprinkles store. I ordered the seasonal "Cookie Dough" ice cream flavor--one of my favorites; I wish it were a regular menu item--in the "Sprinkles Sundae," complete with my all-time favorite "Peanut Butter Chip" cupcake. I think because the workers were still getting into the groove of things at Sprinkles, the ice cream scoops were a bit larger than what I usually receive ... and hey, no complaints about that! The ice cream and cupcake quality were the same as I had experienced at other Sprinkles stores, which was great. However, I was a bit disappointed with the "Salted Oatmeal Cornflake" and "Peanut Butter Pretzel Chip" cookies that I ordered. Instead of the normal slightly crispy exterior and moist, soft interior, these cookies were on the harder, crunchier side, and the "Salted Oatmeal Cornflake" was definitely saltier than I would have liked. But, then again, gotta have some grace and patience because the store had just opened -- hopefully the cookies are a bit more consistent with the usual Sprinkles taste by now. The BF ordered the "Sprinkles Shake" with his usual combo of "Captain Crunch" ice cream and "Peanut Butter Chip" cupcake. The shake was as sweet as usual--I got a few sips in there--but we both noticed that the texture was also chunkier than usual. At one point, he had to use a spoon to get some of the larger cupcake chunks (definitely different from being able to inhale everything quickly with a straw). But he had no complaints--he said it was actually nice to munch on those cupcake bits every now and then. The friends we were with decided to share a "Sprinkles Shake" with "Red Velvet" ice cream and cupcakes (she really likes the "Red Velvet"). They were extremely pleased with their foray into Sprinkles and said they would definitely get the "Red Velvet"-heavy shake again (though, they were happy that they shared it, saying that it would have been too much red velvet for one person to handle). Overall, I had a positive experience at this LV Sprinkles. I really, really liked its dÃ©cor--the dazzling lights and huge marquee made it stand out from any other store I've been to so far--and the dÃ©cor really made the store easily spottable. I have no doubts that this location stays busy far into the night and keeps up with the Vegas nightlife. I do hope, though, for customers' sakes, that the ordering system is a bit more streamlined and organized to avoid confusion when entering/exiting the store.

state: Okay… what am I missing? All the positive reviews and the critic awards given by local newspapers for having a good ice cream made me decide to go there. There were several unusual flavors, as well as some classic ones. Maybe I should have chosen one of the classic flavors. Instead, I chose the truffle flavor, thinking it would be a delicious dessert. But when I tasted it, EWWWW!!! I asked what it was, and they told me it was made with truffle… but with mushrooms! I had no idea that someone could make ice cream with that. I needed something to clean my palate right away. I couldn’t get rid of that unpleasant taste. The girl behind the counter found it very amusing. I simply don’t understand the fuss around that place. I like to use fresh, local ingredients, so I prefer Crave or Udder Delights ice cream.

state: A wonderful place! Their tiramisu is delicious – we bought it for a friend’s birthday. The consistency is so creamy and dense that it feels like ice cream. The side dishes are made with fine, soft biscuits, and the dessert was absolutely delightful! A dessert served for about 6 people cost $30, which makes it more expensive than other smaller desserts, but definitely worth it. I also always order their coffee with milk; sometimes they add too much milk and little coffee, but at $2, it’s still a pleasant drink. The outdoor space is very nice, with a view of Mayfield and Murray Hill. The layout of the bakery allows plenty of natural light, and I can imagine coming here on a less busy day to read or just relax and enjoy the sunshine. Try also the bakery products at a discount! You can get muffins or croissants for just $1, if they’re from the previous day. They also have other discounted products, like crostata and chicken sandwiches.

state: My first experience with Donut Bar was at at Yelp event where I tried their pumpkin filled yeast donut and it was pretty disappointing. The dough wasn't as perfectly light as I like. And I really prefer for the entire donut to have a thick layer of glaze - this did not. Also, the filling was barely sweetened and basically tasted like butter. However, after brunch at eat. I figured I might as well stop by and give it another chance. This time I knew not to get a yeast donut and to try the cake instead. I went with one Strawberry Cream Cheese and one Apple Crumble. The latter was nice, but the Strawberry was even better because it was super sweet and flavorful. (In case you couldn't tell, I expect as much sugar as possible.) But both were moist on the inside (the Strawberry even had little juicy specks of red) and the outside had a nice thick glaze. I went on a Saturday and there was a line to the door that moved at a pretty decent speed. There was a big family behind me and I believe I heard someone behind the counter say that kids get a free donut on Saturdays. Pretty cool! Does my three month old count? Haha!

state: Finally, I had the opportunity to visit this famous establishment in Cleveland on my way back from a Greek religious festival in North Royalton. I also visited the Rocky River Metropolitan Park station recently. I tried the flavors of honey and pecan nuts, as well as mint chocolate—both were delicious. I would love to try the orange blossom flavor next time. I know people are very local and enjoy defending their own things, and they might even overestimate their favorite foods. Honey Hut falls into this category. Yes, the ice cream is really good, but is it truly the best in all of Cleveland and the Northeast of Ohio? For me, it’s on par with Mitchell’s (which I also like), but it’s far from the quality of some of the more “high-end” gourmet ice cream shops in Tremont. And definitely not on par with some of the amazing specialty ice cream shops I’ve visited along the coast of Jersey or in Miami. It’s really hard to be number one in any category, but Honey Hut produces ice cream of excellent quality that everyone can enjoy. If it’s been in business for 43 years, you absolutely should try it!

state: My friend wanted a rainbow cake and found Carlos Bakery, which had many photos showing various models. So she ordered one here. We were celebrating our children’s birthdays, which were on different days, and we thought it would be good to have cakes that were similar but different. So we also ordered one here. Although $50 for a small 15-cm cake was the maximum I paid, considering the quality and the chef’s reputation—which should be excellent—I was wrong! The cake looks nice and suitable for kids, but basically that’s all it is. It’s not much different from the cakes you can find in supermarkets or stores like Costco, but it costs three times more! It seems like I could have added sprinkles and a celebrity name and charged three times more! In short: the cake was dense, overly sweet, and dry. The last thing we need is for our kids to get even more upset, with lots of visits to the dentist, which would increase the cost of this cake. I’m very disappointed, considering the famous chef who made it. Maybe he needs to find another assistant or another bakery to represent him, because this doesn’t seem like a good choice. On the other hand, maybe the other cakes and treats are better, but with this expensive experience and the fact that it wasn’t even edible, we’re hesitant to try other options. For two small 15-cm cakes, half of each cake was left over, and the slices we ate were almost whole, which shows how bad it was for our party. No one liked it. In fact, even a 4-year-old didn’t like it, saying it wasn’t soft and moist enough, which is a problem. I’m surprised by the long line mentioned by other reviewers, because the price is too high and the quality doesn’t match the value. Sorry, but no. Thank you, but no.

state: This was the first time my boyfriend and I tried this. We have lived in Pittsburgh our whole lives and have heard good reviews. The menu had plenty of options and looked awesome. I was torn between the chocolate chip sundae and the chocolate dip cone. I decided to get the dip cone but they said they had no chocolate left. This was at 7pm. I then asked for the sundae and they also had no chocolate chip cookies left. Whaaat!? Ugh. So I got a regular vanilla brownie sundae. The sundae was mostly vanilla and had one small brownie and very little chocolate syrup. I asked to add cherries which tasted different to me as well. I can sadly say I was disappointed in my Visit here and am truly not a picky eater. I wish they had possibly put a sign on the window that they were out of these ingredients before people ordered. My boyfriend did say he enjoyed his dirt sundae though. I don't think I will be returning unfortunately.

state: I waited in a long line to get a latte on a cold day in Las Vegas. Was the wait worth it? YES! I tried a cake called Kouign Amann. It’s a croissant with a crispy, sweet crust, like caramelized. It was delicious! The latte was also excellent, and I ordered a simple croissant with butter. But Kouign Amann is what really stands out. Order it! My only complaint is that, in order to shorten the line and make service faster, the staff asks for orders far before the selection of frozen sandwiches and menu options are displayed on the board. Only the uncooled cakes are visible. People like me, who were customers for the first time, didn’t see the other options until it was time to pay. If I had seen those options, I would have ordered something else to try.

state: Finally, I got the chance to try Carlo’s Bakery in Las Vegas. In the past, there was always a long line whenever I passed by. I didn’t have the patience to wait. A few weeks ago, there was no line at all, and the bakery’s windows were filled with delicious desserts. I asked the young woman what were the two most popular items, and I bought them. She recommended “Lobster Tail” and “Cannoli”. However, I was a bit disappointed with both. I’ve tried these items several times on the East Coast. The versions from Carlo’s were good, but not as great as I expected. I was especially disappointed with the cannoli—they didn’t have a fresh taste. The dough had an old, stale flavor. I would go back to try more desserts if there wasn’t a long line. For me, it’s not worth waiting in such a long line based on this experience. I hope I get good results next time.

state: Every time I go to Las Vegas, it’s hard for me to resist the temptation to come here and buy one of their products. Everything looks so good! However, even though it’s difficult, I’ve decided to hold myself back. I plan to try their variety in moderation. That just means I’ll have to go back to Las Vegas again—great! So far, I’ve tried their Red Velvet cake, a vanilla macaron, and, of course, some TKOs. The Red Velvet cake was okay, but not the best I’ve tried. But the vanilla macaron is one of the best I’ve ever had. They have perfect textures and a well-balanced flavor profile. Not too subtle or overwhelming. Perfect! I really appreciate that. As for the TKOs, I can tell you exactly where I was when I tried one last time. That memory will stay with me forever. I had to stop walking to enjoy the moment. *Pauses to think…* In any case, the cream inside is a soft cloud of sweetness that blends perfectly with the delicious chocolate cookie. It’s essential to try it. As for the coffee, it’s good. Too sweet for my taste, but not bad. It’s not exceptional either. However, it doesn’t ruin the experience along with the delicious cakes here.

state: An apparent local institution and Tom Hanks recommended. The good: Classic frozen treat stand. Fresh, smooth custard (we saw a couple of the extruders working while waiting). Tons of flavor combinations with their snowstorms (mix in shakes or blizzards). Reasonable prices. The bad: While all three lines and drive through were open, the lines do take longer than I would think, even with what looked to be a full staff. While I appreciate that this is a tough job, with what propably seems like endless lines of hungry customers, I would have liked a bit more friendliness from our stereotypical surly teenager. The unknown: Perhaps I ordered wrong, but while delicious, my turtle sundae seemed a little light on the custard. I was left with quite a bit of hard chocolate/nutty shell and had to steal some spoons of custard from Cheddartarian's double custard root beer float. The other treats ordered by earlier guests looked quite a bit more generous. Ultimately, I would go back though, and that is as good a measure as anything.

state: The staff is quick and efficient. The store is lovely. Their skills in making fondant for cakes are incredible. HOWEVER, everything may seem delicious, but the taste is disappointing. We waited in line for about 25 minutes and were really disappointed. We bought: a yellow cupcake with butter frosting – the cake was dry, and the frosting had no flavor. A “pouf” of cream – the cream inside also lacked flavor and tasted like overcooked eggs. The dough part wasn’t even crunchy at all. A strawberry shortcake – besides the strawberries, I threw the plate away. The cake was again dry, and the custard was watery. A cookie with sparkles – it was okay. Nothing worth waiting half an hour for. We threw away most of the products because they were very tasteless. If you’re going to eat something that isn’t healthy, every bite must be really good. This wasn’t the case. Moreover, the prices are high, and the place is crowded, although unfortunately, the cakes don’t live up to expectations.

I decided to try the “ICED CEREAL MILK LATTE” and it was delicious! The staff member confirmed that it wasn’t too sweet, and she was right. It wasn’t overly sweet, but it had an incredibly delicious taste with a slight hint of cereal milk. It was so good that I wanted to go back the next day to try another one, this time in a larger size.

state: This place must be one of my favorite spots to eat ice cream! In fact, in Chicago (my hometown), I tried a donut filled with vanilla ice cream and chopped fruits. I was absolutely thrilled! I searched for a long time, and finally found this amazing place! I have to say that, besides being delicious, the staff are the most wonderful people I’ve ever met! They have a lovely personality and are very friendly. For me, it’s a great advantage when there’s excellent food and amazing people who make the experience even better! The parking space is quite small, like most places in the city center. I always manage to find a spot, even when it’s very crowded (and they are really crowded!!!). They have an outdoor area with a pleasant space where you can enjoy your food! The interior is very small, but it’s definitely worth it! I must visit Novel Ice Cream!

state: I visited Handel’s for the first time with a group of friends a very long time ago, when Kauai Cafe was still in this square. I didn’t even know it was a ice cream place, just from the service window. That’s how they keep the place clean—without having a busy storefront. It’s a smart strategy, I guess. They have a wide variety of options: cones, ice cream desserts, smoothies, “hurricanes,” etc. There are many flavors to choose from, but I decided to try the Oreo flavor instead. Actually, it wasn’t anything special. I’m satisfied with my “Dreyer’s Cookies ‘N Cream” ice cream at home. Anyway, I haven’t been here for a while, since I’m a fan of Thrifty’s ice cream at Sweet Addiction. When I came back here for the second time, I ordered the “Raspberry Sherbet Parfait” because it looked good in the photos. Wow, it was delicious! I can hardly remember the last time I ate such great sherbet. But that’s why I keep coming back. However, the amount you get may vary depending on the employee who prepares it. Sometimes, the portions are large and filling, and other times, they’re just small. The lines can be long during summer. Maybe I’ll try other flavors in the future, but for now, I’m definitely a fan of their “Sherbet”!

state: Everyone who knows me knows my love for ice cream! Today was my first time trying ice cream in Arizona...I am usually very picky so it took me a long time and searching on yelp to find something that would catch my eye and attract my taste buds. I found Churn on Yelp and decided to try it out. This place was amazing!! I was happily greeted by two wonderful employees. Sebastian has such a great amount of energy and was so kind, I was so happy to be there just for his energy itself! The store was set up as a beautiful candy shop that will catch the eye of any child, adult or senior citizen. The music is very bubbly and exciting! I was very indecisive of what to get, after reviewing pictures on Yelp I decided to get either a sundae or a cookie ice cream. I asked Sebastian between the two which was the best and his eyes lit up of excitement and passion as he said the icecream cookie! I told him which ice cream I wanted and told him to pick out everything himself on which he feels would be best. He did not steer me wrong at all! He gave me a tasteful girl scout cookie ice cream with peanut butter cookies and chocolate sprinkles. This was by far thee most amazing I have ever had thus far! I am astonished about the service, food, and everything! It is def a must go for anyone who enjoys the sweeter things in life!

state: This place really impressed me. At first, I was skeptical because it looked too much like a small business, but I was pleasantly surprised. The owners of the store treated us very kindly and helpfully. They told us the whole story and how they make ice cream in small quantities, using one of the best ice cream manufacturers in the United States. They also mentioned that their donuts were ranked among the top 50 in the U.S. Both deserve all the praise. All the ice cream was more creamy and tasty than anything I’ve ever tasted before. And the donuts! The best I’ve ever had, and probably the best I’ll ever have. I don’t like donuts that are too sweet or have too much frosting. This was a perfect combination of sweet and salty flavors, as well as texture. We’ll be back!

state: Those who say that Bouchon’s macarons are great clearly know nothing about macarons at all. I consider myself a macaron enthusiast; I discovered these desserts while I was in Paris a few years ago. The Bouchon macarons are awful. They’re too big, too dense, and “chewy,” and they’re also excessively cold. They weren’t fresh or delicate at all. Even though they don’t meet the standards of Pierre Hermé or Ladurée, they still fall far behind other places in New York, San Francisco, and Vancouver. Usually, we enjoy every bite, but at Bouchon, we didn’t even want to finish them. It was a tough job. And, besides, it’s very expensive. The only reason I give them two stars is because the “TKO” (a type of adult Oreo cookie) was good.

state: My wife and I were in Las Vegas a month ago, and we stopped at Milk Bar at the Cosmo hotel. As expected, it was quite busy, but the line moved quickly. We ordered a single serving of fruit-flavored ice cream (inspired by “fruity pebbles”) – essentially creamy ice cream with a fruit flavor. Personally, I loved the taste and the cereal coating on the edges (corn flakes, which was an extra). The next day, we also tried the birthday pudding drink; it was delicious, but very sweet – I couldn’t finish it! The birthday cake is filled with chips, cake pieces, and cereal milk. I still really want to go back to Milk Bar, and I’m very grateful that my wife convinced me to go.

state: Man oh man. if I wasn't won over by their huge following and excellent cupcakes made with natural ingredients, I was definitely won over by the limited edition Batman cupcakes that they had last Saturday. The staff was so friendly when I called in to see if they had anymore, they even went ahead and made me a couple extra with the left over decorations they had in stock. I loved them for that reason. Well and because their cupcakes are awesome. Their location in Las Vegas is touristy, mostly because it is at the Linq hotel and casino right in their promenade. Mostly.Mostly tourists are going here but sometimes they have locals around or local specials so you need to check. Also they have different flavors on different days, so if you are seeking a special flavor make sure to call first for availability. For example on Monday they have strawberry, but on Tuesday they have banana, but not strawberry, on Wednesday they have a limited edition pumpkin spice BUT no banana, and so on. You get the idea. Parking is easy here, plus it is free and close by to the promenade. They are open long hours and the inside smells delicious and is super clean! I love this place I'll be back for sure!!!

state: Mmmmm. I was very excited to see Bouchon Bakery on my way to my room at the Venetian. I didn’t expect the prices to be so bad, considering it’s in a touristy area of a touristy city, and they offer high-quality, authentic French desserts and food. I’ve seen much worse food at similar prices in Las Vegas. During my stay, I tried the chocolate pudding (three layers of different flavors, creamy and delicious, and just the right size for a snack), a raspberry macaron (a little too sweet, but very soft), a chocolate bread (crispy and delicious, with just the right amount of soft chocolate pieces), and a carrot cake cookie (two huge, very soft cookies that look like a cake, with a delicious cream cheese frosting). The service was good, quite fast, and not pretentious; in fact, it was the opposite—a woman who helped me said everything wrong—“macaRON,” not “macaROON”. Plus, extra points for the fake disposable utensils that look exactly like the real ones. Very elegant, Thomas Keller.

It was sweet, but not too much, and the chocolate had a delicious flavor, but not too bitter. I’ll spend the rest of my life wondering if this is the best cookie I’ve ever had.

The café is decorated according to the seasonal events, so it’s definitely a great place for beautiful Instagram photos, as well as for trying desserts made with high-quality matcha! I would definitely recommend this place to anyone!

state: If you like cupcakes, this is the place for you. If you don't, this place will change your mind! It's located on the street on the way to the High Roller. It's small inside with a line on the left for cupcakes and the right for ice cream. There probably will be a small line especially for the cupcakes. The cupcakes are displayed on very upscale looking wooden shelves. They have a decent selection of flavors. Having tried a few I can say you cannot go to wrong with any of them. The peanut butter is one of my favorites. These are American-style, so expect a very thick layer of buttercream icing that is sweet along with a fairly dense though moist cake. For a bit of extra fun try their cupcake ATM outside available 24/7 for your cupcake cravings. Choose from the touchscreen, and the machine delivers a boxed cupcake. Cool! We tried the ice cream too (Rocky Road for me). It was ok but nothing too amazing. The cupcakes are the highlight here.

state: I really don’t want to give this place a perfect rating, but the staff/owners need to know that some of their employees are dishonest! I have a 2-year-old son who loves ice cream, but he’s not ready for regular cones yet, so “baby” ice cream is perfect for him. He loves the vanilla flavor, and the amount is just right. Every time my family goes there, we order this ice cream for him, and there are no problems. But today, we were served by a teenager—maybe in his early 20s—who refused to give it to him. He said, “Baby ice cream is only for babies! He wants ice cream, so he needs a normal size!” I’m sorry, but is it really true that only babies can get small ice cream? It wasn’t just about the price; I know they offer small ice cream for free, but if it were important, we would pay for it, because it’s the right size for him. But that guy just refused! I don’t know if he was trying to make money or thinking we were taking advantage of him, but it left me with a bad taste in my mouth! My family really likes this place. The ice cream is always good and perfect for any hot summer day in Las Vegas! So, the store itself deserves 5 stars. Most of the employees we’ve met in the past are genuinely nice and seem to enjoy what they do, unlike that guy who unfortunately had to be dealt with today!

state: I went to try out the “Strawberry Split”. The last time we went there, just before closing time, they didn’t have much left. I entered and was glad to see the “Strawberry Split”! It was huge. My husband ordered the “Expresso Chocolate”, while my friend, who is a chocolate enthusiast, chose the “Triple Chocolate Threat” after being disappointed not to get the “Chocolate Euphoria” that day. Both of them had cake donuts, and we thought they weren’t particularly special. My friend said that the “Chocolate Threat” wasn’t even enough chocolatey, and I agree. I came for the “Strawberry” and wasn’t disappointed. The donut has a slightly hard crust, like a croissant. I would prefer one with a softer crust, but my husband and my friend liked the crust as it was. My husband also said it reminded him of a Chinese birthday cake. I was satisfied with what I had expected… months or even years ago…

state: If you’re in the Venetian area, near the elevator entrance of the hotel, then Bouchon Bakery is a must-visit place to start your day. There’s usually a long line, but service is quite fast. Whether you want macarons, baguettes, or coffee, Bouchon Bakery makes the wait worth it. I usually order small portions because I’m always busy, and that’s exactly why this place is famous for that. You won’t get a full French meal here, but there’s a Bouchon location where you can eat. In any case, the service is reliable, fast, and friendly. Like everything about French cuisine, the quality is excellent, and the prices are relatively high. It’s only open until 2 p.m., so come early to enjoy the treats and satisfy your pastry cravings.

state: Although I have never tried any of the delicious desserts they offer, Amelie’s provides an excellent experience as a bakery and coffee shop. The Wi-Fi is good, and it’s usually possible to find an outlet nearby if needed. The staff are usually young, and sometimes they may seem a bit late (but maybe they’re just shy or confused). The atmosphere is modern and spacious; the coffee is good, and if they can keep the baristas committed, there’s also hope for espresso drinks. After spending time and money in Parisian bakeries many times over the years, Amelie’s seems a bit expensive compared to other bakeries. However, since it’s rare in Charlotte, it seems there’s a supply-and-demand dynamic that makes the cost justified.

I would definitely come back here if I were ever in town, but alas, I live 2,600 miles away.

state: They were extremely crowded on a 3 PM Friday afternoon how to draw a number to get service ended up getting quite a selection as there are a lot of items to choose from. Staff is very friendly. got the chocolate walnut hazelnut cake the pistachio chocolate cake, cannoli cake, Napoleon, German chocolate cake,cappuccino brownie and the lemon coconut cake. to be totally honest none of them were good they werent offensively bad per se but lacked flavor. my main issue was with the Napoleon, as this is my favorite dessert. this was literally not a Napoleon. it had the traditional Napoleon topping but then the body of it was chocolate mousse and with a very very thin layer of cream and phyllo. so that was a huge disappointment. the other cakes also didn't taste like what they were advertised to especially the pistachio cake and just in general weren't very good they all had the mousse and maybe it's a personal issue I have with mousse. The German chocolate cake also just wasn't very sweet and the cappuccino brownie we a-likened to a Costco brownie it just honestly to me tasted like Betty Crocker- it did not taste special and it did not have a coffee flavor at all. I feel bad being so critical because it was a really beautiful store and the desserts are all very aesthetic but I just don't think it was worth it especially for the price which ended up being about $36. The quality was like a grocery store.

state: So, my evaluation is based on the coffee. When I was in Las Vegas with my husband, we tried to avoid Starbucks cafes, because they were actually more expensive than those in New York. Most of the time, I’m the first to wake up, so one morning when I went from the IT room to the Venetian to get some coffee, I found this place. The desserts seemed great, but I can’t really describe them, since I’ve never tried any. The coffee was good, and the staff were friendly. The bakery itself is quite small, at least the one I visited. There isn’t much space to sit, so you just take your order and go outside or back to your hotel room. In the morning, there was a smelly man sitting in the lobby area of the Venetian bridge/promenade, right in front of Bouchon. So, if he’s still there, I definitely recommend taking your order and leaving.

state: The coffee was good; I ordered a coffee with milk, so I can’t criticize much. The variety of foods is excellent! I was very impressed by the gluten-free options! The gluten-free cakes were great for breakfast, and I brought some macarons along for the trip. The texture of the macarons is a bit airy (you need to press them on a baking sheet before baking), and they use a lot of colorant, but they’re delicious and tasty. In terms of the atmosphere, this place is fantastic. The decor is beautiful and charming, and at 5 a.m., it was quiet. But I imagine it would be the perfect place to chat or work, especially since it’s open 24 hours a day! The staff at the counter were friendly and helpful with all my questions about gluten-free options. If I weren’t away from home, I would definitely come back here.

state: My son and I stopped in this late evening for a sweet treat after attending the Phoenix Symphony. I checked Yelp for nearby places and stumbled on Novel. You can see all the fresh donuts and the gentleman that helped us (sorry, can't remember his name!) offered us samples of anything we'd like to try. We'll be back again! Parking sucks, but it's downtown Phoenix so it comes with the territory.

state: We paid our second visi to this location of Sprinkles yesterday, and I guess I'm a fan! Service was young, sweet, and eager to please while it was surprisingly slow yesterday. We stopped in at around 8:30 after a ride on the high roller and picked up a chai cupcake, lemon coconut, vegan red velet, and vanilla minis. The minis are so cute and perfect for kids if you don't want them bouncing off the walls from the sugar. My favorite was the lemon coconut of our selection, although the chai was also quite tasty with its strong chai spices. Vegan red velvet is made with coconut oil and my friend (who is vegan) said it was very moist and delicious. I'd say the Sprinkles here are up to par with the locations I've visited in California with the exception of one thing: I have yet to see the SALTED CARAMEL cupcake at this location. Salted caramel is hands down, the best Sprinkles cupcake flavor ever, so please carry it soon. Thanks!

state: I’m very happy that there’s finally a bakery offering 85 cents per loaf of bread here in Las Vegas. I no longer have to drive all the way to southern California just to get “fresh bread”. This bakery is much smaller than those I’ve visited before. The quality of the bread and the iced coffee with sea salt is just as good as those from other bakeries. Please keep it this way! I give it a 3-star rating due to their lack of efficiency in managing inventory and queue control, as well as their “no ice” policy for drinks. Inventory: The shelves usually have one or two loaves of bread, or they’re empty. But you can see a shelf full of cold bread in a corner. I suggest assigning someone else to deliver those loaves of bread. Queue control: This store has been open for 2–3 months now, yet there’s still a long queue, and most of the time, it’s outside the store. I understand. Everyone in Las Vegas wants their bread. Once, I went there on Tuesday night around 8 p.m., thinking I could avoid the long queue. Well, I managed to avoid the queue for buying bread. But the queue for paying was long, and it took a lot of time. There were only 2 cashiers when there were more than 20 people in line. They definitely need more help: assign another cashier or someone to pack the bread, so the payment process can be faster.

state: I want to be completely honest: I am a celiac. I don’t eat donuts. However, my husband and most of my friends really like donuts. No, don’t feel sorry for me (okay, maybe a little!). state: I LOVE SPRINKLES CUPCAKES AND ICE CREAM! Living in California, I've had the luck of being near several locations so I was pretty excited when they opened another one in Vegas. This one is a combo of both cupcakes and ice cream, yay! They're connected so if you can't decide like me, you can easily view the goodies in both stores. Their cupcakes are always delicious! I've had the Black and White, Red Velvet (both sugar and sugar free), Peanut Butter, Smores, Margarita, Carrot, and Dark Chocolate at various visits. Their Margarita cupcake (made for a limited time during Cinco de Mayo) is the only one I haven't throughly enjoyed to the very last crumb. I decided on ice cream this time. Sprinkles makes their own ice cream and allows you to have it alone, in one of their delicious waffle cones (regular or red velvet), cookie sandwiches, cupcake top sandwiches, and a number of unique toppings. The cupcake top sandwich is bomb, as you can choose two different of the day's flavors, but I opted for some dark chocolate ice cream sprinkled with red velvet cupcake crumbs. So good, as the woman who helped me agreed! Sprinkles is a famous brand, so the cupcakes and ice cream combos are more than the average similar establishments, but for the occasional treat I think it's more than worth it!

state: While I was in Paris, my boyfriend was in Las Vegas...oddly enough in the fake Paris hotel...you can guess who won the battle of emailing Eiffel Tower pictures. I decided he too needed to smuggle baked goods in his luggage. I think he did a better job than me. I only asked for bouchons, but I was also given a chocolate tart. I think my heart stopped for a couple seconds while eating it, and I'm not sure if it's because I shouldn't have eaten the whole thing by myself or because it tasted of chocolate heaven. Even though it had been in the freezer for a couple days, it was still pretty damn amazing. The bouchons were just not that amazing in retrospect after the tart. They were good, but I can make a glorified brownie too if necessary. I am far too lazy for a tart. I would eat everything again though, and then some more, don't get me wrong.

state: After hearing so many good things about Carlo’s Bake Shop from my friends, I decided it was something I really wanted to try in Las Vegas. Some people play games, others drink – I like eating. Carbs aren’t part of vacationing, right? This review is from someone who doesn’t watch “Cake Boss”. Although I love cooking shows and food competitions (Food Network is my favorite), I never really became interested in “Cake Boss”. My friends always talk a lot about the show and baking, so I decided I needed to find out why. After wandering around the shops at Venetian Canal Shops and following the signs toward the bakery (and the Buddy V’s nearby), I finally found the hallway, which was quite crowded with people. In some Yelp photos, it looks chaotic – but maybe I was lucky, because it wasn’t that bad. There was a line, and it took about 15 minutes to get to the front. There was someone watching the line, which was good, as they really prevented people from cutting in line. The line was in front of the kitchen, where you could see the bakers decorating the cakes. At that time, they were making cannoli towers. They looked great, so I was already convinced! I had to pick one up. As soon as you enter the bakery and place your order, there’s a rush of people looking at the displays, trying to decide what to buy. The person in front of me kept coming and going, trying to decide which cookies to buy. I think a menu with photos of the available products would be great here! It would be useful to have a menu, so that when you reach the front of the line, you know exactly what you want to order. There were no lobster dishes on display, so I chose a box of Christmas cookies, which were already wrapped up, along with some cookies and a cannoli tower. My order cost around $40. $40 and an hour later, the only thing I could think about was “meh”. It didn’t live up to expectations. The cannoli tower was okay, but I felt it was a bit soggy and not as flavorful as I expected. The cookies were good, but it wasn’t something I would expect to get back in line for again. The box of cookies was a gift, but the person who received it opened it after dinner, and we tried one of the butter cookies – it was good. Definitely not as flavorful as other butter cookies I’ve tried in less famous bakeries. If you’re a fan of the show, I understand why you’d come here. But if you’re like me and just want a good cannoli, I’ll keep looking.

state: I love this restaurant. I’m a confectioner, and I discovered this place because it’s close to my home, in the fun area of NODA. I just fell in love with it right away. I really liked the decor, the variety of products, and the beautiful display with all those delicious items. They have excellent fruit teas and drinks, along with very special and artistic lighting. I tried many things here—crunchy croissants, mini fruit cakes, and more. I also love the small tea cakes, chocolate cakes, and always buy macarons in various flavors, colors, and varieties. It’s exciting and diverse. They offer a range of meals, from fresh and creative salads to what they call “Tartines” – open sandwiches. My favorite is fig cake with bacon and brie. I can’t count how many times I ordered a full portion and ate everything at once. Every time I go there, I enjoy everything I order and always try something new from the display. The only problem for me is that if you don’t arrive at the right time, the line might be 20 people or more. Although they have a decent staff, it’s not enough to handle such long lines. But you can enter and leave with good service, excellent food, and many things to enjoy. They have tables inside and outside, and they offer everything to take away. The containers are well-designed so that your food arrives safely and with great taste at home. I would recommend this restaurant to anyone who doesn’t want to control their calories, who loves sweets, and who wants to try new flavors and tastes. Again, it’s a popular place, and there are other places to visit. A new restaurant is coming soon, and they call it their “main store”. I can’t wait to visit it!

state: This is the only reason to go to Las Vegas. Who cares about the bright lights, the big buildings, when you can eat delicious ice cream!?!? I went here on a Friday night around 7:30 PM. There were four people working and the line was into the street. However, the line move fairly quickly and even if it was longer I would've waited. I decided on a fourth Cooper sampler which is by and large the best option on the menu. I had blueberry cobbler, chocolate marshmallow, banana cream pie and Keylime pie. The person who took my order was knowledgeable about all of the ice cream's and knew what was in each of them. I like the banana cream pie ice cream the best followed by the Keylime pie followed by the blueberry cobbler and chocolate marshmallow tied. I also thought that the four items sampler was super affordable based on how delicious it was and how much ice cream there with us. There is no reason to ever go to Las Vegas and not stop here for ice cream even if it is a little bit out-of-the-way. The only other tip is to my knowledge there are no bathrooms and there isn't much seating outside so that could be a challenge.

state: TIP: They have an upstairs and downstairs location! Had to say that first because I waited in line downstairs for like 15 minutes. I was heading to Treasure Island so I took the elevator next to Bouchon and found they had another bakery counter upstairs with no line. Anyways, I love love love their macarons. So far it's a tie between the pistachio and salted caramel. They are a little pricey ($5 each) but they're about 2.5x the size of a normal macaron and they're just amazing. My second favorite thing to get here is a vanilla chai latte, goes perfect with a macaron :D. Coffee prices are comparable to starbucks. Sad to say I actually haven't tried anything else here. I really have only been able to come here while taking a long walk on the strip. Again, sad to say I don't ever stay the Venetian hotel where it would be much more convenient.

state: I’ve been here since the opening, and I can say that everything is fine. The bakery has its ups and downs, depending on which day you visit. The variety of breads is limited, and most items run out quickly whenever I come here. I’m a fan of fruit cakes, and the red fruit cake they serve here is good. The last time I visited, I was impressed by the strawberry cold tea—since I usually avoid trying other places’ cold teas. I’m afraid it might taste like Nesquik! (laughs) Surprisingly, this tea hit the mark. It contains pieces of strawberries, which is a bonus. As for the other teas with milk, honestly, they just taste like milk with cream, which isn’t my favorite. Additionally, one of my favorite teas is cold coffee with sea salt! I recommend it to anyone who loves coffee—it’s not very strong; it’s simply the perfect cold coffee for daily use, with a touch of sea salt cream. If it’s hot, I recommend trying the green grapefruit cold tea! This place deserves 3 stars.

state: Wow, I’m in love! I really like that Las Vegas has such a place. It reminds me of something you might find in a smaller town along the East Coast. I love these small ice cream spots. The best offer is the four-flavor tasting – you get four servings of ice cream for just $4.25! What a deal! I bought this and tried the cookie with chocolate chips, pistachio, chocolate with peanut butter, and another flavor with peanut butter too… but I can’t remember the name! (Oh, sorry!) I really liked the pistachio flavor; it’s definitely one of my favorite flavors. This place doesn’t have any indoor space, so be prepared to wait outside. It can also be very crowded – the last time I went, I had to wait over half an hour. It would be great if they had more staff to serve all the people, since last time there were only two people working.

state: I was really excited to try the Milk Bar. I watched a program called “The Mind of a Chef” some time ago, and the parts with Christina Tosi were my favorites. We don’t have a Milk Bar here in Vancouver, so when I heard there was one in Las Vegas, I told my sister that we should go there before leaving to buy some cookies to take home. My sister and I made a special stop at the Cosmopolitan just for them. I bought each type of cookie: compound cookie, cream cheese with raspberries, corn marshmallow with chocolate, double chocolate cookie, and corn cookie. They weren’t cheap, and considering the exchange rate, they were even more expensive. So, I had high expectations. However, I felt a little nervous when I saw them packaged neatly but not baked on site, but I hoped for the best. Unfortunately, I was disappointed. I shared the cookies with my husband and parents. Among all the cookies, the compound cookie was my favorite, but it wasn’t anything special. Maybe it’s because I expected some crunch from the pretzel and cornstarch pieces, but there was almost no crunch at all. The second cookie I liked the most was the corn one, but I would have preferred a stronger corn flavor and maybe some texture from corn flour. The raspberry cookie was okay. It was soft, which was good, but it just tasted very sweet, and the raspberries seemed artificial to me (we have plenty of fresh raspberries throughout summer). The double chocolate cookie didn’t appeal to me at all. I already know the recipe from Tartine Bakery for rye chocolate cookies with salted chocolate. It’s a great chocolate cookie. This cookie didn’t have any deep flavor; it just tasted like cocoa with a bitter taste that couldn’t be removed from my mouth. The corn marshmallow with chocolate was good. The corn added some crunch, and the marshmallows reminded me of my childhood, because they had a flavor similar to those found in cereal. Who knows… maybe if they were baked fresh, right out of the oven, the story would be different. But unfortunately, the taste didn’t meet expectations (or the price).

state: I’m a huge fan of Mason’s Creamery! I love that they offer a variety of unique flavors that are different from the usual ones. I always enjoy visiting to try new flavors. I really liked the berry ice cream—it has a subtle sweet and creamy taste. The last time I went there, I tried the salty caramel ice cream: it isn’t too fancy, but I couldn’t resist the salty flavor that contrasts with the sweetness of the caramel. It’s one of my favorite items. I also saw on Facebook that they sometimes have a temporary ramen shop. I haven’t been there yet, but I’ve heard mixed opinions from friends who have visited. I would love to try it when it’s available. The atmosphere at this place is charming and modern. It’s a small ice cream shop with many outdoor seats. I noticed they’ve set up a area at the back with long tables under a canopy with nice lights. I also really like the plastic spoons they use to serve the ice cream—they change color depending on the temperature!

state: Summary: The food is excellent, and the coffee was delicious. However, the customer experience and waiting time are terrible. I went here with some friends—each of us ordered a coffee, a sandwich, and some desserts. The desserts were served right when we ordered them, since they had just come out of the oven, which makes sense. The coffees we ordered were also great. But when the barista delivered them one by one, she mixed up three of them, saying “this is caramel, no milk,” when in fact they contained milk. In the end, after a bit of “coffee game,” we all managed to figure out which ones were which. All the items we ordered were very tasty, including the grilled meat sandwich, the chicken sandwich with dried tomatoes, a sausage sandwich, egg and cheese sandwich, and a bacon quiche. However, we actually waited about 40 minutes for the food to be prepared. Additionally, since there are no tables due to the pandemic, there are no seats inside. If it’s obvious that people are waiting in line, there should be some kind of notification system, like a tap or message, so you’re informed when your food is ready. This would help improve the overall customer experience, and during the pandemic, it would also reduce the time people spend in a small space waiting to be called.

state: Ironic that I'm giving Bouchon BAKERY such high marks, considering I am NOT a fan of Bouchon restaurant (eaten there twice and not impressed nor satisfied both times). I have yet to try the MUCH reviewed macarons here. However, this is what I have tried: 1. Strawberry croissant...AWESOME. Fresh made strawberry jam inside a buttery, flaky croissant that's dusted with confectioner's sugar.. Not TOO sweet IMO and OH SO enjoyable. 2. Chocoloate Bouchon...Imagine the best brownie you ever ate, but more moist and less dense; then add some semi sweet chocolate chips in the middle, dust it off with some confectioner's sugar and you have a chocolate Bouchon. They clearly used a very high quality dark chocolate, could be a Valrhona 60%+ dark baking chocolate. Who knows? But I do know that I will be buying more of these bit sized treats. 3. Almond Brioche...The edges have a slightly stale and burnt taste to them. While some may prefer this texture and flavor combination, I did not. After discarding the edges, I was left with an amazing piece of soft and moist brioche bread with a wonderful almond paste and sliced almonds. I thoroughly enjoyed it. 4. Pretzel sticks...Personally, I love pretzels and pretzel bread. So while this was nothing special, I still enjoyed it quite a bit. If I could take it home and heat it up in the oven and dip it in some great mustard or cheese dip...then it would be GREAT! There are still many things I plan to try soon, will update this as I try them.

state: Any shopping trip needs a place like Eataly. La Pasticceria is the dessert section, offering options like tiramisu, fruit cakes, and cannoli. I went there on my last day in Las Vegas to have a coffee, as I was very tired. All coffee drinks were available hot or cold, and there were three different sizes. In terms of price, it was slightly more expensive than Starbucks—a cold coffee in the smallest size cost $4.90 (before taxes). However, the quality was excellent: strong, smooth, and creamy. Additionally, they had paper straws available. Las Vegas still falls short in terms of conservation efforts (no recycling), so paper straws are a positive step.

state: Don't hate me but I much prefer a cookie or a brownie over a cupcake but I have to tell you right now that if I must have a cupcake...I'm going to Sprinkles. Luckily there is a location in Chicago!!! When I woke up on my first morning in Vegas, I saw the new High Roller Ferris Wheel and thought it was the coolest thing I have seen on the strip in a long time! My colleague and I were looking for something to do after dinner one night and he suggested the new Ferris wheel. I didn't really realize the shear size of it until I got closer. I think it was about half way down the Linq right around Sprinkles. I made a mental note of the place on our way to the Ferris wheel and after our insane ride up there, I needed a little something sweet to nibble on so I suggested we stop at Sprinkles on our way back. He had already eaten dessert so I was on my own, but didn't hesitate to walk in here to explore what they have to offer. I noticed an array of ice cream flavors and the line out the door for the ice cream and I jumped in line for a cupcake. I glanced at what they had left and since I couldn't decide what to order, I went for the classic Black & White....a chocolate cupcake with vanilla icing and chocolate sprinkles. I asked for it to-go and received it in a brown bag with a wooden fork attached with a sticker. It was adorable!! I actually had to take a photo on site. The girls behind the counter were just as sweet as can be. They were so kind and friendly. These are the kind of customer service people that belong in a cupcake shop!! All smiles, giggles and they knew cupcakes!! Trust me, I quizzed them. ;) I also grabbed a bottle of water while I was there and my total was about $5 or so. Not bad for a quick snack on the strip! When I got back to my hotel room, I ate my cupcake in bed like a little kid. It was delicious. Very fresh, but there was a slight bit too much frosting, if I have one complaint. I will definitely hit up the cupcake ATM in Chicago next time we're in the city. I have heard all about it from friends and now that I have experienced Sprinkles, I gotta take the hubs!

state: I was very underwhelmed with my latest purchase from Page. The Hot Nancy B - a great concept with warm chocolate chip cookies, hot fudge, ice cream, and whipped cream - suffered greatly from a lack of execution in three of the four components. Page continues to have the best texture of soft serve ice cream around, hands down. The flavor and sweetness were lacking which provided a very weak base for the rest of the sundae. The fudge, although deep and luxurious in appearance, again lacked flavor... it's amazing what a little salt and sugar could do to transform this into something great. The whipped cream is left unsweetened... this is a great concept to contrast a sundae that is exceptionally sweet, but in this application it simply fell flat. The cookies were far and away the best component... a thick and crispy exterior with large, melting gobs of chocolate inside and a balanced sweetness to contrast the thick, velvety ice cream. This will not prevent me from returning, but I hope the next time is a bit more satisfying.

state: I’ve heard many things about how good their cookies are, thanks to my friends who enjoy baking. So I was excited when I found the cookie and ice cream stand while strolling along the Strip. The ice cream was very tempting, but it wasn’t an option, as dinner was less than an hour away. However, the staff here were very kind and even offered me a sample. The ice cream was definitely delicious, but also a bit expensive. I decided to buy some cookies since I could take them with me. I bought a compost cookie, a cornflake cookie, chocolate cookie, and a raisin and cream cookie. Keep in mind that cookies are cheaper if you buy 3 or more (3 for $3 or 3 for $8)! The compost cookie was my favorite of the three. Sweet and salty, with many different textures and flavors in just one cookie. Delicious! My wife preferred the cornflake, chocolate, and raisin cookie. Both of us thought the raisin and cream cookie was a little too creamy and not as flavorful as the other two, in our opinion.

state: Always loved going to their San Diego location when I lived there. Perfect place to grab pastries for any gathering. All their pastries are made fresh (fresh bread!!!) and kept in display boxes for you to grab with tongs. My favorite things to grab there are the ube breads, chocolate, and their hot dog rolls. Sorry I'm not sure of the exact names but it's pretty self explanatory. They do have a selection of drinks as well to help wash down all their delicacies. Unfortunately the location they are at in China town smells of fresh sewage which severely takes away from the sweet aromas that should engulf you when you walk home. Other then that, some of the workers are a bit rude, even the supervisor (it says so on her badge) gave me attitude because I couldn't hear her through her mask. #covidperks other then that, I'll still come here when I'm in the area to treat myself to a few pastries and try not to over do it.

I’ve had negative experiences with other establishments due to my reviews, but I haven’t had any negative experiences with them. And I would like to keep this situation the same. If they serve something that isn’t good, they correct it. They try their best to do a good job. I understand that it’s homemade and served on the spot, so not all products can be perfectly identical. But it’s frustrating to buy a pot or jar of food, get home, and find out that it’s not what you expected. The overall rating of 4.5 stars shows that many people are satisfied, so take my review with a grain of salt. If the taste seems appealing, give it a try (especially on Tuesday), and you’ll probably like it. This review reflects only my impressions – it shouldn’t carry more weight than the numerous 5-star reviews for this place.

state: I've received a few recommendations from friends about this spot! It's close to my home but slightly off the main Central shopping area. You'll see it on the other side of hwy 74. The shop itself is small, cute, and smells incredible! Park in the open gravel lot and enjoy your pastries on the picnic tables, no inside seating. The employees were helpful when I shared it was my first time and wanted to try the "favorites". They recommended the tiramisu, lemon bar, s'mores bar, or slice of cheesecake. There was cookies, puff pastries filled with cream, brownies, macarons, and more! I wanted everything. The lemon bar was great, the s'mores bar was del delicious, and the lobster tail was awesome! I can't wait to come back and try more.

state: This review mainly focuses on the “biscuit cup”. It’s extremely expensive. I understand, but it’s quite small, especially compared to the other photos shown on Yelp. Moreover, it’s just one side of the macaron biscuit, so it should be less expensive. I could have bought a larger portion at Cold Stone, and I would have been much happier. The “marshmallow” (or “caramel custard”) is too salty. I don’t even think there was any sweetness; just salt. So we simply returned it. Therefore, if you don’t like salty sweets like me, don’t buy it. The person who worked there was kind and helpful, and the ice cream was pretty good, but the “marshmallow” basically ruined my experience. Another thing: why does a 16-ounce coffee cost $3.25? That’s more than what Starbucks charges, and this isn’t a specialty coffee place, so it shouldn’t be so expensive.

state: Absolutely incredible ice cream. A pleasant place to sit outside, at the picnic tables, during our wonderful spring weather. The staff were friendly and willing to let us try any flavor before buying it. We tried the lemon ice cream—it was creamy with the perfect balance between sour and sweet. There was also pistachio ice cream, which had plenty of chopped pistachios. The lily of the valley ice cream was incredibly fresh and not too sweet. The chocolate and banana ice cream had delicious crumbly pieces of chocolate, with the perfect balance between banana and chocolate in a creamy base. And there was “Black Forest” ice cream—it had a strong chocolate flavor, pieces of cherry, and crumbly chocolate pieces. We will definitely come back. Go in groups so you have a reason to try all the ice creams.

state:
Some interesting facts:  
1. I only stayed in the city for about 5 full days.  
2. I’m lactose intolerant (but I take Digestive Advantage – lactose intolerance tablets – which helped me enjoy places like this!!).  
3. I’ve been here three times, and each time I bought one or two ice creams. The creativity and variety of flavors made us want to come back again. It’s more than just an ordinary ice cream: there are simple ice creams with sugar, ice creams with waffle, ice creams with waffle in cups, chocolate coatings, ice creams with chocolate coatings… Even some were covered with sprinkles. Anything with fudge, caramel, coffee, or espresso as part of the ice cream – try it! “Decadent” is a very gentle description. It’s a very popular place where people line up to see what flavors are available. Just be careful not to step on anyone, especially small children who might run around… or even small adults. Move slowly and carefully – no one wants to get hurt :) The staff is friendly and quick in serving. There’s a seating area with small tables. There are bathrooms that are locked with keys. Ask for the keys that come with the spoon. This will be one of the reasons I recommend visiting Madison, Wisconsin :) Great service, excellent location for walking, and EXCELLENT ICECREAMS. I still think about those ice creams with waffle coatings…
