state: We’ve been there a few times, and there are some positive and negative aspects about this bakery. Positive points: Excellent location, with a wide variety of bakery products—especially cheesecakes and other Italian-style baked goods, which are hard to find elsewhere. The service is very fast and friendly. Their hours are longer than those of nearby bakeries, making it great for grabbing a snack or coffee to take home after dinner. Negative points: There really isn’t any place inside or outside where you can sit down and enjoy your food. Since the business seems to target couples and families who walk by in the area, it’s odd that there aren’t any benches or picnic tables for sitting and eating. The quality of some products isn’t as consistent as Sunflour, which is just a few blocks away. For example, the filling in some items looks almost like pudding, and the cinnamon rolls are exposed to air, making them seem dry. Another issue is the price. I’m sure that as they become more established in the area, this will improve over time, but for now, they’re significantly more expensive than nearby bakeries (again, Sunflour and Nova’s). Paying $4 for a muffin or chocolate biscuit seems expensive (although the bakery products aren’t that costly :-). I hope to visit again occasionally to see what’s new, but probably I’ll wait before making it the favorite bakery in the neighborhood.

state: Love it! OMG! This little Italian dessert shop inside of Eataly is phenomenal! You're going to have some decisions to make when you get here! Everything looks delicious (and probably is!)! We liked it so much, we went twice in one day! My favorite out of everything was the tiramisu pudding/dessert. It's the best! It had small pieces of tiramisu cake mixed in the pudding. The taste wasn't too sweet or bitter, it was just right. All of the desserts are authentic. Eating dessert here took me back to the days when I visited Rome and other Italian cities some years back. They also have a small coffee shop. I ordered a tiramisu iced coffee. It was good too but not as good as the dessert. It had a little bit of booze in it. Imagine...coffee and booze together at around 9 am? Lol. I also ordered a slice of chocolate cake with hazelnut mixed in. It was tasty as well but a bit dry. I took a couple of bites from my bf's desserts. Very good as well. We don't recall the names of them. Sorry! He ordered a hot chocolate in the morning and it was delicious! The taste wasn't too rich or sweet. Definitely stop here if you're in the area and into sweets. It's really close to New York New York and the MGM Grand. It took us about eight minutes to walk here from MGM. Aside from this shop, there's a variety of Italian foods and products to choose from in the other shops. There's also a casino in the back. I say any dessert you choose from here will probably be delicious. It's the tiramisu that does it for me! By the way, they change up some of the desserts they have in the morning during the afternoon. The service here is impeccable. I would give this spot more than five stars if I could. Totally recommend! :)

state: Okay so I'm not one to normally post reviews but OH MAN THIS PLACE!!!!! I've had their ice cream twice. The first time my roommate brought me home just a cup of strawberry ice cream. It was probably the best strawberry ice cream I've had! The second time, I went to the ice cream shop. It is in a cute little hidden village of shops. When we first walked in we were greeted immediately by the nice owners! They let us try all the flavors we wanted. I tried the Fat Elvis (peanut butter ice cream w/ caramelized bananas and bacon). It was delicious. I also had to try the honey lavender because I have heard great things and it was so light and yummy. But I was there for one thing. The donut melt!!!! Donuts + ice cream?! What could be better?? I got the Cookie Monster (blue cookies and cream flavor with chocolate chip cookies, Oreos and vanilla wafers). They warm up the donut sandwiches and they are so perfect. And you get one free topping! My boyfriend got the Leslie Knope which is a European waffle ice cream sandwich. He chose the Fat Elvis flavor. It was also delicious! I would much rather support a local small shop and this is just the place I will be picking. If you haven't already, GO TRY IT!!! You won't be disappointed!

My husband ordered the banana ice cream, and he loved it—it also had chunks! They serve the ice cream in boxes or Chinese food cones. Did I mention they are open until midnight? IMPRESSIVE! We will definitely come back.

Often, I buy things that are outside my usual comfort zone, and everything I tried was amazing. I can’t say enough about them. (Also, come back to Concord! haha)

state: Fatty Daddy’s is a small shop located in a quiet square. I’m from Philadelphia, and it would be great if it were in the city—with endless queues! The ice cream flavors are really fun, and they’re all delicious. The staff is very friendly and helpful, explaining the flavors to us and offering samples for my friends and me. I bought an ice cream from Fatty Daddy’s, and it was incredible! An Lucky Charms ice cream, a Fruity Pebbles macaron, and a perfectly toasted malvavisco. Get a 10% discount on Yelp! It’s absolutely worth it—original concept, great customer service, and delicious desserts.

state: When I was a child, I used to come here frequently. But about 50 years have passed, and it’s still here. Every time we visit the city and pass by here, there’s always a long line. Even on a regular working day, it wasn’t too bad, so we decided to stop. I ordered a dessert that resembled a snowstorm—its ice cream is real, not just artificial stuff. My husband ordered a smoothie, and it was so thick; it was delicious! Applause for keeping a successful business going for so long!

state: Did you know that Ghirardelli chocolate is just as delicious when melted on ice cream or at the base of a sundae, as it is in a decadent chocolate bar? If you’ve never experienced how wonderful hot Ghirardelli chocolate is, you definitely should try it. I always take my kids to any Ghirardelli ice cream shop. The ice cream is creamy and delicious, and it simply complements any topping you choose. The service is professional, and the portions are proportional to the price. I’m always willing to increase my calorie intake because of Ghirardelli!

I ate mine with a chocolate almond ice cream ball and an peanut butter ice cream ball, along with a coconut macaron and a toasted marshmallow on top. They use a kitchen stirrer to toast the marshmallow, and it was really delicious – it looked like a marshmallow roasted over a fire. I’ve found a new favorite dessert! :)

state: My first experience here was incredible. A few months ago, I tried a delicious carrot cake shaped like a whoopie pie. But when I returned recently, I found out that it wasn’t available anymore. And there was no alternative! At 8:30 in the morning, this branch didn’t have Better Nutters, TKOs, or Oh-Ohs. So, I ordered a oat and nut cookie, a pistachio macaron, and a salty caramel macaron. The oat and nut cookie was really dry. Usually, Bouchon is worth the calories, but not this cookie. The pistachio macaron was also quite boring, although it was better than the cookie. The salty caramel macaron, as always, was delicious. But I’m not sure if I’ll go back to this place just for that macaron.

On Monday night, there were about 10 people in line when we arrived. When we finally got to sit down with our usual portions (2 and a half scoops each), I chose butter cake with dark chocolate, and my friend chose a cake with peach jam and chocolate. Both were served beautifully in a waffle dish, which was prepared using an old waffle machine right in front of us. The prices are very reasonable—$6 for 2 and a half scoops and a waffle dish. I can’t wait to go back and try the ice cream tasting again.

state: Delicious ice cream with a wide variety of flavors that change constantly. Mason’s Creamery is well-known locally for its unique flavors, and in my opinion, it meets expectations quite well. I’ve tried the mango and taro flavors (I have a moderate preference for taro—the mango flavor started to taste a bit mushy after a few scoops). I also saw flavors like guava and sweet corn, among others. The mango and taro flavors were strong, but not so intense that they overpowered the overall taste; the ice cream had a satisfying consistency. The place itself is more like a kiosk. The building has a small interior area that includes a kitchen and space for waiting, but there are no immediate seating options. When leaving, there are indoor seating areas in a tent nearby with tables and chairs, along with some outdoor benches.

state: As a big fan of Christina Tosi, I was very excited to try the Milk Bar. Unfortunately, I was quite disappointed. I bought a slice of birthday cake, birthday cake truffles, a corn biscuit, and a slice of “crack pie” (a type of cake). The birthday cake was the one I didn’t like the most. The topping had a strange taste, similar to lemon. The birthday cake truffles had a sandy texture; they seemed similar to Starbucks’ birthday cake cupcakes, but with chocolate replaced by sand. The corn biscuit was extremely salty. It seemed like someone replaced sugar with salt. And the “crack pie” was okay—it was very sweet and hard to eat more than one bite. It had the flavor of a walnut cake, but without the walnuts. Considering all the expectations and the price, I expected something better.

state: I came here for a baby tea party organized by a colleague, and I was very impressed with the space, the food, and the staff. If you’ve never seen anything beyond the candy display window in front of this location, you’re missing out on an amazing experience. The space is really large—it’s hard to believe. There are so many small decorative items to enjoy that you’ll never get bored. I also didn’t know that the place could be rented out. Someone told me it could accommodate a wedding party of 80 people! We rented just a few rooms at the back for about 20 people, and the space was more than enough. Amelie’s offered us a Lorraine quiche, which was delicious, along with spinach quiche, their famous desserts, coffee, and orange juice. I was so impressed with the food that I brought some home for my husband; he tried almost everything, as he couldn’t decide what to eat.

state: Just a few blocks from the center, this donut shop offered an interesting selection of varieties. I tried the “Big Papa,” “grilled cheese,” “crème brûlée,” and Nutella donuts. The “Big Papa” was large and sweet—it even had a normal-sized “pop tart” inside! I recommend it because it’s easy to take photos and it offers a great experience. I think the “grilled cheese” was good as a combination of salty and sweet flavors. It was two warm sugar-filled donuts with cheese between them; they were big enough for me and my two friends to share easily. We ordered the “crème brûlée” because the staff said it was one of the best-selling items. I found it decent, but not particularly impressive. There was a crispy layer of caramel on top and cream inside. It might be a matter of personal taste, but I would prefer the “Boston crème” due to the chocolate and cream combination. Finally, the Nutella donut didn’t have a very pronounced Nutella flavor. It’s hard to convey the Nutella taste without actually using it. The coffee is okay, but I would prefer coffee from a café. However, it was pleasant to enjoy it with the donuts. They have a terrace area where you can eat in the back, and a fun aquarium inside. The atmosphere is more about enjoying it quickly rather than staying and relaxing. It was a nice quick stop in the morning.

state: These are donuts for people who think they don't like donuts. Why? Because once you've tried one you'll say, "Wow--this must be what donuts are supposed to taste like." Or maybe even a "Oh, so this is why everyone goes nuts over these things." Don't get me wrong, I'll alway be a bagel gal, but these donuts are the top of the line. I had one--just one!--and it shook my world. And get this... It was only a glazed one. I know. That little 'ole glazed donut was airy, light, not too sweet, perfection in my mouth. It's mind-boggling that I didn't even eat it hot and it was still that good. Anyways, I'm going back and I'm not even waiting for a cheat day. It's worth the extra day of exercise, trust me--and these 5-stars.

state: Sprinkles is always a great choice! I’ve already tried their cupcakes before, but this was the first time I tried their ice cream sandwich at the Strip location in Las Vegas. The store is located right in the center of the Strip, so it’s a convenient place for a snack. Additionally, it’s close to a fountain and a giant carousel, allowing you to eat outdoors and enjoy the view and atmosphere. They offer a wide range of desserts: ice cream, ice cream sandwich, biscuit sandwich, etc. I wanted to try the ice cream sandwich, so naturally, I ordered the “red velvet” sandwich with red velvet ice cream. Delicious! Definitely worth trying if you’re in the area!

state: In terms of price, selection, portion and taste -- Milk Bar is a flat 2.5 out of 5. The concept has so much potential, but the execution falls short. My boyfriend and I came by last night for a pre-Marquee treat. We noticed the "Fancy Shakes" -- classic milkshakes with alcohol included -- and decided to try a couple. He went with the Cereal Milk White Russian, and I went with the Chocolate Malt. Both were $12 each, both had vodka and kahlua. Maybe we should've gone with something else, but these were pretty lackluster. They were extremely sweet, even for milkshakes, and the alcohol didn't seem to complement the taste at all. Hard to finish, and they were tiny to begin with! Rounding up because they have a delicious variety of cookies and other drinks. Plus, they're open late. Wish they had more than 4 flavors of shakes, though. We will not be back.

state: I love the ice cream with the “s’more” topping. I don’t like the ice cream sandwich with chocolate. The first piece was delicious, but both cookies had too much salt, which I couldn’t tolerate. Then, the salt spread throughout my ice cream, making it so salty that I couldn’t eat it. It was a sad moment, as the ice cream is really delicious. I also really appreciate the customer service; the staff are very friendly. I’ll go back to try the ice cream in pretzel cone shape. My favorite ice creams are mint and Vietnamese coffee flavor.

state: The “Pacific Sunset Ice Cream” and cookie-cream ice cream are the best ones you can find in the city. My boyfriend and I love going there to buy ice creams to take home, along with our dessert for that night. You’re the best, and the owner is very kind! There’s just one thing… the number of times we feel like having an ice cream or several scoops after 8 p.m. is incredible. We hope you can find a way to stay open later; we know that many people in Arizona don’t go out until sunset. For summer, maybe you should consider this place, since the sun sets at 8 p.m. We can’t wait to enjoy your delicious food again!

I wish there wasn’t that granule in it, but the topping and flavor are really excellent. My suggestion is to try the “sampler” of 4 flavors. state: Stopped in this Sunday morning to pick up breakfast to go. Despite what other reviews suggest, the line was quite short and my food was served promptly. The pastry options were beautiful and extensive, but I chose to go with a croissant egg and cheese breakfast sandwich and a cappuccino. Let me tell you. I think I made the right choice. The sandwich was buttery, flaky, and hearty without being greasy, which is truly an art. A simple delight. And the cappuccino was fabulous, and topped with cinnamon and cocoa. Next time, I'll definitely have the cappuccino at the restaurant, as I think it would have been even better piping hot. It's Little Italy in Cleveland, so parking is a challenge, but Presti's is well worth a few drives around the block.

state: If you enjoy the “milk and cereal” dessert at Afters in California, you’ll also love this place. They have their own version with corn cookies on milk ice cream, and it’s a truly delicious treat when you’re in Las Vegas. What I liked was that the ice cream wasn’t too sweet, and the salty taste of the corn cookies combined very well. I tried all their cookies (except the confetti one), and my final conclusion is that the “BLUEBERRY AND CREME” cookie is the best. The others tasted exactly like regular chocolate cookies. The “BLUEBERRY AND CREME” cookie stood out especially. Moreover, it has a perfect balance of sweetness. In fact, it tastes just like a strawberry milk ice cream. If I ever visit Milk in Las Vegas again, it’s probably because of the cookies.

state: We decided to try the cupcake machine during a trip to Las Vegas in December. You can enter the store and order your treat, but what’s the fun in that? It’s something you should experience at least once. You make the order, pay, and then watch the robotic arms pick up the dessert from a computer screen. The machine emphasizes that no charges are applied until the dessert is in your hand. They come packaged individually in small boxes with the “sprinkles” logo. My wife ordered a peanut butter cookie, and I asked for a cupcake with spiced butter frosting. Both were of decent size, and the price was reasonable. I hope to see more of these places in California. If they exist there, they would be a success. There are also tables and chairs right outside, which was very convenient.

state: Five words: Meringue ice cream on a stick!!! Seriously, the best thing in Las Vegas, especially on a hot summer day. But you need to go early, because they run out quickly. So, along with that delicious stick, we also bought some regular donuts. But of course, these aren’t “regular” donuts! We ordered “Oh My Birthday Cake Oreo”, raspberry cheesecake, raspberry cheesecake with Meyer lemon, roasted coconut, birthday cake, and Twix chocolate. My favorite (besides the meringue ice cream on a stick with vanilla ice cream and chocolate sauce) was the coconut and raspberry cheesecake. All were great, but really, I couldn’t stop thinking about that meringue stick! WITH ICE CREAM! MY FAVORITE! I love vanilla ice cream! And putting it on a meringue stick is simply amazing! We came back a few days later, but it was too late! I almost cried when I saw that they were gone! This is a MUST-visit place if you’re visiting Las Vegas or living there. But go early, because they run out quickly, and you might have bad luck during lunch! Definitely worth waking up early and getting those donuts and ice cream!

state:
My friend highly recommended La Pasticceria due to its desserts. So I decided to visit this place to try them out. Wow! I forgot how pleasant it is to watch the desserts while waiting in line. I really wanted to buy them all, but my wallet wouldn’t allow it. For my first purchase, I decided to try the peach croissant and the Nutella croissant. And I wasn’t disappointed! They were delicious, and I went back the next day to buy some more before heading home. My roommate happily accepted the “unusual souvenir” from Las Vegas: FOODS:  
* Peach croissant – light in texture, with a fruit flavor. I wish the peach jam was spread evenly across the croissant.  
* Nutella croissant – there’s no mistake with Nutella, but… (read next line)  
* Chocolate croissant – if I had to choose between the Nutella croissant and the chocolate one, I would pick the chocolate one. I don’t know why, but I like it better.  
* Cream-filled croissant – recommended by someone who was in line in front of me. Delicious!  
ATMOSFER: It was quiet during the morning, between 8 a.m. and 9 a.m., when I visited. I went back to another restaurant for dinner, and it was very busy and noisy there. The staff were very friendly and helpful. They were very patient. Bonus: The paper bag is really cute. It’s a bit expensive, but there’s no problem in treating yourself when you’re in Las Vegas, right? The best way is to share it with family/friends so you can try a little of everything. Also, the morning should be less chaotic!

state: Mason’s Cremery is a small, charming store located on the edge of Ohio City. The service was excellent. As a first-time visitor, the kind staff encouraged me to try all the ice cream flavors and provided information about the place—which was very interesting. The ice cream was just good; nothing exceptional. I would probably choose frozen yogurt instead of a portion. The texture was okay, but after the first bite, the flavor wasn’t as appealing. I tried triple chocolate ice cream, marshmallow ice cream, and Krispies rice ice cream—none were as impressive as I expected. However, I might come back. They often change their flavors, and it seems they have a unique touch. It’s hard for a local ice cream shop to stand out in a city with a network like Mitchell’s, but I would still choose Mason’s.

state: The craving for something sweet came back again, so we headed to “Batch Bakehouse” – a place with a discreet appearance (almost imperceptible), but don’t be fooled, because the products they offer are truly exceptional! After fighting against my own impulses to take everything, we decided to settle for some apple tarts, a butter cake with strawberries and cream, and a “Black Bottom” cupcake. The individual apple tarts are perfect if you don’t want to go through the trouble of making a large portion. The dough was deliciously buttery, and the base stayed firm. The filling consisted of apple pieces instead of slices, which works well for a “mini” tart like this. The flavors and levels of sweetness were perfect. The butter cake seemed more elegant than a muffin: soft, with melted cream cheese in the mouth, and a slightly sour-tart flavor from the fruit that stimulates the palate from time to time… Great! Finally, the “Black Bottom” cupcake – if you look closely, it’s actually a version of a lava cake. And who wouldn’t enjoy it? I appreciated that the chocolate, although dark, wasn’t too bitter, and that the outer crust wasn’t too dry. No wonder this place is so popular and a must-visit.

state: Two words: Cookie cup!!! The cookie cup consists of two macaron cookies, with two ice cream balls on top, and finished with a baked marshmallow. You can choose two different flavors of ice cream for the two balls. If you feel adventurous, you can add a first topping for $0.75, and each additional topping for $0.50. The toppings include oats cookies, Oreo, colorful granola, and chocolate granola, to name a few. The staff were friendly and helpful. As someone who’s very indecisive, I didn’t feel pressured to choose a flavor right away. They were really willing to let me try all 24 ice cream flavors, since there was no line behind me. I tried just two flavors, and I fell in love with Mocha Java Yaya and Mint Ice Cream. I laughed a lot at the names of the flavors, like “Netflix & Chill”. I would definitely try some flavors while having fun. The best part was watching the marshmallow bake right in front of us. If you’re looking for something lighter, they also have ice cream balls available. This place didn’t get five stars from me because of the price and too much sugar. The first bites of the cookie cup were amazing. However, the subsequent bites were overly sweet. Also, the price is a bit high—$7.50 for the cup. I’ve already eaten macaron sandwiches with ice cream in great flavors for just $4.50. Overall, this place is great for kids. There’s a free water station near the napkins. If you plan to eat your dessert there, there are some tables inside and some outside. Don’t forget to check Yelp to get a 10% discount on your purchase. They also have a loyalty card: buy 9 ice cream balls and get the 10th for free.

Other yummy options are their berry salad, liver pate on a baguette sandwich, and their BLT croissant. Highly suggest! Oh and they're apparently open 24/7!

state: This place is hard to find. Anyway, I really wanted to try some macaroni. My companion is a huge fan of desserts, so he encouraged me when I mentioned this place. But we were disappointed. He ordered a chocolate cake, and I ordered three pieces of macaroni. Visually, the macaroni looked appealing, and the size was generous compared to other options in the area. The taste was too sweet—macaroni with lemon shouldn’t be sweet at all. The chocolate cake was just like eating a bar of chocolate. And the prices were outrageous: 2 drinks with coffee + 1 dessert + 3 pieces of macaroni, for a total of $26! I think there are better options in the area, so maybe look elsewhere.

state: I was very excited to see Carlo’s Bakery in the Venetian stores. I had visited the original location in Hoboken, and I was really impressed by the desserts and the staff. This new location had a similar style. Social distancing was being enforced, with only a few customers entering the bakery at a time. I walked around the displays and checked out the products. A staff member came up to me to take my order. I ordered two cupcakes (both with white cake – one with chocolate icing, the other with vanilla icing), two chocolate chip cookies, and two brownies. The staff member didn’t talk much to me, and didn’t seem very friendly. Even though I arrived during a quiet time, it could have been a busy day. After placing my order, they told me to wait until they called me to pick it up and pay. I waited about 5 minutes before they called me. Everything was well packaged so that I could survive the 5-minute journey to my room at The Palazzo. My total cost was a little less than $30, which seems a bit expensive for 6 items. When I got back to my room, I couldn’t wait to try one of the cupcakes. It was delicious! The cake was moist, and the icing was perfect. Exactly as I remembered from my visit to Carlo’s Bake Shop in Hoboken. After eating the cupcake, I couldn’t resist and also ate one of the chocolate chip cookies. They were very soft and had a strong chocolate flavor. These cookies were just as good as those I brought back from Carlo’s Bake Shop for my family to try. Very tasty! The only thing I didn’t like was the brownie. It had a strange taste. Usually, I love chocolate brownies, but I couldn’t finish this one. It had that dusty chocolate taste. The icing on top was okay. Overall, I really like this bakery. The cupcakes and cookies are definitely my favorites, both at this store in Las Vegas and in Hoboken. I definitely recommend it!

state: Well – they don’t save on ingredients like DQ has been doing lately. I came by here when I got lost at the entrance to Whole Foods’ parking lot, and I decided I needed to enter to try the “handmade” cream ice cream. Especially after reading so many good reviews from other customers. Usually, I don’t get a milkshake when I buy ice cream, because they’re so quick and easy to drink that they don’t last long enough for me. But I decided to try it here, because the photos I saw showed that it was delicious. I chose Oreo as the topping and chocolate ice cream. I saw the staff put a big amount of ice cream into the machine, along with lots of Oreo cookies and some milk, and it seemed like I could eat it for days. But after everything was mixed together, it was poured into a cup that holds 12 or 16 ounces, with an inch on top so they could add more Oreo pieces. So there wasn’t much shake left. It would be great if they had given me a version with toppings, like those in metal containers in restaurants, instead of just discarding the delicious leftover. And I never thought I’d say this, but it was just too much Oreo for me. I also think I missed out on the delicious experience of high-fat ice cream, which everyone talks about, when mixed into a milkshake. Next time, and definitely there will be a next time, I’ll order ice cream, maybe mixed with Reese’s.

state: Four words: Vegan Chocolate Ice Cream. Really, it’s one of the best secrets in Cleveland. You don’t need to be a vegan to enjoy it (and I know that). I’ve also recommended this ice cream to my friends and family, and they usually include it in their ice creams too. Usually, there are two vegan flavors available, and honestly, they’re the best dairy-free ice creams I’ve tried. In fact, they’re better than most “regular” ice creams, and they’re super creamy. Definitely trust me and try a spoonful next time you’re around here—even my coworkers, who aren’t usually fans, enjoy it. Okay, enough. Besides the amazing ice cream, another advantage of Mitchell’s is that it’s a great example of a charming local business. I love the interior decoration. It’s located in an old theater, and when you look up, you can see the old wooden beams intersecting with a big glass wall, from which you can see the workers preparing different batches of ice cream. I’ve seen them wash and prepare fresh strawberries, which is very refreshing in a world full of artificial flavors. If you order the vegan chocolate ice cream, I recommend also getting an ice cream with it, because it melts quickly and the portions are quite large. So, I usually take it home and store it in the freezer. If you’re in the market or eating in Ohio City, definitely give it a try for a delicious dessert!

state: One night, after a rich dinner, my friends and I went to this place and tried it out. The hardest part is finding a parking spot, as the city center can be quite tricky to navigate. Melt was quite small and, overall, very clean. Unfortunately, there were no public bathrooms for me. And I was ready! The dairy products also helped… apart from the jokes! We ordered a portion of cucumber salad, which was really refreshing, and even the neighborhood cat noticed it. We also ordered a portion of “Cookie Monster,” which my friends thought was the perfect amount of sweetness and texture of cookies. And the blue color was amazing. Overall, it’s a small but fantastic place, and we highly recommend visiting it today. Even the cat recommends it—it’s hungry!

state: A frozen dessert that few can match. Recently, I’ve been enjoying “ice cream sandwiches” very much. So when I went to Scottsdale for the weekend, I had to try this place out. The refrigerators were full of unique flavors. Since I really prefer mint or chocolate flavors, I chose those. I ordered a mint ice cream with chunks and a double chocolate ice cream. Both were placed comfortably between a oat milk biscuit with raisins on one side, and a macadamia nut biscuit with white chocolate on the other. Although the biscuits were larger than usual, they weren’t my first choice, but they were the only ones available. I ended up at the end of the night, so I can’t blame them for not having many options. The ice cream was delicious, creamy, and gave me a cool treat. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for tasty ice cream and biscuits in a package.
